body.translated_text: // <s>Āyurvedamahodadhi</s> (The Great Ocean of Āyurveda) //
<s>Annapānavidhi</s> (Regulations on Food and Drink)

body.text: ... ṇī mūtramalādikānāṃ jātā janitrīva harītakī nṛṇām // 5 //
body.translated_text: ... <s>Harītakī</s> (Terminalia chebula) has become like a mother for the elimination of urine, feces, and other waste products. // 5 //

children.text: grīṣme tulyaguḍāṃ sasaindhavayutāṃ meghāc ca varṣāgame
children.translated_text: In summer, one should take [<s>harītakī</s>] with equal [quantity of] <s>guḍa</s> (jaggery) mixed with <s>saindhava</s> (rock salt); at the onset of the rainy season,
with equal [quantity of] <s>śarkarā</s> (sugar) in autumn; with <s>śuṇṭhī</s> (dry ginger) [which is] free from impurity at the onset of winter;
with <s>pippalī</s> (long pepper) in the cold season; in the spring season combined with <s>kṣaudra</s> (honey),

children.text: rājan bhakṣa (bhuṅkṣva) harītakīm iva rujo naśyantu te śatravaḥ // 6 //
children.translated_text: O King, consume <s>harītakī</s> — may your enemies perish just as diseases [perish]. // 6 //
Those who avoid exercise in spring, who are fond of sexual intercourse in summer,

children.text: saktāḥ prāvṛṣi palvalāmbhasi nave kūpodake dveṣiṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: who are attached to stagnant pond water during the rains, and who are hostile to fresh well water;
who are fond of pungent, sour, and salty [foods] in autumn, who eat <s>dadhi</s> (yogurt) [in autumn], who are lazy with sleep in winter,

children.text: śītāmbhaḥparigāhinas tu śiśire naśyantu te śatravaḥ // 7 //
children.translated_text: and who bathe in cold water in the cold season — may those enemies perish! // 7 //

body.translated_text: Now, the section on drinking water (<s>pānīyavarga</s>).

children.translated_text: Sweet, cool in its post-digestive effect (<s>pākarasa</s>), cold, and pacifying all three <s>doṣas</s> (humors),
purifying, supremely wholesome, and delightful is the water of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>. // 8 //

children.text: proktaṃ svādu svaccham atyantarucyaṃ pathyaṃ pākyaṃ pācanaṃ pāpahāri /
children.translated_text: It is declared to be sweet, clear, exceedingly appetizing, wholesome, digestible, promoting digestion, and removing sin;

children.text: tṛṣṇāmohadhvaṃsanaṃ cātimedhyaṃ prajñāṃ dhatte vāri bhāgīrathīyam // 9 //
children.translated_text: destroying thirst and delusion, and supremely promoting intellect — the water of <s>Bhāgīrathī</s> (the <s>Gaṅgā</s>) bestows wisdom. // 9 //

body.translated_text: Thus [the properties] of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>.

children.text: tasmāt kiṃcid gurutaraṃ svādu pittāpahaṃ param /
children.translated_text: Somewhat heavier than that, sweet, supremely removing <s>pitta</s> (bile),
aggravating <s>vāta</s> (wind), stimulating the digestive fire (<s>vahni</s>), and dry — such is the water of the <s>Yamunā</s>. // 10 //

body.translated_text: Thus [the properties] of the <s>Yamunā</s>.

children.text: atisvacchaṃ praśastaṃ ca śītalaṃ laghu lekhanam /
children.translated_text: Exceedingly clear, excellent, cool, light, and scraping (<s>lekhana</s>),
pacifying <s>pitta</s> and <s>śleṣma</s> (phlegm) — the water of the <s>Narmadā</s> conquers all diseases. // 11 //

body.translated_text: Thus [the properties] of the <s>Narmadā</s>.

children.translated_text: Pacifying itching and skin diseases (<s>kuṣṭha</s>), supremely kindling the digestive fire,
promoting digestion, and destroying <s>vāta</s> and <s>pitta</s> — such is the water born of the <s>Godāvarī</s>. // 12 //
Removing the affliction of <s>pitta</s> and blood disorders, eliminating the faults of <s>kuṣṭha</s> and other dreadful diseases,
supremely wholesome, kindling digestion and removing sin — the water of <s>Godāvarī</s> wards off thirst. // 13 //

body.translated_text: Thus [the properties] of the <s>Godāvarī</s>.

children.translated_text: Dry and cool is the water, aggravating <s>vātarakta</s> (gout),
somewhat lighter and sweet — born from the <s>Kṛṣṇaveṇyā</s> (Kṛṣṇā river). // 14 //

body.translated_text: Thus [the properties] of the <s>Kṛṣṇaveṇyā</s>.

children.translated_text: The water of the <s>Kāverī</s> is wholesome, destroying diseases (<s>āma</s>), bestowing strength and complexion,
fiery [in potency] yet very cool, and removes skin diseases (<s>dadru</s>) and <s>kuṣṭha</s> and poison. // 15 //

body.translated_text: Thus [the properties] of the <s>Kāverī</s>.

children.text: tridoṣaśamanaṃ pathyaṃ svādu hṛdyaṃ ca jīvanam /
children.translated_text: Pacifying all three <s>doṣas</s>, wholesome, sweet, pleasing to the heart, and life-giving,

children.text: bhramaghnaṃ ca pipāsāghnaṃ divyaṃ vāri manoharam // 16 //
children.translated_text: destroying dizziness (<s>bhrama</s>) and thirst — divine water is delightful. // 16 //

body.translated_text: Thus [the properties of] untimely rain water (<s>akālajala</s>).

children.translated_text: Rivers born in the central and intermediate directions are light and remove the three <s>doṣas</s>;
those of the southern direction are great rivers that destroy <s>pitta</s> and <s>śleṣma</s> (phlegm);
those born in the northern direction are wholesome, light, and remove the three <s>doṣas</s>;
rivers originating in the eastern region immediately remove <s>vāta</s> and <s>kapha</s>;
those of the west release <s>pitta</s> and destroy <s>kapha</s> and <s>vāta</s>. // 17 //

children.text: iti saṃkṣepataḥ proktā nadyaḥ sūkṣmāś ca saṃprati /
children.translated_text: Thus rivers have been described in brief; now the subtle [distinctions]. Sea water is foul-smelling, alkaline, and aggravates all <s>doṣas</s>. // 18 //
It is harmful to the eyes and destroys intoxication, splenic enlargement (<s>plīha</s>), abdominal tumors (<s>gulma</s>), and tympanitis (<s>āvartana</s>).

body.translated_text: Now, the characteristics of the eight types of water.
I shall now describe the qualities and defects of divine and other [waters] with discernment. // 19 //
Divine (<s>divya</s>), atmospheric (<s>āntarikṣa</s>), riverine (<s>nādeya</s>), from wells (<s>kaupa</s>), from springs (<s>caudeya</s>), marshy (<s>sārasa</s>),

children.translated_text: from tanks (<s>tāḍāga</s>), and from underground springs (<s>audbhida</s>), and mountain [water] (<s>śaila</s>) — water is remembered as being of eight types. // 20 //

children.text: tāḍāgam audbhidaṃ śailaṃ jalam aṣṭavidhaṃ smṛtam // 20 //
children.translated_text: Resembling the great lightning released from autumn clouds,
removing all <s>doṣas</s> and sweet — this is called divine (<s>divya</s>) water. // 21 //

children.text: sarvadoṣāpahaṃ svādu divyam ity ucyate jalam // 21 //
children.translated_text: Released from rain clouds, having an indistinct sweet taste,
water resembling crystal — this is known as atmospheric (<s>āntarikṣa</s>). // 22 //
From a river born of mountains, having the luster of <s>gomedaka</s> (hessonite) gems,
situated in an excellent tract of land — such water is called riverine (<s>nādeya</s>). // 23 //
Arising from excavated ground, originating from great rocky formations,
clear, sweet, and pleasant — this is called well water (<s>kaupa</s>). // 24 //

children.text: vimalaṃ madhuraṃ svādu kaupaṃ jalam udāhṛtam // 24 //
children.translated_text: Naturally [flowing] through long rock crevices, having the appearance of blue lotus petals,
covered by spreading creepers — this is designated as spring water (<s>caudeya</s>). // 25 //
Water born in marshy regions, [known as] <s>sārasa</s>, is heavy and slimy,
sweet and producing <s>śleṣma</s> (phlegm), and is known to aggravate <s>vāta</s> and other [<s>doṣas</s>]. // 26 //
Whether from a river, a rocky descent, or a reservoir, situated in a secluded place,
covered by spreading creepers — this is designated as tank water (<s>tāḍāga</s>). // 27 //
Situated in an excellent tract of land, stored for not more than one year,
astringent-sweet and pleasant — this is known as underground spring water (<s>audbhida</s>). // 28 //
Arising from mountain ridges, touched by wind, frost, and heat,
light, cool, pure, and sweet — this is known as trickling mountain water (<s>prasravaṇa</s>). // 29 //

children.text: laghu śītāmalaṃ svādu smṛtaṃ prasravaṇaṃ jalam // 29 //
children.translated_text: These [waters], when uncontaminated by buffalo, horse, elephant, deer, aquatic creatures, and other [animals],
should be collected in earthen vessels. // 30 //
All water born from the sky is to be judged by its sweetness;

children.text: sarvam ākāśajaṃ vāri svāduto hy anumīyate /
children.translated_text: terrestrial water, however, is recognized by experts in taste according to the nature of the terrain. // 31 //
Having red, grey, yellow hues, [or found] on white or dark [soils],
[water acquires] pungent, sour, bitter, alkaline, astringent, sweet, and other [tastes]. // 32 //
Now, the qualities of riverine and other [waters].

body.translated_text: Riverine water is <s>vāta</s>-aggravating, dry, kindling digestion, light, and scraping;

children.translated_text: tank water is <s>vāta</s>-aggravating, sweet, astringent, and causes itching upon digestion. // 33 //

children.text: tāḍāgaṃ vātalaṃ svādu kaṣāyaṃ kaṭupāki ca // 33 //
children.translated_text: Reservoir water removes <s>vāta</s> and <s>śleṣma</s>, is alkaline, causes itching, and aggravates <s>pitta</s>;
well-derived (<s>cauṇḍeya</s>) water kindles the fire, is dry, sweet, and also produces <s>kapha</s>. // 34 //

children.text: cauṇḍayam agnikaraṃ rūkṣaṃ madhuraṃ kaphakṛt tathā // 34 //
children.translated_text: Water from flowing springs (<s>prasravaṇa</s>) destroys <s>kapha</s>, kindles digestion, is pleasing to the heart, and light;
well water (<s>kaupa</s>) is alkaline, aggravates <s>pitta</s>, and destroys <s>śleṣma</s> and <s>vāta</s>. // 35 //

children.text: sakṣāraṃ pittalaṃ kaupaṃ śleṣmaghnaṃ vātajit tathā // 35 //
children.translated_text: Underground spring water (<s>audbhida</s>) is remembered as sweet, pacifying <s>pitta</s>, and not causing burning;
paddy-field water (<s>kedāra</s>) is sweet in digestion, heavy in post-digestive effect, and aggravates the <s>doṣas</s>. // 36 //

children.text: kedāraṃ madhuraṃ pāke gurudoṣavipākalam (proktaṃ vipāke guru doṣalam) // 36 //
children.translated_text: Similarly, stagnant pool water (<s>pālvala</s>) is condemned, and is particularly aggravating to the <s>doṣas</s>;

children.text: tadvat pālvalam uddiṣṭaṃ viśeṣād doṣalaṃ ca tat /
children.translated_text: water from arid regions (<s>jāṅgala</s>) removes all <s>doṣas</s>, is pleasing to the heart, and faultless. // 37 //
Well water also destroys thirst and fatigue and increases pleasure.

body.text:
kaupaṃ jalaṃ ca tṛṣṇāghnaṃ śramaghnaṃ prītivardhanam /
(ānūpaṃ śleṣmalaṃ proktaṃ medodoṣavivardhanam /)

children.text: dīpanaṃ svādu śītaṃ ca toyaṃ sādhāraṇaṃ laghu // 38 //
children.translated_text: Water from ordinary regions (<s>sādhāraṇa</s>) kindles digestion, is sweet, cool, and light. // 38 //

body.translated_text: (Water from marshy regions is declared to increase <s>śleṣma</s> and fat-related disorders.)
Thus [the properties of] water from arid, marshy, and ordinary regions.
Now, the regulation of water-drinking according to season.

children.text: kaupaṃ prasravaṇaṃ vasantasamaye grīṣme tad evocitaṃ
children.translated_text: In the spring season, well water or trickling spring water is suitable; in summer, the same is recommended;

children.text: kāle vā nabhavṛṣṭideśyam athavā kaupaṃ ghanānāṃ punaḥ /
children.translated_text: or at the time of rain, [water] from the region where clouds [deposit it], or again well water during the rains;
in the cold season, all water from lakes and tanks; at the arrival of autumn,
one should use water whose <s>doṣas</s> have been dispelled by the rays of the sun and moon and by the wind. // 39 //
Water that has an indistinct taste and smell, praised as removing [the effects of] wind and heat,

children.text: pavitram ambu tat pathyaṃ anyatra (kva) kathitaṃ pibet // 40 //
children.translated_text: purifying and wholesome — wherever described, one should drink such [water]. // 40 //

body.translated_text: Should one seek water from a lake that has been infused by the heat of the sun and moon over days and nights?
Now, the qualities of hot water (<s>uṣṇāmbu</s>).

body.text: tac cāvyaktarasaṃ himaṃ laghutaraṃ gharmāṃbu mūrchāpahaṃ

children.translated_text: it destroys [the effects of] summer heat, <s>śleṣma</s> diseases, and delusion; it removes fatigue and eliminates drowsiness and excessive sleep;
it is pleasing to the heart, sweet, bestows varied [benefits], promotes memory, and cuts through the mass of burning sensations;

children.text: itthaṃ deham alāyuṣor dhṛtikaraṃ saṃjīvanaṃ jīvanam // 41 //
children.translated_text: thus it gives firmness to the body of the living being, is restorative and life-sustaining. // 41 //

body.translated_text: That [hot water] has an indistinct taste, is cool [in post-digestive effect], lighter [than cold water], and removes fainting caused by heat;
Now, the characteristics of condemned water.

body.text:
viṇmūtratṛṇanīlikāviṣayutaṃ taptaṃ dhanaṃ phenilaṃ
dantagrāhyam anārtavaṃ salavaṇaṃ śaivālakaiḥ saṃbhṛtam /
body.translated_text: Water contaminated with excrement, urine, straw, and blue [algae], heated, thick, frothy, clinging to the teeth, not seasonal, salty, and mixed with moss;

body.text:
lūtājantuvimiśritaṃ gurutaraṃ parṇaughapaṅkāvilaṃ
candrārkāṃśusugopitaṃ ca na piben nīraṃ sadā doṣalam {cf. Rājanighaṇṭu 14.56} // 45 //
body.translated_text: mixed with spiders and insects, very heavy, turbid with masses of leaves and mud, and hidden from the rays of the sun and moon — one should never drink such water, for it always aggravates the <s>doṣas</s>. {cf. <s>Rājanighaṇṭu</s> 14.56} // 45 //
Now, the characteristics of recommended water.

children.text: prasannaṃ svādu hṛdyaṃ ca pathyaṃ saṃtarpaṇaṃ laghu /
children.translated_text: Clear, sweet, pleasing to the heart, wholesome, nourishing, and light;
water from a single source, always available in adequate quantity, should be used. // 43 //

body.translated_text: Now, the benefits of drinking water at the end of the night.

children.translated_text: Cough, dyspnea, excessive diarrhea, fever, itching, hiccup, strangury, diseases of the back, flanks, and spine,
urinary retention, abdominal diseases, hemorrhoids, edema, intestinal worms, and diseases of the ears, nose, and eyes —

children.text: ye cānye vātapittakṣayakaphajakṛtā vyādhayaḥ santi jantoḥ
children.translated_text: whatever other diseases arise from <s>vāta</s>, <s>pitta</s>, depletion, and <s>kapha</s> in living beings,

children.text: tāṃs tān abhyāsayogād apaharati payaḥpānam ante niśāyāḥ // 44 //
children.translated_text: all those are removed by the regular practice of drinking water at the end of the night. // 44 //

children.text: aṃbhasaś culakān aṣṭau pibed anudinaṃ naraḥ /
children.translated_text: A person should drink eight handfuls (<s>culaka</s>) of water daily;
becoming strong as a young elephant, the wise one shall live a hundred years. // 45 //

body.translated_text: Now, the benefits of water drunk through the nostrils (<s>ghrāṇapīta</s>).

children.translated_text: At the end of the night when the clouds have cleared, rising early every morning,

children.text: pibati khalu naro yo ghrāṇarandhreṇa vāri /
children.translated_text: the person who indeed drinks water through the nasal passages,
he becomes full of intelligence, equal to <s>Tārkṣya</s> (<s>Garuḍa</s>) in visual acuity,
free from wrinkles and grey hair, and liberated from all diseases. // 46 //

body.translated_text: Now, the method of using water for the protection of the eyes.

children.text: śītāmbupūritamukhaḥ prativāsaraṃ yaḥ kālatraye 'pi nayanadvitayaṃ jalena /
children.translated_text: He who fills his mouth with cold water every day and at all three times [of the day] sprinkles both eyes with water,

children.text: āsiñcati dhruvam asau na kadācid akṣirogavyathāvidhuratāṃ bhajate manuṣyaḥ // 47 //
children.translated_text: that person certainly never experiences the distress of eye diseases. // 47 //
Riverine water, placed in a new earthen pot, heated by the rays of the sun [during the day],
then cooled at night by moonbeams and gently stirred by a mild breeze, {cf. <s>Rājanighaṇṭu</s> 14.54ab}
cold, with the luster of a split gem, so light that it raises no doubt,
fragrant with <s>pāṭalī</s>, <s>utpala</s> (blue lotus), and <s>ketakī</s> flowers — one should regularly drink such water. // 48 //

body.text:
re re rudrajaṭāṭavīparisakhyālolabhasmāvilaṃ
pronmañjatsurasundarīkucataṭasphāracchalacchīkaram /
dhārādhautakarālitāṃbaratanuṃ (?) niḥśeṣapāpāpahaṃ
gāṅgaṃ tuṅgataraṅgabhaṅgagahanaṃ pānīyam ānīyatām // 49 // ? // 50 //
body.translated_text: O! Bring the water of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> — turbid with the ashes scattered by <s>Rudra's</s> vigorous <s>Tāṇḍava</s> dance, splashing with drops from the breasts of the beautiful celestial maidens rising [from the water], its body washed by streams and tinged with the hue of <s>alaktaka</s> (?), removing the sins of all remaining [beings], deep with the waves of <s>Tuṅga</s>, <s>Taraṅga</s>, and <s>Bhaṅga</s> — let such water be brought! // 49 // ? // 50 //
Now, the qualities of boiled and cooled water (<s>śṛtoṣṇajala</s>).

children.translated_text: Wholesome, kindling and promoting digestion, lighter [than unboiled water], removing dyspnea and cough,
pacifying hiccup, flatulence, fresh fever, and lethargy, removing <s>śleṣma</s> and conquering <s>vāta</s>,
purifying the abdomen and bladder and promoting intellect, removing pain in the heart and flanks,
declared beneficial in abdominal tumors (<s>gulma</s>), loss of appetite (<s>arocaka</s>), and nasal catarrh (<s>pīnasa</s>) — such is boiled and cooled water. // 51 //
In conditions dominated by <s>pitta</s>, in <s>pitta</s> diseases, in disorders of <s>pitta</s> with blood and <s>kapha</s>,
in fainting, vomiting, fever, burning sensation, summer heat, excessive diarrhea, and affliction; // 52 //

body.text:
dhātukṣīṇe viṣārte ca sannipāte viśeṣataḥ /
śastaṃ śoṣe 'kṣiroge ca śṛtaṃ śītaṃ jalaṃ sadā // 54 // (3 ?)
body.translated_text: in depletion of <s>dhātus</s> (bodily tissues), in poisoning, and especially in <s>sannipāta</s> (disorder of all three <s>doṣas</s>), it is praised in wasting diseases and eye disorders — one should always [use] boiled and cooled water. // 54 //
Now, the qualities of water according to the time of drinking.

children.text: chatrāmṛtaṃ viṣaṃ vajraṃ catvāro vāriṇo guṇāḥ /
children.translated_text: The four qualities of water are: umbrella-like (<s>chatra</s>), nectar-like (<s>amṛta</s>), poison-like (<s>viṣa</s>), and thunderbolt-like (<s>vajra</s>),

children.text: bhuktvā tadaiva pratyūṣe abhukte bhojanaiḥ saha // 55 //
children.translated_text: [corresponding to drinking] immediately after eating, at dawn, on an empty stomach, and together with food. // 55 //

children.text: ajīrṇaṃ jīrayaty āśu pītam uṣṇodakaṃ niśi /
children.translated_text: Hot water drunk at night quickly digests indigestion;

children.text: varṣāsu na jalaṃ grāhyaṃ nādeyaṃ bahudoṣakṛt // 57 //
children.translated_text: during the rains, riverine water should not be taken, as it greatly aggravates the <s>doṣas</s>. // 57 //

body.translated_text: Now, the qualities of boiled water (<s>śṛtodaka</s>).

children.text: kaphe pādāvaśeṣaṃ tu pānīyaṃ laghu dīpanam /
children.translated_text: In <s>kapha</s> [conditions], [water boiled down to] one-quarter [of its original volume] is light and kindles digestion;

children.text: divāśṛtaṃ tu yat toyaṃ rātrau tad gurutāṃ vrajet //
children.translated_text: water boiled during the day becomes heavy at night;

children.text: śṛtaṃ śītaṃ tridoṣaghnam uṣitaṃ tac ca doṣakṛt /
children.translated_text: boiled and cooled water destroys all three <s>doṣas</s> — and when stale, it aggravates the <s>doṣas</s>;

children.text: tat pādaśeṣaṃ doṣaghnaṃ ardhahīnaṃ tu vātajit // 57 //
children.translated_text: [boiled down to] one-quarter destroys the <s>doṣas</s>; reduced by half conquers <s>vāta</s>. // 57 //

body.text: rātrau śṛtaṃ tu divase gurutvam api gacchati /
body.translated_text: Water boiled at night becomes heavy during the day.
Now, the prohibition of drinking cold water in flank pain and other [conditions].
In flank pain (<s>pārśvaśūla</s>), in cold (<s>pratiśyāya</s>), in <s>vāta</s> disorders, in throat obstruction, // 58 //

children.translated_text: in flatulence (<s>ādhmāna</s>), in numbness (<s>stimita</s>), in hoarseness (<s>koṣṭha</s>), immediately after purification, in fresh fever,
in hiccup and in <s>snehaja pitta</s> (oleaginous bile disorder), one should avoid cold water. // 59 //

body.translated_text: Now, the regulation of drinking small quantities of water in abdominal tumors and other [conditions].

children.translated_text: In abdominal tumors (<s>gulma</s>), hemorrhoids (<s>arśas</s>), abdominal hardness (<s>grahāṇī</s>), wasting, abdominal distension, weak digestive fire, and flatulence,

children.text: śophe pāṇḍugalagrahe ca jagade (vraṇagade) mohe (mehe) ca netrāmaye /
children.translated_text: in edema (<s>śopha</s>), throat obstruction, wounds, delusion (or urinary disorders), and eye diseases,
in <s>vāta</s>-induced loss of appetite, excessive diarrhea accompanied by <s>kapha</s>, and <s>kuṣṭha</s> with cold,

children.text: uṣṇaṃ vāri suśītalaṃ śṛtahimaṃ svalpaṃ prapeyaṃ jalam // 60 //
children.translated_text: one should drink hot water, or well-cooled water, or boiled and cooled water, in small quantities. // 60 //
When free from <s>āma</s> (undigested matter), after meals, one may drink very cool water;

children.text: ajīrṇe tu pibed vāri śītalaṃ svecchayā punaḥ //
children.translated_text: in indigestion, however, one should drink cool water again as desired.

body.translated_text: Now, the qualities of water cooled by immersion (<s>nirvāpitodaka</s>).

children.translated_text: Water combined with heated iron balls and quenched with a metal lump,
removes all <s>doṣas</s>, is wholesome, and always alleviates disorders.

body.translated_text: Now, the praise of water.

children.text: kvacid uṣṇaṃ kvacic chītaṃ kvacit kvathitaśītalam /
children.translated_text: Sometimes hot, sometimes cold, sometimes boiled and then cooled,

children.text: kvacid bheṣajasaṃyuktaṃ kvacid vāri nivāryate {cf. Rājanighaṇṭu 14.80} //
children.translated_text: sometimes mixed with medicine — water is never to be completely prohibited. {cf. <s>Rājanighaṇṭu</s> 14.80}

children.text: tṛṣito moham āyāti mohāt prāṇān vimuñcati /
children.translated_text: One who is thirsty becomes delirious, and from delirium one loses one's <s>prāṇa</s> (vital breath);

children.text: tasmāt svalpaṃ ca dātavyaṃ na kvacid vāri vāryate // 65 //
children.translated_text: therefore, a small amount should be given — water should never be entirely withheld. // 65 //

children.text: pānīyaṃ prāṇināṃ prāṇā viśvam eva hi tan mayam /
children.translated_text: Water is the very life-breath of living beings; indeed, the entire world is pervaded by it.
Therefore, even in the strictest regimen, water should never be completely prohibited. // 66 //
In cases of fainting, <s>pitta</s> (bile), heat, and burning sensations, in bleeding disorders (<s>pittarakta</s>), in alcoholic intoxication,
in those afflicted by dizziness and exhaustion, and in <s>tamaka</s> (asthmatic breathing) — cold water should be drunk.
One may drink thousands of <s>ghaṭas</s> (pots) as long as the sun has not set;

children.text: astaṃ gate divānāthe bindur eko ghaṭāyate // 68 //
children.translated_text: once the lord of the day has set, even a single drop becomes like a pot. // 68 //

children.text: ajīrṇe cauṣadhaṃ vāri jīrṇe vāri balapradam /
children.translated_text: In <s>ajīrṇa</s> (indigestion), water is like medicine; when digestion is complete, water gives strength;

children.text: bhojane cāmṛtaṃ vāri rātrau vāri viṣopamam // 62 //
children.translated_text: during a meal, water is like <s>amṛta</s> (nectar); at night, water is like poison. // 62 //

children.text: atyambupānān na vipacyate 'nnaṃ nirambupānāc ca sa eva doṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: From drinking too much water, food is not digested; and from drinking no water at all, the same defect arises.

children.text: tasmān naro vahnivivardhanāya muhurmuhur vāri pibed abhūri // 70 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, to strengthen the digestive fire, one should drink water little by little, not in excess. // 70 //
One who is afflicted by hunger, dryness, and irritation of the heart and throat, should first eat many morsels

children.text: na bhukte prapibed ambu śītalaṃ mātrayā yutam // 71 //
children.translated_text: and not drink cold water immediately — one should drink it in measured quantity. // 71 //

children.text: tena hṛtkaṇṭhaśuddhiḥ syāt sukhenānnaṃ pataty adhaḥ /
children.translated_text: By this, purification of the heart and throat occurs, and the food easily descends downward;

children.text: snigdhayuktaṃ ca yad bhaktaṃ tatas saṃtarpaṇaṃ bhavet // 72 //
children.translated_text: and when the food is accompanied by unctuous substances, then it becomes nourishing. // 72 //

children.text: ādau dravaṃ samaśnīyāt tatrāmbu na pibed bahu /
children.translated_text: At the beginning, one should eat liquid foods; therein one should not drink much water.

children.text: madhye tu kathinaṃ bhuṅkte yatheṣṭaṃ śasyate jalam // 73 //
children.translated_text: In the middle, one eats solid food — then water is recommended as desired. // 73 //

children.text: prāk dravaṃ puruṣo 'śnīyāt madhye tu kathināśanaḥ /
children.translated_text: First, one should eat liquid food; in the middle, one should take solid food;

children.text: ante punar dravāśī tu vastyārogye (?) na muṃcati // 74 //
children.translated_text: and at the end, one who eats liquid food again does not suffer from diseases of the bladder. // 74 //
Likewise, water drunk at the end of a meal bestows strength.

children.text: dravyaṃ prayāti bhuktānte kin tu tanmātrayā pibet // 75 //
children.translated_text: Liquid food is beneficial at the end of eating, but one should drink it in measured quantity. // 75 //

children.text: ādau jalaṃ vahnivināśakāri paścāt tadante kaphabṛṃhaṇaṃ ca /
children.translated_text: Water at the beginning destroys the digestive fire; at the end, it increases <s>kapha</s> (phlegm).

children.text: madhye tu pītaṃ samatāsukhaṃ ca tasyābhiyogo 'bhimatas sakṛc ca // 76 //
children.translated_text: But drunk in the middle, it brings balance and comfort — its regular practice in moderation is recommended. // 76 //

children.text: amṛtaṃ viṣam iti salilaṃ cedaṃ niṣṭhā (vidyā) d atividitatatvārthaḥ /
children.translated_text: Water is <s>amṛta</s> (nectar) or <s>viṣa</s> (poison) — this is the established knowledge for one who fully understands its true nature.

children.text: yuttayā sevitam amṛtaṃ viṣam etad ayuktitaḥ pītam // 77 //
children.translated_text: Consumed with proper method, it is nectar; drunk improperly, it is poison. // 77 //
One who is well-established should fill two parts of the stomach with food,
one part with water, and leave the fourth part for the movement of <s>vāyu</s> (air). // 78 //

children.text: grāse grāse tu pātavyaṃ śītalaṃ vāri sarvadā /
children.translated_text: With every morsel, cold water should always be sipped.
Food accompanied by abundant water is digested quickly by the fire. // 79 //

children.text: tasmād ādāv atisvalpaṃ madhye ca tṛptidāyakam /
children.translated_text: Therefore, at the beginning very little, in the middle that which satisfies,

children.text: mātrayā ca pibed ante na rogair bādhyate naraḥ // 80 //
children.translated_text: and at the end in measured quantity — one who drinks thus is not afflicted by diseases. // 80 //

body.translated_text: Perfumed with fresh flowers such as <s>pāṭalī</s> (trumpet flower), <s>campaka</s>, and others,

body.text: pathyaṃ sugandhi hṛdyaṃ ca śītalāmbu sadā pibet // 81 //
body.translated_text: cool water that is wholesome, fragrant, and pleasing to the heart should always be drunk. // 81 //

children.translated_text: That which is easily available, perfumed with <s>sarovāla</s> (lotus fiber) and <s>śakala</s> (bark) pieces,

children.text: karpūreṇa ca yat toyaṃ tat peyaṃ sarvadā nṛṇām // 82 //
children.translated_text: and water scented with <s>karpūra</s> (camphor) — that should always be drunk by people. // 82 //

children.text: grīṣme śaradi pātavyaṃ svecchayā salilaṃ naraiḥ /
children.translated_text: In summer and autumn, water may be drunk freely at will by people.
At other times, only a small amount should be drunk out of fear of <s>vāta</s> (wind) and <s>śleṣma</s> (phlegm). // 83 //

children.text: anye (anne) nāpi vinā jantuḥ prāṇān saṃdhārayec ciram /
children.translated_text: Even without food, a creature cannot sustain its vital breaths for long.
In the absence of water, one tormented by thirst quickly dies. // 84 //
When milk is combined with food at the beginning, middle, and end of a meal,

children.text: kṛśaṃ sādhyaṃ (kārśyaṃ sābhyaṃ) tathā sthaulyaṃ bhavanti kramaśo guṇāḥ // 85 //
children.translated_text: emaciation, health, and corpulence respectively are the resulting qualities. // 85 //

children.text: pānīyaṃ pānīyaṃ śaradi vasante ca pānīyam /
children.translated_text: Rainwater in autumn and spring is fit for drinking.

children.text: nādeyaṃ nādeyaṃ śaradi vasante ca nādeyam // 86 //
children.translated_text: River water in autumn and spring is fit for drinking. // 86 //

body.text: ity āyur vedamahodadhau śrīsuṣeṇakṛtau pānīyaguṇāḥ samāptāḥ //
body.translated_text: Thus ends the section on the qualities of drinking water in the <s>Āyurvedamahodadhi</s> composed by <s>Suṣeṇa</s>.
Now begins the section on water heated with wood (<s>kāṣṭhataptodakavarga</s>).

children.translated_text: it destroys misfortune, <s>raktapitta</s> (bleeding disorders), and purifies the <s>doṣas</s> (bodily humors). // 1 //

body.translated_text: Water heated with the wood of <s>gandharvahasata</s> (castor plant) is highly esteemed;

children.text: bhallātakaiś ca kāṣṭhaiś ca taptaṃ vāri śubhodakam /
children.translated_text: Water heated with the wood of <s>bhallātaka</s> (marking nut) is auspicious water;
it removes <s>vāta</s> (wind) and <s>śleṣma</s> (phlegm), is wholesome, and increases virility and vitality. // 2 //
Water heated with the wood of <s>pālāśa</s> (Butea frondosa) and <s>udumbara</s> (fig tree) is auspicious;
it heals wounds and ulcers, and increases blood, strength, and virility. // 3 //
Water from a tank heated with the wood of <s>jambū</s> (rose apple), <s>kapittha</s> (wood apple), and <s>āmra</s> (mango)
bestows intellect and strength, and destroys defects of virility and worms. // 4 //
Water from a well or tank should be heated with <s>dumbarī</s> (fig) wood;

children.text: kaphahṛt tac ca nirdiṣṭaṃ doṣāṇāṃ ca vināśanam // 5 //
children.translated_text: it removes <s>kapha</s> (phlegm) and is declared to be free of fault and destructive of <s>doṣas</s> (humors). // 5 //
Water heated with <s>khadira</s> (catechu) wood destroys <s>raktapitta</s> (bleeding disorders);

children.text: āpyāyanakaraṃ grīṣme śreṣṭham uktam idaṃ jalam // 6 //
children.translated_text: it is nourishing, and in summer it is declared to be the best water. // 6 //
Water from rivers and seas heated with <s>kadamba</s> and <s>nimba</s> (neem) wood
is wholesome, removes <s>doṣas</s> (humors), and destroys itching and <s>raktapitta</s> (bleeding disorders). // 7 //
Water heated with <s>dhātrī</s> (āmalakī, gooseberry) and <s>dāru</s> (devadāru, deodar) wood, being the water of purification,
is excellent in removing <s>vāta</s> (wind) and <s>pitta</s> (bile), and is supremely <s>rasāyana</s> (rejuvenative). // 8 //

children.text: puṣkarassa (madhukasya) ca kāṣṭhaiś ca taptaṃ kūpodbhavodakam /
children.translated_text: Well water heated with the wood of <s>puṣkara</s> (or <s>madhuka</s>, licorice)
is excellent in removing <s>vāta</s> (wind) and <s>pitta</s> (bile), and is supremely <s>rasāyana</s> (rejuvenative). // 9 //

body.text:
(grahaṇīpāṇḍuhṛtkāsaśvāsahṛtparamaṃ hitaṃ /)
karpūra (karkandhu) dārusaṃbhūtataptam uṣṇodakaṃ śubham (nādeyam udakottamam /)

children.translated_text: This abode of the digestive fire was demonstrated by <s>Suśruta</s>. // 10 //

body.translated_text: Water heated with the wood of <s>karpūra</s> (or <s>karkandhu</s>, jujube) is auspicious warm water, beneficial for <s>grahaṇī</s> (digestive disorders), <s>pāṇḍu</s> (anemia), heart disease, cough, <s>śvāsa</s> (dyspnea), and heart ailments.

children.translated_text: With the resin-woods of <s>sallakī</s> (frankincense) and <s>śāka</s> (teak), each separately,

children.text: taptaṃ nirjharajaṃ vāri nāmayān janayed varam (rogān saṃjanaded bahūn) // 11 //
children.translated_text: spring water heated thus either cures diseases or produces many. // 11 //

children.text: vaṭaiś cārjunakāṣṭhaiś ca saṃtataṃ tāpitaṃ jalam /
children.translated_text: Water constantly heated with <s>vaṭa</s> (banyan) and <s>arjuna</s> wood
generates strength, intellect, and progeny — this was demonstrated by <s>Maitreya</s>. // 12 //
<s>Tarkārī</s> (a vegetable preparation) destroys <s>vāta</s> (wind) but increases itching and skin diseases.
Fresh water, well-heated, is beneficial for cleansing impurities. // 13 //

body.translated_text: // Thus ends the section on water heated with wood (<s>kāṣṭhataptodakavarga</s>). //
Now, the special qualities according to the type of vessel.

children.text: hemapātre ca susvādu vipāke śītalaṃ madhu /
children.translated_text: Water in a golden vessel is very tasty, cooling in its post-digestive effect, sweet as honey,
pacifies all three <s>doṣas</s> (humors), and promotes virility, strength, and intellect — it is auspicious. // 1 //

children.text: trapupātrodakaṃ yac ca picchalaṃ madhuraṃ rase /
children.translated_text: Water kept in a tin vessel is slimy and sweet in taste,
produces <s>kapha</s> (phlegm) in potency, and increases digestive power and <s>vāta</s> (wind). // 2 //

body.text: ghoṣapātre yad udakaṃ vipāke kaṭukaṃ guru

children.text: pittaśleṣmapradaṃ vṛddhe yathākālaṃ balāya ca (vṛddhau vyathākālānurūpitam) // 3 //
children.translated_text: it produces <s>pitta</s> (bile) and <s>śleṣma</s> (phlegm) in the elderly, according to time and strength. // 3 //

body.translated_text: Water in a bell-metal (<s>ghoṣa</s>) vessel is pungent in post-digestive effect and heavy;

children.translated_text: and sprinkling it on the eyes — this pacifies all three <s>doṣas</s> and is beneficial. // 4 //

body.translated_text: Drinking milk that has been poured in a stream, which is very cool upon smelling,

children.translated_text: Water in a copper vessel is drying in taste, somewhat astringent and pungent;
it produces <s>pitta</s> (bile) and <s>vāta</s> (wind) in the elderly, and destroys digestive power and wind. // 5 //
Water stored in a brass vessel is pungent and destroys <s>śleṣma</s> (phlegm);
it is bilious, somewhat hot, and aggravates urinary disorders (<s>meharoga</s>). // 6 //

children.text: lohabhājanasaṃsthaṃ ca payaḥ pānaṃ ca dūṣitam /
children.translated_text: Milk and water kept in an iron vessel become contaminated;
they cause <s>raktapitta</s> (bleeding disorders), itching, and are supreme in pacifying the three <s>doṣas</s>. // 7 //
Water heated in an iron vessel causes itching and weakens the digestive fire;
it is said to be beneficial for purging impurities and cleansing the internal organs. // 8 //
Water heated in a <s>madhūdumbara</s> (fig wood) vessel is the best water;

children.text: vapuḥ kāntipradaṃ pitte (proktaṃ) vahnimāndyakaraṃ sakṛt (ca tat) // 9 //
children.translated_text: it bestows beauty and radiance to the body, but occasionally weakens the digestive fire. // 9 //

body.text: bhājane mṛnmaye taptaṃ malānāṃ kṣālane hitam

children.translated_text: it balances the <s>dhātus</s> (bodily tissues) and increases virility, strength, and <s>ojas</s> (vital essence). // 10 //

body.translated_text: Water heated in an earthen vessel is beneficial for cleansing impurities;
// Thus ends the section on vessel-infusion methods in the <s>Āyurvedamahodadhi</s> composed by <s>Suṣeṇa</s>. //
Now the qualities of <s>kṣīra</s> (milk) are described.

body.text:
tatrāpi gavyamāhiṣayor eva sadopayogitvāt
tayor eva prathamaṃ svarūpaṃ vicāryate //
body.translated_text: Among these, since cow's and buffalo's milk are constantly used, their nature is examined first.

children.text: gavyaṃ himaṃ medhyatama hi dugdhaṃ prāṇapradaṃ pittasamīraṇaghnam /
children.translated_text: Cow's milk is cooling, supremely intellect-enhancing, life-giving, and destroys <s>pitta</s> (bile) and <s>vāta</s> (wind);

children.text: rasāyanaṃ varṇakaraṃ mukeśyaṃ ārogyahetuḥ satataṃ narāṇām // 1 //
children.translated_text: it is <s>rasāyana</s> (rejuvenative), complexion-enhancing, beneficial for <s>mukha</s> (the face), and constantly promotes health in people. // 1 //

children.text: kṣīraṃ sākṣāt* jīvanaṃ janmasāhyā(tmyā)t tad dhāroṣṇaṃ gavyam āyuṣyam uṣṇam /
children.translated_text: Milk is directly life-sustaining; due to being habituated from birth, cow's milk that nourishes the <s>dhātus</s> (tissues) is life-promoting and warming.

children.text: prātaḥ sāyaṃ grāmyadharmāvasāne bhukte paścād okasātmyaṃ karoti // 2 //
children.translated_text: Drunk morning and evening, after the conclusion of sexual activity, and after meals, it creates habituation. // 2 //

body.translated_text: Now, the special qualities of milk according to the color of cows.

children.translated_text: The milk of white cows destroys <s>vāta</s> (wind); that of black cows destroys <s>pitta</s> (bile);
that of red cows destroys <s>kapha</s> (phlegm); and the milk of tawny cows destroys all three. // 3 //
It is cooling, sweet, unctuous, and supremely removes <s>vāta</s> (wind) and <s>pitta</s> (bile);

children.text: vṛṣyam ojaskaraṃ hṛdyaṃ śleṣmaghnaṃ ca rasāyanam // 4 //
children.translated_text: it is aphrodisiac, promotes <s>ojas</s> (vital essence), is pleasing to the heart, destroys <s>śleṣma</s> (phlegm), and is <s>rasāyana</s> (rejuvenative). // 4 //
it pacifies <s>śvāsa</s> (dyspnea) and <s>kāsa</s> (cough), and removes the three types of fatigue and intoxication. // 5 //

body.translated_text: Sweet in post-digestive effect, intellect-enhancing, it bestows strength to those weakened by <s>kṣaya</s> (consumption);

children.translated_text: In chronic fever, <s>mūtrakṛcchra</s> (urinary difficulty), and <s>raktapitta</s> (bleeding disorders), it is recommended.
Cow's milk is pure and promotes strength and nourishment. // 6 //
Cow's milk cures dizziness, bleeding, <s>pitta</s> (bile), fatigue, intoxication,
<s>kṣaya</s> (consumption), misfortune, <s>gulma</s> (abdominal tumors), <s>pradara</s> (excessive discharge), poisoning, <s>pāṇḍu</s> (anemia), and <s>vāmaya</s> (vomiting);
it pacifies <s>kṛcchra</s> (painful conditions), fever, <s>śvayathu</s> (swelling), and diseases of the spleen,
and quickly alleviates thirst, obesity, fainting, fever, and <s>vāta</s> (wind disorders). // 7 //

body.translated_text: It is excellent, promotes eye health and longevity, and bestows radiance and beauty.
Now, the special qualities according to the type of vessel.

children.translated_text: Milk in a copper vessel removes <s>vāta</s> (wind); in a golden vessel, it destroys <s>pitta</s> (bile);
in a silver vessel, it removes <s>śleṣma</s> (phlegm); and in a bell-metal vessel, it purifies the blood. // 8 //

body.translated_text: Thus ends the section on cow's milk.
Now, buffalo milk (<s>mahiṣīkṣīra</s>).

children.translated_text: <s>Māhiṣa</s> (buffalo) milk bestows strength, complexion, and <s>ojas</s> (vital essence); it promotes sleep and gives strength of semen.

children.text: tīkṣṇāgniśamanaṃ svādu rase pāke ca puṣṭidam // 1 //
children.translated_text: It quells intense digestive fire, is sweet in taste and post-digestive effect, and is nourishing. // 1 //
For one whose body is exhausted from exercise, it removes fatigue and dispels <s>vāta</s> (wind);
even for an old man devoid of desire, it bestows desire for women. // 2 //

body.translated_text: Even for a strong young man, it especially grants desire.
Thus ends the section on buffalo milk.
Now, goat's milk (<s>ajākṣīra</s>).

children.translated_text: Because goats have little desire, eat pungent and bitter plants,
do not drink too much water, and exercise much — their milk cures all diseases. // 1 //
Goat's milk strengthens the digestive fire, and supremely removes <s>kṣaya</s> (consumption), desire-disorders, <s>śvāsa</s> (dyspnea), and hiccups;

children.text: raktapittaharam āśv atisāre raktaje ca kathitaṃ hitam eva // 4 [sic!] //
children.translated_text: it removes <s>raktapitta</s> (bleeding disorders) quickly and is declared beneficial in <s>atisāra</s> (diarrhea) caused by blood. // 4 //

body.translated_text: Now, camel's milk (<s>uṣṭrīkṣīra</s>).

children.translated_text: Camel's milk removes numbness and edema, and is excellent for <s>pitta</s> (bile), <s>śleṣma</s> (phlegm), and excessive hemorrhoids;

children.text: ānāhaghnaṃ codarāṇāṃ praśastaṃ jantughnaṃ vai śasyate sarvakālam // 5 //
children.translated_text: it cures <s>ānāha</s> (flatulence), is excellent for abdominal diseases, destroys intestinal worms, and is recommended at all times. // 5 //

body.translated_text: Now, mare's milk (<s>aśvākṣīra</s>).

children.text: uṣṇam aikaśaphaṃ balyaṃ śvāsa (śākhā) vātāpahaṃ payaḥ /
children.translated_text: The milk of single-hoofed animals is warming, strengthening, and removes <s>śvāsa</s> (dyspnea) and <s>vāta</s> (wind);
it has a sweet-sour taste, is dry, slightly salty in secondary taste, and light. // 6 //

body.translated_text: (Donkey and mare's milk.)
Now, human breast milk (<s>strīstanya</s>).

children.translated_text: Human breast milk is sweet, with an astringent secondary taste, and cooling;

children.text: nasyāś cotanapathyaṃ ca jīvanaṃ laghu dīpanam // 7 //
children.translated_text: it is suitable for nasal administration and eye drops, is life-sustaining, light, and stimulates digestion. // 7 //

body.translated_text: Now, elephant's milk (<s>hastinīkṣīra</s>).

children.translated_text: Elephant's milk is sweet, aphrodisiac, with an astringent secondary taste, and heavy;

children.text: snigdhaṃ (sthai) dhairyakaraṃ śītaṃ cakṣuṣyaṃ balavardhanam {cf. Rājanighaṇṭu 15.15} //
children.translated_text: it is unctuous, promotes steadfastness, is cooling, good for the eyes, and strength-enhancing. {cf. <s>Rājanighaṇṭu</s> 15.15}

body.translated_text: Now, the general qualities of all milks.

children.translated_text: Milk is generally declared to be channel-blocking, heavy, and raw;
that which stands for a long time should be known as heavier, more nourishing, and more strengthening. // 8 //

children.text: varjayitvā striyāḥ stanya āmam eva hi khāṇḍitam /
children.translated_text: Except for a woman's breast milk, all raw milk that is consumed

children.text: dharoṣmam amṛtaṃ kṣīraṃ viparītam ato cyate ('nyathā) // 9 //
children.translated_text: warm from the udder is <s>amṛta</s> (nectar); otherwise, it deteriorates. // 9 //

body.translated_text: Now, condemned milk (<s>ninditadugdha</s>).

children.text: aniṣṭagandham amlaṃ ca vivarṇaṃ virasaṃ ca yat /
children.translated_text: Milk that has an unpleasant smell, is sour, discolored, or tasteless,

children.text: varjaṃ (rjyaṃ) salavaṇaṃ kṣīraṃ yac ca vigrathitaṃ bhavet /
children.translated_text: or that is salty or curdled — such milk should be rejected.

children.text: kṣīraṃ na bhuñjīna (divā) yadi bhuñjīta na svapet /
children.translated_text: One should not consume milk during the day; if one does consume it, one should not sleep.

children.text: yadi svapet kṣayaṃ cāyus tasmāt kṣīraṃ divāmṛtam // 11 //
children.translated_text: If one sleeps after drinking milk, it causes <s>kṣaya</s> (consumption) and shortens life; therefore, milk consumed during the day is death-like. // 11 //

body.translated_text: Now, the qualities of <s>dhāroṣṇa</s> (warm milk fresh from the udder) and other preparations.

children.translated_text: Freshly drawn warm [milk] is like nectar, wholesome; when cooled in a stream, it aggravates the three <s>doṣas</s>;
when boiled and cooled, it destroys the three <s>doṣas</s>; boiled and warm, it conquers <s>kapha</s> and <s>vāta</s>. (12)

children.text: athāvikaṃ pathyatamaṃ śṛtoṣṇaṃ mājaṃ payo vai śṛtaśītam eva /
children.translated_text: Moreover, sheep's milk is most wholesome when boiled and warm; goat's milk indeed when boiled and cooled;

children.text: dhārāsuśītaṃ mahiṣīpayaś ca dhāroṣṇam evaṃ hitam eva gavyam // 13 //
children.translated_text: buffalo milk when well-cooled in a stream; and cow's milk is beneficial when freshly drawn warm. (13)
And further:

children.text: pittaghnaṃ māhiṣaṃ kṣīraṃ vātaghnaṃ cāvikaṃ payaḥ /
children.translated_text: Buffalo milk destroys <s>pitta</s>; sheep's milk destroys <s>vāta</s>;
cow's milk removes <s>vāta</s> and <s>pitta</s>; goat's milk destroys the three <s>doṣas</s>. (14)

body.translated_text: Now, the qualities of morning milk and so forth:

children.text: prāyaḥ prābhātikaṃ kṣīraṃ guru viṣṭambhi śītalam /
children.translated_text: Generally, morning milk is heavy, constipating, and cooling,
due to the predominance of <s>soma</s> (lunar) qualities at night and the absence of exercise. (17)
For those heated by the sun, through exercise and exposure to wind,
afternoon milk removes <s>vāta</s> and <s>pitta</s> and is beneficial for the eyes. (16)

body.translated_text: Now, the special qualities of drinking milk in the forenoon and other times:

children.translated_text: In the forenoon, milk is aphrodisiac, nourishing, and promotes digestive fire;
at midday it gives strength, promotes sexual vigor, and breaks up painful urinary stones;

children.text: bāle tv agnikaraṃ kṣaye balakaraṃ vṛddhasya retovahaṃ
children.translated_text: for a child it promotes digestive fire, in wasting diseases it gives strength, for the elderly it carries semen;

children.text: rātrau kṣīram anekadoṣaśamanaṃ sevyaṃ sadā prāṇibhiḥ // 17 //
children.translated_text: at night, milk alleviates numerous disorders and should always be consumed by living beings. (17)

body.text: bhuktā ye kaṭutīvracaṇḍavidalā ye cāmlatiktā rasāḥ

children.translated_text: that are dry, alkaline, burning, desiccating, and excessively heating,
that are astringent, pungent, dry, and exceedingly hard to digest —

children.text: tat sarvaṃ balakṛt karoti tarasā dugdhaṃ niśāsevitam // 18 //
children.translated_text: all that is counteracted and made strength-giving swiftly by milk consumed at night. (18)

body.translated_text: Those who have eaten foods that are pungent, sharp, harsh, splitting, sour, or bitter in taste,
Now, the time-limit for the alteration of milk:

children.translated_text: After five <s>muhūrtas</s> (approximately two hours and twenty minutes), milk undergoes alteration;

children.text: tad eva dviguṇe kāle viṣavad dhanti mānavam // 19 //
children.translated_text: that same [milk], after twice that time, strikes a person like poison. (19)

body.translated_text: Now, further praise of the qualities of freshly drawn warm milk:

children.translated_text: Freshly drawn warm cow's milk pacifies the aggravation of <s>vāta</s> and promotes nourishment;
it swiftly destroys anemia (<s>pāṇḍu</s>) and jaundice (<s>kāmalaka</s>), and cures difficult urinary disorders;
it conquers burning sensations in the body, heat in the hands, feet, and eyes, and excess of bile (<s>pitta</s>),
corrupted blood, emaciation, diseases caused by emaciation, and urinary disorders. (20)

body.translated_text: Now, the determination of wholesome times for boiled and other [kinds of] milk:

body.text: akvathitaṃ daśa ghaṭikāḥ kvathitaṃ dviguṇāś ca tāḥ payaḥ pathyam

children.text: uṣasi ca sarasādyāṃ (?) (koṣṇaṃ ca svarasāḍhyaṃ) yāvat tāvat payaḥ prāśyam // 21 //
children.translated_text: at dawn, warm with its natural juices — for that long, milk should be drunk. (21)

body.translated_text: Unboiled milk is wholesome for ten <s>ghaṭikās</s> (four hours); boiled milk for twice that duration;
Now, the wholesomeness and unwholesomeness of milk in fever:

children.translated_text: In chronic fever, when <s>kapha</s> is diminished, milk is like nectar;

children.text: tad eva taruṇe pītaṃ viṣavad dhanti mānavam // 22 //
children.translated_text: that very same [milk], drunk in acute fever, strikes a person like poison. (22)

children.text: tasmāc chṛtaṃ vāpy aśrutaṃ kṣīraṃ tātkālikaṃ pibet /
children.translated_text: Therefore, one should drink milk — whether boiled or unboiled — that is fresh;
that which has been prepared by adding one-quarter water and boiling — that is the [proper] milk. (23)

body.translated_text: Therefore, that is the best for strength-giving, beneficial, and removes all ailments.
Now, the preparation of milk for those to whom milk is not agreeable:

body.text: (yeṣāṃ na sātmyaṃ) etac ca sākṣāt kṣīreṇa pītaṃ cādhmānakārakam // 24 //
body.translated_text: For those to whom it is not agreeable, this [milk] drunk directly causes bloating. (24)

children.translated_text: For them, adding half water with dry ginger and long pepper,

children.text: āvartayet kṣīraśeṣaṃ tat pītvā sukham āvahet // 25 //
children.translated_text: one should boil until only the milk remains; drinking that brings comfort. (25)

body.translated_text: Now, the determination of drinking times according to the types of cow's milk and other milks:

body.text:
pūrvāhṇe māhiṣaṃ saśarkaraṃ svecchayā vā?
yeṣāṃ sāmyaṃ sadā bhavet /

children.translated_text: cow's milk should be [taken] in the forenoon, buffalo milk in the afternoon;

children.text: kṣīraṃ saśarkaraṃ pathyaṃ yathāsātmyaṃ ca sarvadāḥ iti pāṭhyam)
children.translated_text: milk with sugar is wholesome, always according to one's habit. (Variant reading)

children.text: ādau madhyāhne vā (tenādau tat tu madhye ca) grāmasyānte kadācana // 26 //
children.translated_text: at the beginning, at midday, or at the end of the village [meal], occasionally. (26)

body.translated_text: Buffalo milk with sugar in the forenoon, or according to one's own preference, for those to whom it is always agreeable;

body.text: sarvaṃ tan mānaśeṣaṃ (sarvabhojanaśeṣe) tu payaḥ śastaṃ (peyaṃ) sadā naraiḥ /
body.translated_text: After all food, milk should always be drunk by people.
Now, a description of the qualities of boiled-and-cooled milk and other types:

body.text: pittaghnaṃ śṛtaśītalaṃ kaphaharaṃ pakvaṃ tad uṣṇaṃ punaḥ

children.text: śītaṃ yat tu na pācitaṃ tad akhilaṃ viṣṭambhadoṣāvaham
children.translated_text: that which is cold and uncooked is entirely productive of constipation and disorders;

children.text: dhāroṣṇaṃ tv amṛtaṃ payaḥ śramaharaṃ nidrākaraṃ kāntidaṃ
children.translated_text: freshly drawn warm milk is like nectar, removes fatigue, induces sleep, gives radiance,

children.text: tṛṣyaṃ bṛhaṇam agnivardhanam iti svādu tridoṣāpaham // 27 //
children.translated_text: is thirst-quenching, nourishing, promotes digestive fire — sweet, it removes the three <s>doṣas</s>. (27)

body.translated_text: Boiled and cooled, it destroys <s>pitta</s>; boiled, it removes <s>kapha</s>; and that same heated again —
Now, the prohibition of drinking milk together with food-poisons:

children.text: kṣīraṃ bhuñjīta godhūmānnena naiva ca naiva ca /
children.translated_text: One should never, never drink milk with wheat-food;

children.text: piṣṭānnenāpi nāśnīyān na dadhnā lavaṇena ca // 28 //
children.translated_text: nor should one eat it with food made from flour, nor with yogurt, nor with salt. (28)

children.text: na māṣair na ca mudrair vā na guḍena phalena vā /
children.translated_text: Not with black gram (<s>māṣa</s>), nor with green gram (<s>mudga</s>), nor with jaggery, nor with fruit;

children.text: bhūmikandair na vā śākair matsyamāṃsādibhir na vā // 29 //
children.translated_text: not with root-vegetables, nor with leafy vegetables, nor with fish, meat, and the like. (29)

body.translated_text: Now, the qualities of <s>pāyasa</s> (milk-rice pudding):

children.text: pāyasaṃ bhakṣayed yuktyā tat pakvaṃ hi samaṃ pibet /
children.translated_text: One should eat <s>pāyasa</s> with discernment; indeed, when properly cooked, one should drink it;

children.text: vṛṣyaṃ hṛdyaṃ ca pathyaṃ ca tat pittānalanāśanam // 30 //
children.translated_text: it is aphrodisiac, pleasing to the heart, wholesome, and destroys <s>pitta</s> and digestive fire [disorders]. (30)

body.translated_text: Now, the prohibition of drinking milk three times a day even for those with balanced digestion:

children.text: snigdhatvād gauravāj jāḍyāt trikālaṃ na pibet payaḥ /
children.translated_text: Due to its unctuousness, heaviness, and coldness, one should not drink milk three times a day —

children.text: samāgnir api kiṃ cānyo mandāgnir viṣamo 'thavā // 31 //
children.translated_text: even one with balanced digestive fire, let alone another with weak or irregular fire. (31)

body.translated_text: The permission for those with sharp digestive fire:

children.text: tīkṣṇāgninā tu pātavyaṃ dvikālam api māhiṣam /
children.translated_text: However, one with sharp digestive fire may drink buffalo milk even twice a day;

children.text: tasya dhātūn pacaty agnir yadā tena na siñcati // 32 //
children.translated_text: when one's fire digests the <s>dhātus</s> (tissues) and is not nourishing them — [then milk serves as nourishment]. (32)

body.translated_text: Now, further praise of milk:

children.text: kṣiraṃ [rasaṃ] hitaṃ śreṣṭharasāyanaṃ ca kṣīraṃ vapurvarṇabalāyuṣe ca /
children.translated_text: Milk is beneficial, the best <s>rasāyana</s> (rejuvenative); milk promotes physique, complexion, strength, and longevity;

children.text: kṣīraṃ hi cāyuṣyakaraṃ narāṇāṃ kṣīraṃ balāsthāpanam uttamaṃ ca // 33 //
children.translated_text: milk indeed promotes longevity for people; milk is the supreme establisher of strength. (33)

children.text: kṣīraṃ hi sandīpanapācanīyaṃ kṣīraṃ hi coṣṇaṃ malaśodhanaṃ ca /
children.translated_text: Milk indeed stimulates and aids digestion; hot milk indeed purifies waste matter;

children.text: kṣīraṃ hi saṃdhānakṛduṣṇaśītaṃ kṣīraṃ kavoṣṇaṃ malanāśānaṃ ca // 34 //
children.translated_text: milk, hot and cold, promotes healing; lukewarm milk indeed destroys impurities. (34)

body.translated_text: Now, the prohibition of consuming milk together with fish and other [incompatibles]:

children.translated_text: Milk consumed with fish, meat, jaggery, green gram, and radish causes skin disease (<s>kuṣṭha</s>);

children.text: śākajāmbavasurādisevitaṃ mārayaty abudham āśu sarpavat {cf. Rājanighaṇṭu 15.30} // 35 //
children.translated_text: consumed with leafy vegetables, <s>jāmbu</s> (rose apple), <s>surā</s> (liquor), and the like, it kills the ignorant swiftly like a serpent. (35)

body.translated_text: Now, the method of drinking milk with specific tastes:

children.text: kṣīreṇa saha bhojyāni na viruddhāni tadyathā /
children.translated_text: With milk, one should eat foods that are not incompatible, as follows:

children.text: āmreṣṭā [amleṣv ā]malakaṃ pathyaṃ śarkarā madhureṣu ca // 36 //
children.translated_text: With sour [foods], <s>āmalaka</s> (emblic myrobalan) is wholesome; with sweet [foods], sugar. (36)

body.text: paṭolaḥ śāka [tikta] vargeṣu kaṭuke cārdrakaṃ bhajet [paceḥ] //
body.translated_text: Among vegetables [i.e., bitter foods], <s>paṭola</s> (pointed gourd) [is appropriate]; with pungent [foods], one should add fresh ginger;

body.text: kaṣāyeṣu yavaś caiva lavaṇeṣu ca saindhavam // 37 //
body.translated_text: with astringent [foods], barley; and with salty [foods], rock salt (<s>saindhava</s>). (37)
Thus ends the section on milk (<s>kṣīravarga</s>) in the <s>Āyurvedamahodadhi</s> composed by <s>Suṣeṇa</s>.
Now, the qualities of cow's yogurt:

children.translated_text: Moreover, it is exceedingly cooling, stimulates digestion, and promotes strength;

children.text: vātaghnaṃ madhuraṃ rūkṣaṃ dadhi gavyaṃ manoharam // 38 //
children.translated_text: cow's yogurt is <s>vāta</s>-destroying, sweet, dry, and delightful. (38)
Unctuous, sweet in post-digestive effect, it stimulates digestion and promotes strength;

children.text: vātāpahaṃ pavitraṃ ca dadhi gavyaṃ rucipradam // 39 //
children.translated_text: cow's yogurt removes <s>vāta</s>, is purifying, and promotes appetite. (39)
In loss of appetite, in rhinitis, in urinary difficulty, in cold fever, in irregular fever,

children.text: durnāmarogagrahaṇīgade ca gavyaṃ praśastaṃ dadhi sarvadaiva // 40 //
children.translated_text: in hemorrhoids, in <s>grahaṇī</s> (chronic diarrhea) — cow's yogurt is always recommended. (40)

body.translated_text: Now, the merits and demerits of yogurt use according to season:

children.translated_text: In autumn, summer, and spring, yogurt is condemned and causes disorders;

children.text: hemante śiśire tac ca varṣākāle phalapradam // 41 //
children.translated_text: but in winter, the cold season, and the rainy season, it yields [beneficial] results. (41)

body.translated_text: Now, the qualities of buffalo yogurt:

children.translated_text: Sweet in post-digestive effect, aphrodisiac, it purifies blood and <s>pitta</s>;
buffalo yogurt especially promotes mucus. (42)
Unctuous, sweet, and cooling, it is supreme for promoting strength and complexion;
aphrodisiac, fat-producing, pleasant-tasting, fatigue-removing, and <s>vāta</s>-destroying. (43)
It promotes phlegm and undigested matter, and is nourishing with abundant juices;
purifying, heat-alleviating — buffalo yogurt promotes radiance. (44)

children.text: māhiṣaṃ dadhi balāsakārakaṃ vāhnimāndyakaram āśu gurutvāt /
children.translated_text: Buffalo yogurt causes mucus, produces sluggishness of digestive fire due to its heaviness;

children.text: tat prayojya kaṭukair avacūrṇe māhiṣaṃ ca laghutām upayāti // 45 //
children.translated_text: when mixed with pungent powders, buffalo yogurt becomes light. (45)

body.translated_text: Buffalo yogurt.
Now, the qualities of goat's yogurt:

children.translated_text: Goat's yogurt destroys <s>kapha</s> and <s>vāta</s>, removes <s>vāta</s>, is warming,

children.text: durnāmaśvasane ca kāsasahite cāgneś ca saṃdīpanam /
children.translated_text: stimulates digestive fire in difficult breathing accompanied by cough;
aphrodisiac, nourishing, giving digestive fire, radiance, and strength, destroying all diseases,

children.text: āsāṃśeṣva (rśaḥsv a)tisārake vigaditaṃ pathyaṃ sadā prāṇinām // 46 //
children.translated_text: it is always wholesome for living beings, indicated in hemorrhoids and chronic diarrhea. (46)
It removes cough and dyspnea, promotes appetite, destroys edema and chronic diarrhea;
fiery, it destroys all <s>doṣas</s> — goat's yogurt especially. (47)

body.translated_text: Now, the qualities of sheep's yogurt:

children.translated_text: Sheep's yogurt is unctuous, sweet, heavy, and productive of <s>pitta</s> and <s>kapha</s>;
it is wholesome in conditions of pure <s>vāta</s> and in edema caused by <s>vāta</s> and blood. (48)

body.translated_text: Now, the qualities of mare's yogurt:

children.text: vājijaṃ samadhuraṃ valavarṇaṃ svedadāham upayāti vināśam (gurutvam) /
children.translated_text: Mare's yogurt is slightly sweet, promotes strength and complexion; perspiration and burning are destroyed;

children.text: dīpanīyam atidoṣalaṃ sadā cākṣuṣaṃ ca marutaḥ pravikopi // 49 //
children.translated_text: it is digestive-stimulating, highly disorder-prone, always beneficial for the eyes, and aggravates <s>vāta</s>. (49)

body.translated_text: Now, the qualities of camel yogurt:

children.text: vātārśakuṣṭhakrimināśanaṃ syāt* auṣṭraṃ vipāke kaṭukaṃ satiktam /
children.translated_text: Camel yogurt destroys <s>vāta</s>, hemorrhoids, leprosy, and worms; it is pungent in post-digestive effect, with a bitter [taste];

children.text: sakṣāram amlaṃ kaṭu kuṣṭhakopi (kṛmikoṣṭhanāśanaṃ) balyaṃ ca saṃtarpaṇam āśu kāri // 50 //
children.translated_text: alkaline, sour, pungent, destroying worms and intestinal [disorders], strengthening, and quickly nourishing. (50)

body.translated_text: Now, the qualities of elephant's yogurt:

body.text: guru coṣṇaṃ kaṣāyaṃ ca kaphamūtrāpahaṃ ca tat /
body.translated_text: Heavy, hot, astringent — it removes <s>kapha</s> and urinary [disorders].
Now, the qualities of woman's yogurt:

body.text: snigdhaṃ vipāke madhuraṃ balyaṃ saṃtarpaṇaṃ guru // 51 //
body.translated_text: Unctuous, sweet in post-digestive effect, strengthening, nourishing, and heavy. (51)
Beneficial for the eyes, destroying all <s>doṣas</s> — woman's yogurt is of the highest quality. (52)

children.translated_text: Light in digestion, destroying phlegm, hot in potency, destroying <s>pitta</s>;
woman's yogurt, with an astringent secondary taste, promotes fecal matter. (53)

children.text: satukṣīreṇa vañjātaṃ guruvad dadhi tat smṛtam ///54 //
children.translated_text: yogurt produced from boiled milk is considered heavy. (54)

body.translated_text: One should develop a taste for yogurt mixed with whey;

body.text:
(dadhnas tu yad adhas toyaṃ tan mastuni pariśṛtaṃ /
śṛtāt kṣīrāc ca yañjātaṃ guṇavad dadhi tat smṛtam /)
vātapittaharaṃ rucyaṃ dhātvagnibalavardhanam /
body.translated_text: (That water which is below the yogurt, mixed with whey, and that which is produced from boiled milk — that yogurt is considered to have good qualities.) It removes <s>vāta</s> and <s>pitta</s>, promotes appetite, and increases tissue-fire and strength.
Now, the qualities of yogurt-sugar preparation (<s>dadhikhaṇḍa</s>):

children.text: daghnaḥ khaṇḍo gurur vṛṣyo vijñeyo balavardhanaḥ /
children.translated_text: Yogurt-sugar is heavy, aphrodisiac, known to promote strength;
when strained through cloth, it destroys <s>kapha</s> and <s>pitta</s>. (55)
Now, the qualities of thin (fat-free) yogurt:

children.text: dadhi tv asāraṃ rūkṣaṃ ca grāhi viḍbhedi (viṣṭambhi) vātalam /
children.translated_text: Thin yogurt is dry, astringent, constipating, and <s>vāta</s>-promoting;
digestive-stimulating, very light, slightly astringent, and appetite-promoting. (56)

body.translated_text: Now, the qualities of whey (<s>mastu</s>):
Whey removes thirst and fatigue, [is cooling,] and purifies the channels;
sour, astringent, and sweet; non-aphrodisiac; it removes <s>kapha</s> and <s>vāta</s>. (57)
Now, the general qualities of yogurt:

children.text: amlaṃ syād rasapākato gurutaraṃ vātāpahaṃ śītalaṃ
children.translated_text: Sour in taste and post-digestive effect, very heavy, it removes <s>vāta</s>, is cooling,
astringent and hot, indicated in <s>grahaṇī</s> (chronic diarrhea), removes urinary and fecal difficulties;
strengthening, producing edema, <s>kapha</s>, and sluggishness of fire, increasing blood, giving [satisfaction when] eaten;
in cough, dryness, loss of appetite, rhinitis, irregular fever, and cold fever — it is full [of benefit]
In <s>grahaṇī</s> (chronic diarrhea), rhinitis, urinary difficulty, and irregular fever,

children.text: arocake ca mandāgnau śasyate dadhi sarvadā // 59 //
children.translated_text: in loss of appetite and sluggish digestion — yogurt is always recommended. (59)
One should never eat yogurt without salt, pepper, ghee, sugar, green gram, <s>dhātrī</s> (āmalaka), or flower-juice;

children.text: na ca śaradi vasante noṣṇakāle na rātrau na dadhi kaphavikāre [pitta] pītaroge na dadyāt // 6 //
children.translated_text: not in autumn, spring, or the hot season, not at night; yogurt should not be given in <s>kapha</s> disorders or <s>pitta</s>-blood diseases. (60)
With cardamom, rock salt, sugar, black pepper, <s>dhātrī</s> (āmalaka), jaggery, and ghee,
yogurt is wholesome, especially when consumed with green gram soup;

children.text: naivoṣṇaṃ bahu picchalaṃ na ca śaradgrīṣme vasante hitaṃ
children.translated_text: never [drink it] hot, in large quantities, or slimy; nor is it beneficial in autumn, summer, or spring; it causes <s>pitta</s>-blood, fever, skin disease, vertigo, and is productive of erysipelas and other [disorders]. (61)
(Otherwise)
removes <s>kapha</s>, destroys <s>vāta</s>, and kindles the digestive fire;
it should be consumed in the cold and winter seasons as wholesome;
one becomes of firm body, beautiful form, and good constitution. (62)

body.translated_text: Yogurt mixed with <s>trikaṭuka</s> (three pungents) or with mustard seed powder

children.translated_text: Yogurt with jaggery, pleasantly warm, properly [strained] through washed cloth —
Strained and smoked by the playful hands of young women,
mixed with <s>śiśirakiraṇa</s> (camphor), <s>viśvā</s> (dry ginger), <s>jājī</s> (jasmine), and <s>cūrṇa</s> (powder),
it removes <s>kapha</s> (phlegm), destroys <s>vāta</s> (wind), and kindles the digestive fire.

body.translated_text: (It produces bodily firmness and radiance in people.)

children.translated_text: It should be consumed as wholesome during the cold and cool seasons;
one becomes purified in body, handsome, and endowed with vitality.

body.translated_text: Served with great elegance and well-churned. // 63 //

children.translated_text: <s>Dadhi</s> (curd) when fresh is unwholesome, but when combined with wholesome substances,
it is strength-giving, exceedingly potent, and promotes fat and appetite.
It removes <s>kapha</s> (phlegm) in conditions of <s>vāta</s> (wind) and does not excessively aggravate <s>pitta</s> (bile);

children.text: tad aniśam iha sevyaṃ mādhuraṃ cāmlabhāvāt // 64 //
children.translated_text: therefore it should always be consumed as sweet, due to its sour nature. // 64 //

children.text: madhuraṃ bhakṣayec caitad atyamlaṃ varjayet sadā /
children.translated_text: One should eat it sweet; one should always avoid it when excessively sour.
Sweet curd destroys diseases; excessively sour curd causes diseases. // 65 //

body.translated_text: Thus ends the section on curd (<s>dadhivarga</s>) in the <s>Āyurvedamahodadhi</s> composed by <s>Suṣeṇa</s>.
Now the properties of <s>mastu</s> (whey) are described.
It purifies the <s>srotas</s> (channels), stimulates taste, and quickly kindles the digestive fire;

body.text: śrotaḥ śuddiṃ vidhatte prakaṭayati ruciṃ dīpayaty āśu vahniṃ

children.text: kṛtvā śuddhiṃ malānāṃ jarayati ca haṭhād bhuktam annaṃ vicitram
children.translated_text: having purified the waste products, it digests with ease the various food that has been eaten.

children.text: uṣṇaṃ cāmlaṃ kaṣāyaṃ laghu surabhirasaṃ śūlaviṣṭambhahāri
children.translated_text: It is hot, sour, astringent, light, and of pleasant taste, and it removes <s>śūla</s> (colic) and <s>viṣṭambha</s> (constipation).
The best and most excellent <s>mastu</s> (whey) is beneficial in conditions of <s>kapha</s> (phlegm), <s>vāta</s> (wind), pain, and urinary retention. // 1 //

children.text: laghv anne rucipaktidaṃ klamaharaṃ balyaṃ kaṣāyaṃ saraṃ
children.translated_text: Light, it promotes appetite and digestion, removes fatigue, is strengthening, astringent, and laxative;
it creates desire for food, removes thirst and abdominal distension, and alleviates <s>plīhā</s> (splenic disease), <s>arśas</s> (hemorrhoids), and <s>śopha</s> (swelling).
After vomiting it purifies, removes <s>kapha</s> (phlegm) and <s>vāta</s> (wind), and alleviates constipation and colic;
in <s>pāṇḍu</s> (anemia) it pacifies urinary disorders, <s>gulma</s> (abdominal tumors), and pain—<s>mastu</s> (whey) is excellent and light. // 2 //
Due to its lightness, its appetizing quality, and its ability to destroy constipation and flatulence,
and due to its capacity to purify the channels, curd is surpassed by <s>tākra</s> (buttermilk). // 3 //

body.translated_text: Thus ends the section on <s>mastu</s> (whey) in the <s>Āyurvedamahodadhi</s>.
Now the properties of <s>takra</s> (buttermilk) are described.

body.text: gholaṃ mathitam udaśvittakraṃ caitac caturvidhaṃ kathitam //
body.translated_text: <s>Ghola</s>, <s>mathita</s>, <s>udaśvit</s>, and <s>takra</s>—these are said to be of four kinds.

children.text: sarasaṃ nirjalaṃ svādu kī(ya)d ambhovarjitaṃ mathitam /
children.translated_text: That which contains its own liquid and is without added water is sweet; <s>mathita</s> (churned) is that from which some water has been removed;
The first is with its own liquid and without water; <s>mathita</s> is that from which the liquid has been extracted and water removed.
<s>Udaśvit</s> is that with one-quarter water added; <s>takra</s> is said to have half water.

children.text: pādasalilam udaśvittad ardha[pāda]jalaṃ takram āhuś ca //

body.text: pratyekaṃ ca caturṇāṃ kathā jñeyāḥ prayatnena // 2 //
body.translated_text: The descriptions of each of the four kinds should be known with care. // 2 //

children.translated_text: That with its own liquid and without added water is known as <s>ghola</s>; <s>mathita</s> is that without liquid;
<s>udaśvit</s> has one-quarter water; <s>takra</s> has half water. // 3 //

body.translated_text: Now the properties of <s>takra</s> (buttermilk) from cow, buffalo, and goat.

children.text: gavyaṃ tu dīpanaṃ takraṃ medhyamarśas tridoṣajit /
children.translated_text: Cow's <s>takra</s> (buttermilk) kindles the digestive fire, promotes intellect, is useful in hemorrhoids, and conquers all three <s>doṣas</s> (humors).
Buffalo's <s>takra</s> produces <s>śleṣma</s> (phlegm); goat's is light and removes all three <s>doṣas</s>. // 4 //

body.translated_text: It destroys <s>gulma</s> (abdominal tumors), <s>arśas</s> (hemorrhoids), <s>grahaṇī</s> (malabsorption), <s>śopha</s> (swelling), <s>pāṇḍu</s> (anemia), and disorders of <s>vāta</s> (wind).
Now the properties of the different types of <s>takra</s> (buttermilk).

body.text:
gholaṃ mārutapittahāri māthitaṃ śvāsāpahaṃ śleṣmahṛt
pittaśleṣmavināśyudaśvidadhikaṃ takraṃ tridoṣāpahaṃ //
body.translated_text:
<s>Ghola</s> removes <s>vāta</s> (wind) and <s>pitta</s> (bile); <s>māthita</s> alleviates <s>śvāsa</s> (dyspnea) and removes <s>śleṣma</s> (phlegm);
<s>udaśvit</s> destroys <s>pitta</s> and <s>śleṣma</s>; <s>takra</s> removes all three <s>doṣas</s>.

body.text: mandāgnāv arucau tathaiva nitarām anyeṣu rogeṣv api

children.text: śreṣṭhaṃ takram idaṃ vadanti munayas tenottamaṃ prāṇinām // 6 //
children.translated_text: the sages declare this <s>takra</s> (buttermilk) to be the best and most excellent for living beings. // 6 //

body.translated_text: In cases of weak digestion, loss of appetite, and indeed in other diseases as well,
Now the praise of <s>takra</s> (buttermilk).

children.text: yathā surāṇām amṛtaṃ pradhānaṃ tathā narāṇāṃ bhuvi takram āhuḥ /
children.translated_text: Just as <s>amṛta</s> (nectar) is supreme among the gods, so is <s>takra</s> (buttermilk) declared to be for humans on earth.

children.text: amlena vātaṃ madhureṇa pittaṃ kaphaṃ kaṣāyeṇa nihanti sadyaḥ // 7 //
children.translated_text: By its sourness it destroys <s>vāta</s> (wind), by its sweetness <s>pitta</s> (bile), and by its astringency it instantly destroys <s>kapha</s> (phlegm). // 7 //
It destroys <s>vāta</s> (wind) and <s>śleṣma</s> (phlegm), removes worms, and breaks up <s>kṛcchra</s> (dysuria) and stones;
it removes urinary obstruction, pacifies <s>prameha</s> (urinary diseases), and alleviates <s>plīhā</s> (splenic disease), pain, and <s>gulma</s> (abdominal tumors).
It removes the severe suffering caused by <s>durṇāma</s> (duodenal disease), abdominal disorders, <s>pāṇḍu</s> (anemia), diseases, and <s>jaṭhara</s> (ascites);

children.text: takraṃ dīpanapācanaṃ laghutaraṃ pathyaṃ sadā prāṇinām // 8 //
children.translated_text: <s>takra</s> (buttermilk) kindles digestion, is a digestive, extremely light, and always wholesome for living beings. // 8 //

children.text: āmātisāre ca viśā [ṣṛ] cikāyāṃ vātajvare pāṇḍuṣu kāmaleṣu /
children.translated_text: In <s>āmātisāra</s> (dysentery with undigested matter), in <s>viṣama</s> (irregular) and other fevers, in <s>vātajvara</s> (fever caused by wind), in <s>pāṇḍu</s> (anemia), in <s>kāmalā</s> (jaundice),

children.text: pramehagulmodaravātaśūle nityaṃ pibet takram arocake ca // 9 //
children.translated_text: in <s>prameha</s> (urinary diseases), <s>gulma</s> (abdominal tumors), <s>udara</s> (abdominal diseases), <s>vātaśūla</s> (wind-colic), and <s>arocaka</s> (loss of appetite), one should always drink <s>takra</s> (buttermilk). // 9 //

children.text: takraṃ svādu kaṣāyam amlakarasaṃ bhakṣaṃ (kṣyaṃ) laghūṣṇaṃ hitaṃ
children.translated_text: <s>Takra</s> (buttermilk) is sweet, astringent, and sour in taste; it is digestible, light, hot, and beneficial;
it pacifies <s>gulma</s> (abdominal tumors), <s>arśas</s> (hemorrhoids), <s>pariṇāmaśūla</s> (colic during digestion), and removes <s>chardi</s> (vomiting) and <s>praseka</s> (excessive salivation).
It overcomes thirst, <s>arocaka</s> (loss of appetite), <s>meha</s> (urinary diseases), <s>śopha</s> (swelling), and <s>gara</s> (poisoning), and destroys <s>śleṣma</s> (phlegm) and lethargy;
it should be consumed as it removes urinary disorders, destroys fever, and alleviates pain arising from oleation therapy. // 10 //
In cold seasons, in <s>agnimāndya</s> (weak digestive fire), in <s>kāmalā</s> (jaundice) caused by <s>kapha</s> (phlegm),

children.text: mārgāvarodhe duṣṭau ca vāgnau (yau) takraṃ praśasyate // 11 //
children.translated_text: in obstruction of passages, in impaired digestion, and in disorders of speech, <s>takra</s> (buttermilk) is recommended. // 11 //
However, sweet buttermilk is indeed the foremost aggravator of <s>śleṣma</s> (phlegm);

children.text: vātaghnaṃ pittaśamanaṃ amlaṃ cet pittakṛt sadā // 12 //
children.translated_text: it removes <s>vāta</s> (wind) and pacifies <s>pitta</s> (bile), but if sour, it always aggravates <s>pitta</s>. // 12 //

body.translated_text: The method of specific buttermilk for specific <s>doṣas</s> (humors).

children.translated_text: For <s>vāta</s> (wind), sour buttermilk with <s>saindhava</s> (rock salt); for <s>pitta</s> (bile), sweet with sugar;
for <s>kapha</s> (phlegm) and <s>pitta</s>, or for <s>kapha</s> alone, one should drink buttermilk mixed with <s>vyoṣa</s> (the three pungents) and alkaline substances. // 13 //

children.text: sthaulyaṃ karoti harate nilam etad eva
children.translated_text: This very substance causes corpulence and removes <s>nīla</s> (discoloration)—

children.text: yan noṣṇatām apagataṃ na kadācid eva /
children.translated_text: its warmth never departs at any time.
Combined with ghee, sugar, <s>madhuka</s> (licorice), <s>mudga</s> (green gram), and astringent substances,
it should be consumed avoiding the seasons of spring and autumn. // 14 //
The wise say that buttermilk churned at the stage of extracting butter
when churned for a long time, produces <s>doṣas</s> (humors) in a person. // 15 //

body.translated_text: Prohibitions regarding <s>takra</s> (buttermilk) in specific diseases.

children.text: naiva takraṃ kṣate dadyān noṣmakāle na durbale /
children.translated_text: One should never give buttermilk in cases of wasting, in hot seasons, or to the weak;
not in fainting, vertigo, or burning sensations, nor in diseases of blood and <s>pitta</s> (bile). // 16 //

body.translated_text: Praise of <s>takra</s> (buttermilk).

children.translated_text: Radiant as the moon and <s>kunda</s> (jasmine) flowers, resembling a conch shell, churned pure by the hands of young women,

children.text: paripakvasugandhikapittharasaṃ piba bho nṛpa takraṃ rujāpaharam // 17 //
children.translated_text: with the fragrance of ripe <s>kapittha</s> (wood-apple) juice—drink, O king, this <s>takra</s> (buttermilk) that removes all ailments! // 17 //
<s>Mathita</s> (churned), <s>gorasa</s> (milk product), <s>ghola</s>, mixed with liquid whey,
white, struck with a churning rod, thick—these are its various names. // 18 //
With twice the amount of water and white, this is known as <s>ardhodaka</s> (half-water);

children.text: takraṃ tribhāgabhinnaṃ tu kevalaṃ mathitaṃ smṛtam // 19 //
children.translated_text: <s>takra</s> (buttermilk) divided into three parts is known as plain <s>mathita</s> (churned). // 19 //
The water that floats above the buttermilk is called <s>udaśvit</s>;

children.text: dadhnas tūpari yat toyaṃ tan mastu parikīrtitam // 20 //
children.translated_text: the water that rises above the curd is called <s>mastu</s> (whey). // 20 //
<s>Takūrjakā</s> (a preparation) is binding, aggravates <s>vāta</s> (wind), is drying, and difficult to digest;
<s>maṇḍa</s> (thin gruel) is lighter than buttermilk; <s>kūcikā</s> is like curd-buttermilk. // 21 //
Buttermilk made without a ritual becomes like a sacrifice through its sacrificial quality;

children.text: tasmāt triviṣṭape jātaṃ takraṃ śakrasya durlabham // 22 //
children.translated_text: therefore, buttermilk produced in the three worlds is rare even for <s>Śakra</s> (Indra). // 22 //

children.text: kailāse yadi takram asti giriśaḥ kiṃ nīlaṇṭho bhavet
children.translated_text: If there were buttermilk on <s>Kailāsa</s>, would <s>Giriśa</s> (Śiva) have a blue throat?

children.text: vaikuṇṭhe yadi kṛṣṇatām anubhaved adyāpi kiṃ keśavaḥ /
children.translated_text: If <s>Keśava</s> (Viṣṇu) experienced it in <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s>, would he still have dark complexion?

children.text: indro durbhagatābhayād vijayati (tāṃ kṣayaṃ dvijapatiḥ) lambodaratvaṃ gaṇaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Indra</s> triumphs over the fear of misfortune; <s>Gaṇeśa</s> has his pot-belly;

children.text: kuṣṭhitvaṃ ca kuberako dahanatām agniś ca divyasti cet // 23 //
children.translated_text: <s>Kubera</s> has his ugliness and <s>Agni</s> (fire) his burning nature—if only there were this divine buttermilk! // 23 //

children.text: yad dravyaṃ śaṅkhavarṇaṃ himapaṭalanibhaṃ cārugandhaḥ suśītaṃ
children.translated_text: That substance which is conch-white, resembling a sheet of snow, of beautiful fragrance and pleasantly cool,
bright as the waters of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, churned to froth by the vigorous hands of young women,
pervaded by the churning rod, with foam like bubbles from the force of the palms,

children.text: tat takraṃ sūpadhūpaṃ tv amṛtaguṇanibhaṃ bhāgyavantaḥ pibanti // 24 //
children.translated_text: that buttermilk, well-perfumed, possessing qualities like <s>amṛta</s> (nectar)—the fortunate ones drink it. // 24 //

body.translated_text: Thus ends the section on <s>takra</s> (buttermilk) in the <s>Āyurvedamahodadhi</s> composed by <s>Suṣeṇa</s>.
Now the section on <s>navanīta</s> (fresh butter) is described.

body.text:
śītaṃ varṇabalapradaṃ samadhuraṃ vṛṣyaṃ ca saṃgrāhakaṃ
vātaghnaṃ kapha (kā)hārakaṃ rucikaraṃ hṛdyaṃ tridoṣāpaham (sarvāṅgaśūlāpaham) /
kāsādhvaśramaśāntidaṃ ratikaraṃ kāntipradaṃ puṣṭidaṃ

children.translated_text: {cf. <s>Rājanighaṇṭu</s> 15.63: it destroys cough and removes fatigue}

children.text: sadyaskaṃ navanītam uddhṛtam idaṃ syāt sarvarogāpaham /
children.translated_text: Freshly prepared <s>navanīta</s> (butter) extracted just now removes all diseases.

children.text: (cakṣuṣyaṃ navanītam uddhṛtanavaṃ goḥ sarvadoṣāpaham) cf. Rājanighaṇṭu 15.63} //
children.translated_text: (Freshly extracted new cow's butter is beneficial for the eyes and removes all <s>doṣas</s>) {cf. <s>Rājanighaṇṭu</s> 15.63}

children.text: śītaṃ balāḍharyaṃ madhurāmlavṛṣyaṃ śleṣmā (va) pahaṃ pittamarutpraṇāśam /
children.translated_text: It is cooling, strength-giving, sweet, sour, <s>vṛṣya</s> (aphrodisiac), removes <s>śleṣma</s> (phlegm), and pacifies <s>pitta</s> and <s>vāta</s>;
it relieves grief, wasting, and emaciation—<s>navanīta</s> (butter) when warm is wholesome for the elderly and children. // 2 //

children.text: gavyaṃ vā māhiṣaṃ vāpi navanītaṃ navoddhṛtam /
