children.translated_text: Whether from cow or buffalo, freshly extracted <s>navanīta</s> (butter)
is recommended for children and the elderly as it increases strength, nourishment, and <s>dhātus</s> (bodily tissues). // 3 //

children.text: śītaṃ varṇabalapradaṃ samadhuraṃ vṛṣyaṃ hi saṃgrāhakaṃ
children.translated_text: It is cooling, bestows complexion and strength, is sweet, <s>vṛṣya</s> (aphrodisiac), and binding;
it is <s>hṛdya</s> (cardiac tonic), removes <s>śvāsa</s> (dyspnea) and aging, destroys wasting, and alleviates <s>pitta</s>, sourness, and <s>vāta</s>.
It pacifies cough, hemorrhoids, fatigue, and swelling, and removes prolapse and pain in the limbs;
freshly prepared buffalo <s>navanīta</s> (butter) removes all diseases. // 4 //

body.translated_text: Thus end the properties of <s>navanīta</s> (butter).
Now the properties of <s>ghṛta</s> (ghee) are described.
First, the properties of cow's <s>ghṛta</s> (ghee).

body.text:
dhīkāntismṛtikārakaṃ balakaraṃ medhāpradaṃ buddhikṛt
vātaghnaṃ śramanāśanaṃ svarakaraṃ pittāpahaṃ puṣṭidam /
body.translated_text:
It promotes intellect, radiance, memory, and strength; it bestows <s>medhā</s> (intelligence), creates wisdom;
it removes <s>vāta</s> (wind), destroys fatigue, improves the voice, and alleviates <s>pitta</s> (bile); it is nourishing.

body.text: vahner vṛddhiharaṃ vipākamadhuraṃ vṛṣyaṃ ca śītaṃ sadā
body.translated_text: It increases the digestive fire, is sweet in post-digestive effect, <s>vṛṣya</s> (aphrodisiac), and always cooling;

body.text: sevyaṃ gavyam idaṃ ghṛtaṃ balakaraṃ sadyaḥsamāvartitam // 1 //
body.translated_text: this cow's <s>ghṛta</s> (ghee) should be consumed as it gives strength and is freshly prepared. // 1 //

body.text:
sarpirgavāṃ cāmṛtakaṃ viṣaghnaṃ cākṣuṣyam ārogyakaraṃ ca vṛṣyam /
rasāyanaṃ mandam atīva medhyaṃ snehottama ca (goḥ) vibudhā vadanti
body.translated_text:
Cow's ghee is like <s>amṛta</s> (nectar), destroys poison, is beneficial for the eyes, promotes health, and is <s>vṛṣya</s> (aphrodisiac);
it is a <s>rasāyana</s> (rejuvenative), mild, exceedingly beneficial for intellect—the wise declare it the best among all unctuous substances.
Now the properties of buffalo <s>ghṛta</s> (ghee).

children.translated_text: Buffalo ghee is excellent, promotes firmness, bestows happiness and radiance,
it destroys <s>vāta</s> (wind) and <s>śleṣma</s> (phlegm), gives strength, and promotes clarity of complexion.
It pacifies <s>durṇāma</s> (duodenal disease), <s>grahaṇī</s> (malabsorption) disorders, and kindles weak digestive fire. {cf. <s>Rājanighaṇṭu</s> 15.78}

children.text: cākṣuṣya navagavyataḥ phala (para)m idaṃ hṛdyaṃ manohāri ca // 3 //
children.translated_text: It is beneficial for the eyes; this product of fresh cow's milk is <s>hṛdya</s> (cardiac tonic) and delightful. // 3 //

children.text: māhiṣyaṃ tan mānuṣaṇāṃ ca śastaṃ balyaṃ vṛṣyaṃ bastisādaṃ karoti /
children.translated_text: Buffalo ghee is recommended for humans as it is strengthening, <s>vṛṣya</s> (aphrodisiac), and causes relaxation of the bladder;

children.text: medodbhūtaṃ mehakṛcchaityakāri tasmān nityaṃ sarvakālaṃ niṣevyam //
children.translated_text: it produces fat, causes <s>meha</s> (urinary disorders) and cold sensations—therefore it should always be consumed at all times.

body.translated_text: Properties of goat's <s>ghṛta</s> (ghee).

children.translated_text: Goat's ghee kindles the digestive fire, is beneficial for the eyes, and increases strength;

children.text: kāsaśvāsakṣaye vāpi pathyaṃ pāneṣu tal laghu //
children.translated_text: it is wholesome in <s>kāsa</s> (cough), <s>śvāsa</s> (dyspnea), and <s>kṣaya</s> (wasting); it is light when used as a drink.

body.translated_text: Properties of sheep's <s>ghṛta</s> (ghee).

body.text: āvikaṃ ghṛtam atīvā gurutvād varjyam eva sukumāranaraiś ca /
body.translated_text: Sheep's ghee, being extremely heavy, should be avoided by those of delicate constitution.
Properties of camel's <s>ghṛta</s> (ghee).

body.text: sadya eṣa balapuṣṭikaraṃ syād uṣṭrajaṃ śvayathukāsakaraṃ ca //
body.translated_text: Camel's ghee immediately gives strength and nourishment, but causes <s>śvayathu</s> (edema) and <s>kāsa</s> (cough).
And furthermore,

children.translated_text: Cow's ghee when cooked removes the effects of emesis and destroys <s>kapha</s> (phlegm);
sheep's and goat's and donkey's ghee have properties similar to their respective milks. // 7 //
Camel's ghee is pungent in potency, and removes <s>śleṣma</s> (phlegm), worms, and poison;
it kindles digestion, destroys <s>kapha</s> (phlegm) and <s>vāta</s> (wind), and alleviates <s>kuṣṭha</s> (skin diseases), <s>gulma</s> (abdominal tumors), and abdominal disorders. // 8 //

children.text: pāke laghvādi (vi)kaṃ sarpiḥ na ca pittaprakopanam /
children.translated_text: In digestion, ghee becomes light and does not aggravate <s>pitta</s> (bile);

children.text: kaphe 'nile yonidoṣe ca śvayathau hatam (śophe kampe ca tad dhitam) // 9 //
children.translated_text: in <s>kapha</s> (phlegm), <s>vāta</s> (wind), uterine disorders, and swelling, it is beneficial (also useful in edema and tremors). // 9 //

children.text: pāke laghuṣṭaṃ (ghūṣṇaṃ) vīrye ca kaṣāyaṃ kaphanāśanam /
children.translated_text: In digestion it is light, hot in potency, astringent, and destroys <s>kapha</s> (phlegm);

children.text: dīpanī (naṃ) laghu vīrye ca vidyād aikaśaphaṃ ghṛtam // 10 //
children.translated_text: one should know that ghee from single-hoofed animals is light and appetizing in potency. // 10 //

body.translated_text: Woman's ghee (<s>strīghṛta</s>).

children.text: cakṣuṣyam agnidaṃ strīṇāṃ sarpiḥ syād atamṛopamam [sic!] /
children.translated_text: Woman's ghee is beneficial for the eyes, kindles the digestive fire, and is incomparable in its effects;

children.text: vṛddhiṃ karoti dehāgner laghu pāke viṣāpaham // 11 //
children.translated_text: it increases the bodily fire, is light in digestion, and removes poison. // 11 //

body.translated_text: Elephant cow's ghee (<s>hastinīghṛta</s>).

children.translated_text: It is astringent, binds urine, is bitter, kindles digestion, and is light;
elephant's ghee destroys astringent substances, worms, and poisonous conditions (also destroys <s>kapha</s>, <s>kuṣṭha</s>, poison, and worms). // 12 //

body.translated_text: Praise of ghee (<s>sarpiḥpraśaṃsā</s>).

children.text: āyurvṛddhiṃ vapur api dṛḍhaṃ saukumāryaṃ karoti
children.translated_text: It increases longevity, makes the body firm, and promotes delicacy;
it is the remedy for exhaustion caused by exercise, sexual activity, and fatigue.

children.text: pathyaṃ bālye vayasi taruṇe vārdhake cāpi pathyaṃ
children.translated_text: It is wholesome in childhood, in youth, and also in old age;

children.text: nānyat kiñcid bhavati puruṣe sarpiṣaḥ sthaulyakāri // 13 //
children.translated_text: nothing else in a person causes corpulence like ghee. // 13 //

children.text: yad vedāgamavedibhir nigaditaṃ sākṣād ihāyur nṛṇāṃ
children.translated_text: That which is proclaimed by the knowers of the <s>Vedas</s> and <s>Āgamas</s> as directly promoting longevity among people,

children.text: yad vaidyais tu rasāyanāya kathitaṃ sadyo jarānāśanam /
children.translated_text: that which physicians have declared as a <s>rasāyana</s> (rejuvenative), instantly destroying old age,
that which is spoken of by the intelligent as possessing the beauty of the <s>Sārasvata</s> preparation for the attainment of wisdom—
that is ghee, which shines with the radiance of the <s>ketaka</s> (screw-pine) flower and should be taken with delight. // 14 //

children.text: vīryātiśītaṃ ca guṇe vipāke svādu tridoṣeṣu rasāyanaṃ ca /
children.translated_text: It is exceedingly cool in potency, sweet in post-digestive effect, and is a <s>rasāyana</s> (rejuvenative) for all three <s>doṣas</s> (humors).

children.text: tejobalāyuṣyakaraṃ ca medhyaṃ cākṣuṣyam etad ghṛtam āhur āryāḥ // 15 //
children.translated_text: The noble ones declare this <s>ghṛta</s> (clarified butter) to be promoter of vigor, strength, and longevity, beneficial for the intellect, and good for the eyes. (15)

children.text: ojastejobhivṛddhiṃ janayati sukhadaṃ kāntikṛt samyag uktaṃ
children.translated_text: It produces the increase of <s>ojas</s> (vital essence) and vigor, is happiness-giving, promotes radiance, and is rightly praised;
it destroys sin, misfortune, fatigue, and cures indigestion-born fever caused by breathing difficulties and coughing;

children.text: śūlodāvartarogagrahaṇini ca pajā (madarujaṃ) nāśayaty āśu pittaṃ [pīḍāṃ]
children.translated_text: it quickly destroys <s>śūla</s> (colic), <s>udāvarta</s> (upward movement of wind), diseases of the <s>grahaṇī</s> (bowels), and <s>pitta</s> (bile) affliction,

children.text: vātaghnaṃ pittanāśaṃ svarahati bhave śūddhame (svarakaram agadaṃ kṣudbhrame) caivasevye (vyam) // 16 //
children.translated_text: it destroys <s>vāta</s> (wind) and <s>pitta</s> (bile), benefits the voice, purifies, and is to be used in cases of hunger-dizziness. (16)

body.text:
cākṣuṣyaṃ vṛṣyam āyusmṛtidhṛtikaraṇaṃ rājayakṣmāprakopaṃ [vināśaṃ]
[rūkṣe kṣīṇe ca pathyaṃ valipalitaharaṃ sāmadoṣaprakope /]
bhūtonmādapramatte bahutimiramade kṛtpapaśrīra [syād apasmāra] hāri

children.text: sarveṣāṃ sarvadaiva prathitaguṇagaṇaṃ sādhu pathyaṃ ghṛtaṃ syāt // 17 //
children.translated_text: for everyone at all times, <s>ghṛta</s> (clarified butter) with its widely celebrated collection of qualities is an excellent and wholesome [substance]. (17)

body.translated_text: It is good for the eyes, aphrodisiac, promoter of longevity, memory, and steadfastness, and a destroyer of <s>rājayakṣmā</s> (consumption); it is wholesome when dry and depleted, removes wrinkles and grey hair, and in aggravation of the combined <s>doṣas</s>; in cases of demonic possession, madness, frenzy, and excessive eye disease, it removes epilepsy,

children.translated_text: Fresh [ghee] purifies worms [parasites] and cleanses the urinary bladder;
it is phlegm-producing, bile-destroying, and promotes strength and nourishment. (18)
Old [ghee] removes eye disease, asthma, nasal catarrh, fever, and cough;
it destroys fainting, leprosy, poison, intoxication, demonic possession, and epilepsy. (19)
Old <s>ghṛta</s> aged ten years has a strong smell;
it resembles lac-juice in color, is cooling, and removes [afflictions caused by] serpents and demonic seizure. (20)
Old [ghee] conquers diseases arising from intoxication, epilepsy, fainting, and those of the head, ears, eyes, and womb,
and it cleanses and heals wounds. (21)
It is especially recommended for those suffering from epilepsy, demonic seizure, and madness;

children.text: pūrvoktāś cādhikāṃs tāś ca [?] guṇās tad amṛtopamam // 22 //
children.translated_text: it possesses the previously stated qualities and more — it is like <s>amṛta</s> (nectar). (22)

children.text: nirāmayānāṃ navayauvanānāṃ kṛtvā gavāṃ yacchata dhautamaddhiḥ /
children.translated_text: From healthy, young cows, having taken the freshly washed butter,

children.text: vahnau vipakvaṃ navanītanūnaṃ [yogyaṃ] yogyaṃ ghṛtaṃ tad gajarājasevitām [?] // 23 //
children.translated_text: the <s>ghṛta</s> properly cooked over fire, thin as fresh butter — that ghee is fit to be used by an elephant-king. (23)

body.translated_text: Thus ends the section on <s>ghṛta</s> (clarified butter) in the <s>Āyurvedamahodadhi</s> composed by <s>Suṣeṇa</s>.
Now the properties of oils are described.

children.text: uṣṇaṃ vipāke kaṭukaṃ satiktaṃ kaphāpahaṃ vātanivāraṇaṃ ca /
children.translated_text: Oil is heating in its post-digestive effect, pungent with a bitter [taste], removes <s>kapha</s> (phlegm) and wards off <s>vāta</s> (wind);
it destroys worms, produces strength and appetite — oil destroys worms, phlegm, and wind disorders. (1)

body.text: tilatailam alaṃkaroti keśyaṃ madhuraṃ tiktakaṣāyam uṣṇatīkṣṇam /
body.translated_text: <s>Tilatailam</s> (sesame oil) adorns [the body], is good for the hair, sweet with bitter and astringent [tastes], hot and sharp;

body.text: balakṛtkaphavātajaṃ ca [jantu] kharjū vraṇakaṇḍūtiharaṃ ca [kānti] dāyi // 2 //
body.translated_text: it promotes strength, removes [afflictions] born of <s>kapha</s> and <s>vāta</s>, and cures scabies, wounds, and itching, and bestows radiance. (2)

children.text: kaṇḍūharaṃ kāntivivardhanaṃ ca arśo [varco] vivṛddhi vraṇaropaṇaṃ ca /
children.translated_text: It removes itching, increases radiance, heals piles and wounds,

children.text: tilasya jātaṃ khalu yac ca tailaṃ bāleṣu vṛddheṣv api taila [pathya]m etat // 3 //
children.translated_text: and that oil which is produced from sesame — it is wholesome for both children and the elderly. (3)

children.text: na pittaroge na ca śoṇitotthe pathyaṃ mahāvātavikārasaṃdhau /
children.translated_text: It is not wholesome in diseases of <s>pitta</s> (bile) or in those arising from blood disorders, [but is] wholesome in the conjunction of great <s>vāta</s> (wind) disorders;

children.text: tilodbhavaṃ tailam udaāharanti vātāśritān hanti samastadoṣān // 4 //
children.translated_text: sesame oil, they say, destroys all diseases dependent on <s>vāta</s>. (4)
Pungent, sour in potency, greatly <s>pitta</s>-producing, it causes retention of stool and urine, and produces excessive digestive fire;

children.text: pāmādidoṣāpaharaṃ ca tailaṃ abhyañjanaṃ sarṣapasaṃbhavaṃ ca // 5 //
children.translated_text: oil born of mustard seed removes skin diseases such as scabies and the like, and is used for external application. (5)
<s>Sārṣapa tailam</s> (mustard oil) is pungent and hot, removes <s>kapha</s>, semen, and <s>vāta</s>;

children.text: tīkṣṇoṣṇaṃ picchalaṃ visraṃ raktair aṇḍodbhavaṃ tv ati {cf. Aṣṭāṅgahṛdaya 5.58cd} // 6 //
children.translated_text: it is sharp, hot, slimy, and rank-smelling; that produced from eggs is very much of the blood [nature]. (6)
For the lordly elephants of <s>āmavāta</s> (rheumatism) that roam in the forest of the body,
the foremost and sole slayer is the lion of <s>eraṇḍa</s> (castor oil) unction. (8)
<s>Kausumbha tailam</s> (safflower oil) destroys worms
and promotes vigor and strength, [but] destroys the eyes;

children.text: kharjūś ca keśaś ca karoti koṣṭhe [kaṇḍūṃ ca karoti dṛṣṭeḥ]
children.translated_text: it causes scabies, hair [loss], and itching in the bowels,
yet it is a destroyer of the three <s>doṣas</s> and removes wind disorders. (9)
By the application of <s>karaṃja</s> (pongamia) oil, eye diseases are destroyed;
in leprosy and in those with broken skin, it removes all <s>vāta</s> disorders. (10)

children.text: ākṣaṃ svādu himaṃ keśyaṃ guru pittānilāpaham /
children.translated_text: <s>Ākṣa tailam</s> (oil of <s>vibhītaka</s> nuts) is sweet, cooling, good for the hair, heavy, and removes <s>pitta</s> and <s>vāta</s>;
neem oil is not excessively hot and removes worms, leprosy, and pain. (11)
Linseed oil is not good for the eyes, increases <s>pitta</s>, and destroys <s>vāta</s>;
oil from <s>vibhītaka</s> nuts destroys <s>kapha</s> and <s>pitta</s>, is good for the hair, and nourishes the eyes and ears. (12)

body.translated_text: Castor oil works on the lower body; for other [conditions] it is considered equal to sesame oil.
Thus ends the section on oils in the <s>Āyurvedamahodadhi</s> composed by <s>Suṣeṇa</s>.
Now the properties of honey are described.

children.translated_text: <s>Madhu</s> (honey) cleanses, binds, and heals wounds, and aggravates <s>vāta</s>;
it is dry, astringent, and sweet; <s>madhuśarkarā</s> (honey-sugar) has the same [properties]. (1)
Honey is said to destroy the three <s>doṣas</s>; [when combined] with another [substance], it [cures] <s>sannipāta</s> (derangement of all three humors);
it removes hiccups, asthma, phlegm, vomiting, intoxication, thirst, and poison. (2)

body.text: kṣaudraṃ jalena saṃyuktaṃ (ati) sthaulye piben naraḥ

children.text: kṛśo bhavati saty āha (prāhā) llekhanaṃ tatra jāyate // 3 //
children.translated_text: he becomes thin, it is said — a scraping effect is produced thereby. (3)

body.translated_text: <s>Kṣaudra</s> (a type of honey) mixed with water — a person with obesity should drink it;

children.text: lepe hitaṃ tatra gudāṅkurāṇāṃ gajoddhavaṃ lehyamahobhivṛddhiḥ (?) /
children.translated_text: Application of it is beneficial for hemorrhoidal growths; when licked, it wonderfully increases [health] from the elephant [type of honey];

children.text: sarvo guruś cāpi rasāyanānāṃ kāsāpaho vāpi madhuprayogaḥ // 4 //
children.translated_text: all [types], being heavy, are foremost among <s>rasāyanas</s> (rejuvenatives), and the use of honey also removes cough. (4)

children.text: mehe hitaṃ syān malachardināśaḥ hikkātisāre vraṇakuṣṭhahantā /
children.translated_text: It is beneficial in urinary diseases, destroys impurities and vomiting, cures hiccups and diarrhea, and destroys wounds and leprosy;
destroying itching and wounds, the use of honey is a divine nectar for those who are afflicted and whose digestive fire needs kindling. (5)

children.text: sthāvaraṃ jaṅgamaṃ vāpi kṛtrimaṃ ca viṣāpaham (viṣaṃ haret) /
children.translated_text: It removes poison — whether from stationary sources, moving creatures, or artificial [preparations];
freedom from wrinkles and grey hair is produced in the body [by its use]. (6)
It is beneficial in wasting and consumption, conquers jaundice,

children.text: sthūla kaṣṇo (?) hitaṃ caiva rakte vāpi hitaṃ ca tat // 7 //
children.translated_text: is beneficial for the corpulent, and also beneficial in blood disorders. (7)

children.text: pāke svādu madhu śreṣṭhaṃ vipāke doṣasaṃyutam /
children.translated_text: Honey that is sweet in digestion is excellent; in post-digestive effect, it is associated with the <s>doṣas</s>;
that honey is born from the intoxication of waters contained on earth. (8)
It causes the production of worms and insects; <s>pippalī</s> (long pepper) combined with honey,

children.text: amlena madhuraṃ svādu tan madhuś cāpi doṣakṛt) (?) // 9 //
children.translated_text: and honey that is sweet with a sour [substance] — that too produces faults. (9)

body.translated_text: Now the properties of sugarcane are described.

children.text: snigdhaś ca saṃtarpaṇabṛṃhaṇaś ca saṃjīvanaḥ svādurasaḥ śramaghnaṃ /
children.translated_text: Unctuous, nourishing, invigorating, of sweet taste, and fatigue-destroying,

children.text: vṛṣyaś ca pittaśramavātahārī hy antarvidāhī kaphakṛtsitekṣuḥ //
children.translated_text: aphrodisiac, and a remover of <s>pitta</s>, fatigue, and <s>vāta</s> — [but] causing internal burning and producing <s>kapha</s> — such is the white sugarcane.

children.text: tadvat sakṛṣṇo hi bhaved guṇaiś ca vṛṣyo bhavet tarpaṇadāhahantā /
children.translated_text: Likewise the dark variety possesses similar qualities: aphrodisiac, nourishing, and heat-destroying;
somewhat alkaline, sweet in taste, destroying dryness, and causing wound-swelling. (2)
<s>Pāṇḍuka</s>, <s>bhīruka</s>, <s>vārāha</s>, <s>śvetapotaka</s>,

children.text: kāntāras tāpasekṣuḥ syāt kāṣṭhekṣuś ca vicitrakaḥ // 3 //
children.translated_text: <s>kāntāra</s>, <s>tāpasekṣu</s>, <s>kāṣṭhekṣu</s>, and <s>vicitraka</s> — (3)

body.translated_text: <s>Nepāla</s>, <s>dīpyantra</s>, <s>nīlaya</s>, and <s>raupyakośakṛt</s> —

body.text: ity etā jātayaḥ sthūlā guṇān vakṣyāmy ataḥ param // 4 //
body.translated_text: these are the major varieties; I shall now describe their properties hereafter. (4)

children.text: avidāhi gurur vṛṣyaḥ pauṇḍrako bhīrukas tathā // 5 ///
children.translated_text: non-burning, heavy, and aphrodisiac — such are <s>pauṇḍraka</s> and <s>bhīruka</s>. (5)

body.translated_text: Very cooling, sweet, unctuous, nourishing, and increasing <s>kapha</s>,

children.text: anye tulyaguṇāḥ kecit sakṣāro vaṃśako mataḥ /
children.translated_text: Others have similar qualities; <s>vaṃśaka</s> is considered slightly alkaline;

children.text: vaṃśavacchvetapauṇḍras tu kiñcid uṣṇaḥ sa vātahā // 6 //
children.translated_text: <s>śvetapauṇḍra</s>, like <s>vaṃśaka</s>, is somewhat hot and removes <s>vāta</s>. (6)
<s>Kāntāra</s> and <s>tāpasekṣu</s> are considered to follow the properties of <s>vaṃśaka</s>;

children.text: evaṃguṇas tu kāṣṭhekṣuḥ sa tu vātaprakopanaḥ // 7 //
children.translated_text: <s>kāṣṭhekṣu</s> (woody sugarcane) has similar qualities but aggravates <s>vāta</s>. (7)
<s>Sūcīpatra</s>, <s>nīlāpa</s> (<s>nepāla</s>), and <s>dīrghapatraka</s> —
these destroy <s>vāta</s>, <s>kapha</s>, and <s>pitta</s>, are astringent, and cause [slight] burning. (8)
<s>Kośākara</s> — <s>guḍa</s> (jaggery) [from this variety] is cooling, and removes <s>raktapitta</s> (bleeding disorders) and consumption;

children.text: atīva madhuro mūlo (le) madhye madhura eva ca // 9 //
children.translated_text: the root is exceedingly sweet, the middle portion is sweet as well. (9)

children.text: agreṣu (ṣvā) madhuro jñeyaḥ ikṣur ālavaṇaḥ smṛtaḥ /
children.translated_text: The tips should be known as sweet; sugarcane is considered slightly saline;
it produces <s>kapha</s>, is non-burning, and subdues <s>raktapitta</s> (bleeding disorders). (10)
Sugarcane juice pressed by the teeth has potency equal to sugar;
that which is pressed by a machine is heavy, burning, and causes constipation. (11)
The cooked juice is heavy, unctuous, sharp, and removes <s>kapha</s> and <s>vāta</s>;

children.text: phāṇitaṃ guru madhuraṃ abhiṣyandi ca bṛṃhaṇam // 12 //
children.translated_text: <s>phāṇita</s> (inspissated sugarcane juice) is heavy, sweet, causes secretions, and is nourishing. (12)

body.text: śukraṃ kaphakaraṃ caiva pittaghnaṃ ca viśeṣataḥ /

children.translated_text: being alkaline, sweet, and greatly promoting urination, it purifies the blood,
controls fat, pacifies <s>pitta</s>, destroys <s>vāta</s>, and causes constipation;

children.text: śleṣmāṇaṃ jana(yet*) ca bṛṃhaṇakaro balyaḥ sadā svāsthyakṛt
children.translated_text: it produces <s>kapha</s>, is nourishing, strengthening, and always health-promoting,
destroys <s>vāta</s>, is of mixed [properties], pacifies <s>amlapitta</s> (acid bile), and is always to be taken in moderation. (13)

body.translated_text: It promotes semen, produces <s>kapha</s>, and especially destroys <s>pitta</s>;
Properties of <s>matsyaṇḍikā</s> (sugar preparations) and others:

children.translated_text: <s>Matsyaṇḍikā</s>, <s>khaṇḍa</s> (sugar candy), <s>śarkarā</s> (sugar) — purified, smooth, and polished;
heavy, and in successive stages of cooking becoming sweeter, aphrodisiac, and destroying <s>raktapitta</s> (bleeding disorders).
<s>Śarkarā</s> (sugar) is said to destroy all types of burning sensation,
it pacifies <s>raktapitta</s> (bleeding disorders) and removes vomiting, fainting, and thirst. (15)
<s>Phāṇita</s> (syrup) produced from <s>madhūka</s> flowers is dry, and produces <s>vāta</s> and <s>pitta</s>;
it destroys <s>kapha</s>, is sweet in digestion, and purifies the bladder in post-digestive effect. (16)
Equal to <s>guḍa</s> (jaggery) and <s>śarkarā</s> (sugar), it purifies the bladder and promotes digestion;
it pacifies <s>pitta</s> and subdues <s>raktapitta</s> (bleeding disorders). (17)
Sweet sugar also destroys hiccups and diarrhea;

children.text: rūkṣā vivchedanī caiva kaṣāyā madhurāpi ca // 18 //
children.translated_text: it is dry, separating, astringent, and yet sweet. (18)

body.translated_text: Praise of sugarcane and its varieties:

children.text: vṛṣyaḥ śītoṣṇapittaṃ śamayati madhuro bṛṃhaṇaḥ śleṣmakāri /
children.translated_text: Aphrodisiac, cooling, pacifying hot <s>pitta</s>, sweet, nourishing, and <s>kapha</s>-producing,

children.text: snigdho hṛdyassaraś ca śramaśamanapaṭur mūtraśuddhiṃ karoti /
children.translated_text: unctuous, pleasant to the heart, laxative, skilled at calming fatigue, and purifying the urine,

children.text: medovṛddhiṃ (vidhatte) vardhate śamayati ca malān tarpaṇaṃ cendriyāṇāṃ
children.translated_text: it increases fat, calms impurities, and nourishes the sense organs —

children.text: dantau ni (dantair ni)ṣpīḍya sākṣād amṛtamayaraso (saṃ) bhakṣayed ikṣudaṇḍaḥ (ḍaṃ) // 19 //
children.translated_text: having pressed the sugarcane stalk directly with the teeth, one should consume its nectar-like juice. (19)

children.text: kāntāro raktavarṇaḥ syāt kośākāras tathaiva ca /
children.translated_text: <s>Kāntāra</s> is of red color, and <s>kośākāra</s> likewise;

children.text: śvetas tu pauṇḍrako jñeyaḥ trayaḥ śreṣṭhās tathekṣavaḥ //
children.translated_text: the white one should be known as <s>pauṇḍraka</s> — these three are the best among sugarcanes.

children.text: madhuro mūlabhāvo (ge) syān madhye madhura eva ca /
children.translated_text: The root portion is sweet, the middle is sweet as well,

children.text: agrabhāge punas tasya ikṣoḥ syāl lavaṇo laghu // 20 //
children.translated_text: and the tip portion of the sugarcane is saline and light. (20)
One should eat sugarcane at the proper time, before meals;
although naturally sweet, it is semen-[producing] and when eaten aggravates <s>vāta</s>. (21)
It is burning, constipating, very heavy, and calming to dryness,
astringent, it would generate wind and cause vomiting;
held for some time, from the crushing of the whole root, middle, and leaf portions,
it becomes burning — therefore the mechanically pressed juice is not beneficial. (22)

children.text: mūlamadhyadalanāc ca tatkṣaṇāt sī [pī]yate yadi tu yāntriko rasaḥ /
children.translated_text: But if the mechanically pressed juice is drunk immediately after crushing the root, middle, and leaf portions,

children.text: vātapittaśamanas tadā bhavet tarpaṇaś ca malamūtraśodhanaḥ // 24 //
children.translated_text: then it calms <s>vāta</s> and <s>pitta</s>, is nourishing, and purifies impurities and urine. (24)

body.translated_text: Properties of <s>guḍa</s> (jaggery) and others:

body.text:
pittaghnaḥ pavanāpaho ruvi[ci]karo hṛdyas tridauṣāpahaḥ
saṃyogena viśeṣato jvaraharaḥ saṃtāpaśāntipradaḥ /
viṇmūtrāmayanāśano 'gnijananaḥ kaṇḍupramehāṃti [ta] kṛt

children.text: snigdhasvāduraso laghuḥ śramaharaḥ pathyaḥ purāṇo guḍaḥ // 25 ///
children.translated_text: unctuous, of sweet taste, light, and fatigue-removing — old <s>guḍa</s> (jaggery) is wholesome. (25)

body.translated_text: It destroys <s>pitta</s>, removes wind, promotes appetite, is pleasant to the heart, removes the three <s>doṣas</s>; especially in combination, it removes fever, grants relief from burning sensation; it destroys disorders of stool, urine, and disease, kindles the digestive fire, and cures itching and urinary diseases;

children.text: dāhaṃ nivārayati pittam apākaroti tṛṣṇāṃ chinatti vinihanti ca moharmūrchām /
children.translated_text: It wards off burning, removes <s>pitta</s>, cuts thirst, and destroys delusion and fainting;

children.text: śoṣaṃ vighaṭṭayati tarpayatīndriyāṇi śītaḥ sadā samadhuraḥ khalu siddhakhaṇḍaḥ // 26 //
children.translated_text: it dispels dryness and nourishes the sense organs — <s>siddhakhaṇḍa</s> (refined sugar candy) is always cooling and sweet. (26)
It pacifies thirst, delusion, craving, and oral swelling; it destroys burning and fever;
it removes asthma, vomiting, intoxication, fatigue, and impurities; it is pleasant to the heart and nourishing;

children.text: kṣīṇe retasi pāvake ca viṣame kṣīṇe kṣate durbale
children.translated_text: when semen is depleted, when the digestive fire is disturbed, when one is depleted, wounded, or weak,

children.text: durvāre 'pi ca raktapittakagade sevyā sadā śarkarā // 27 //
children.translated_text: and even in the difficult-to-cure disease of <s>raktapitta</s> (bleeding disorders) — <s>śarkarā</s> (sugar) should always be used. (27)

body.translated_text: Thus ends the section on sugarcane in the <s>Āyurvedamahodadhi</s> composed by <s>Suṣeṇa</s>.
Now the properties of liquor are described.

children.text: saṃdīpanaṃ madyam atīva tīkṣṇaṃ uṣṇaṃ ca taṣṭāṃ (tṛṣṇā) pradapuṣṭidaṃ ca /
children.translated_text: <s>Madya</s> (liquor) is exceedingly sharp and stimulating, hot, thirst-inducing, nourishing,

children.text: susvādu tiktaṃ kaṭukaṃ tathāmlaṃ jambūrasaṃ susvadanīyam etat // 1 //
children.translated_text: very pleasant-tasting, bitter, pungent, and sour, of <s>jambu</s> (rose-apple) flavor, and very palatable. (1)
[It is of a certain type], breaks up humors, produces strength, removes asthma and cough,
is aphrodisiac, light, hot, digestive of impurities, and promotes sleep;

children.text: pittāsṛkkaphasārake ca viṣame kārśye tathā pīnase
children.translated_text: in disorders of <s>pitta</s>, blood, and <s>kapha</s>, and in wasting and nasal catarrh,
it is dry, purifies the channels, promotes appetite, and dries up <s>vāta</s> and the other [<s>doṣas</s>]. (2)

children.text: (śleṣmāṇaṃ vinihanti yuktam aniśaṃ sevyaṃ sadā prāṇinā)
children.translated_text: It destroys <s>kapha</s> (phlegm) when used properly; it should always be consumed by living beings [in moderation].

children.text: kṛśe sthūle hitaṃ rūkṣaṃ sūkṣmaṃ ścoto (sroto) viśodhanam /
children.translated_text: Dry, subtle, and <s>sroto-viśodhana</s> (channel-purifying), it is beneficial for the emaciated and the corpulent;
Drunk with proper method, it is [wholesome], but otherwise it acts like poison. // 3 //

body.text:
gurutva (tad) doṣajananaṃ navaṃ jīrṇam ato 'nyathā /
nātyarthatīkṣṇamṛdvalpasaṃbhāraṃ kaluṣaṃ na ca /
body.translated_text: When fresh it is heavy and <s>doṣa</s>-generating; when aged, the opposite. It should not have excessively sharp, mild, or scanty ingredients, nor should it be turbid.
Now, the properties of <s>surā</s> (grain liquor):

children.translated_text: <s>Surā</s> is heavy, alleviates <s>gulma</s> (abdominal tumors), <s>udara</s> (abdominal diseases), <s>arśas</s> (hemorrhoids), <s>grahaṇī</s> (malabsorption), and <s>śopha</s> (swelling); it is unctuous to the heart;

<s>Surā</s> destroys <s>vāta</s> (wind), and removes <s>medas</s> (fat), <s>asṛk</s> (blood impurities), <s>stanya</s> (breast milk disorders), <s>mūtra</s> (urinary disorders), and <s>kapha</s> (phlegm).

body.translated_text: Now, the properties of <s>vāruṇī</s> (a type of liquor):

children.text: tadguṇā vāruṇī hṛdyā laghutīkṣṇā nihanti ca /
children.translated_text: <s>Vāruṇī</s> has similar properties [to <s>surā</s>], is pleasant to the heart, light, and sharp; it destroys
<s>śūla</s> (colic), <s>kāsa</s> (cough), <s>aruci</s> (anorexia), <s>śvāsa</s> (dyspnea), <s>vibandha</s> (constipation), <s>ādhmāna</s> (flatulence), and <s>pīnasa</s> (rhinitis). // 6 //

body.translated_text: It is astringent, hot, fire-kindling, dry, digestive, and destroys <s>śopha</s> (swelling).
Now, <s>surā</s> made with <s>pathyā</s> (Terminalia chebula) and <s>bibhītaka</s> (Terminalia bellirica):

body.text: nātyarthaṃ pramadā lāghvyāṃ (ghvī) yathā (pathyā) vaibhītikī surā // 7 //
body.translated_text: Like a woman of lightness, <s>surā</s> made with <s>pathyā</s> and <s>bibhītaka</s> is not exceedingly [potent]. // 7 //

body.text: vraṇe pāṇḍvāmaye kuṣṭe na cātyarthaṃ virudhyate /
body.translated_text: In wounds, <s>pāṇḍu</s> (anemia), and <s>kuṣṭha</s> (skin diseases), it is not greatly contraindicated.
Now, <s>yava-surā</s> (barley liquor):
<s>Yava-surā</s> (barley liquor) causes <s>viṣṭambha</s> (constipation), is heavy, dry, and aggravates all three <s>doṣas</s>. // 8 //
Now, the properties of <s>ariṣṭa</s> (medicated wine):

children.translated_text: <s>Ariṣṭa</s> possesses properties according to its ingredients, and is superior to all other alcoholic drinks in its qualities;

It destroys <s>grahaṇī</s> (malabsorption), <s>pāṇḍu</s> (anemia), <s>kuṣṭha</s> (skin diseases), <s>arśas</s> (hemorrhoids), <s>śoṣa</s> (wasting), <s>śoka</s> (grief), <s>udara</s> (abdominal diseases), and <s>jvara</s> (fever). // 9 //
It destroys <s>gulma</s> (abdominal tumors) and <s>krimi</s> (worms); it alleviates <s>plīhan</s> (splenic disorders); it is astringent, pungent, and aggravates <s>vāta</s>.

children.text: mārdvīkaṃ lekhanaṃ hṛdyaṃ nātyuṣṇaṃ madhuraṃ saram // 10 //
children.translated_text: <s>Mārdvīka</s> (grape wine) is scraping, pleasant to the heart, not excessively hot, sweet, and laxative. // 10 //
It mildly aggravates <s>pitta</s> and <s>vāta</s>, and destroys <s>pāṇḍu</s> (anemia), <s>meha</s> (urinary disorders), <s>arśas</s> (hemorrhoids), and <s>krimi</s> (worms).
<s>Gauḍa</s> (jaggery-based liquor) promotes clear vision, facilitates urine and feces, alleviates <s>vāta</s>, and is nourishing and appetite-stimulating. // 11 //

body.translated_text: It is very hot, sharp, dry, sour, pleasant to the heart, appetizing, and laxative. // 15 //

children.translated_text: It is digestive-stimulating, cool to the touch, and destroys <s>pāṇḍu</s> (anemia) and <s>krimi</s> (worms).
Among jaggery-based drinks, <s>madhu</s> (honey wine), <s>mādhvīka</s> (grape wine), and <s>sūkta</s> (vinegar) are progressively lighter. // 16 //
Liquors made from roots, tubers, and fruits should likewise be understood as having similar [graduated] properties.

children.text: śāṇḍākī cāsute(taṃ) cānyat kālāmlaṃ rocanaṃ laghu //
children.translated_text: <s>Śāṇḍākī</s> and other [fermented drinks], as well as <s>kālāmla</s> (black vinegar), are appetizing and light.

body.translated_text: // Thus ends the section on alcoholic beverages. //
Now begins the section on <s>kāñjika</s> (fermented gruel). //

body.text:
dhānyāmlaṃ bhedi tīkṣṇaṃ surabhi laghutaraṃ śo (so)ṣṇasaṃsparśarśītaṃ
rūkṣaṃ caiva klamaghnaṃ śramaharaviṣadaṃ vastisaṃśodhanaṃ ca /

children.text: śastaṃ vāsthāpanaṃ syāt* laghu viṣaśamanaṃ śvāsarogāpanodi
children.translated_text: It is recommended for <s>basti</s> (enema therapy), is light, counteracts poison, and removes <s>śvāsa</s> (dyspnea) and other diseases;

children.text: gaṇḍūṣo dhāraṇe syān mukhagadanivahe gandhanirnāśanaṃ ca /
children.translated_text: Used as a gargle, it cures diseases of the mouth and destroys bad odor.
<s>Dhānyāmla</s> (grain vinegar) is purgative, sharp, hot, aggravates <s>pitta</s>, and is cool to the touch;
It removes fatigue and exhaustion, is appetizing, digestive-stimulating, and purifies the bladder. // 1 //

body.translated_text: <s>Dhānyāmla</s> (grain vinegar) is purgative, sharp, fragrant, very light, hot yet cool to the touch, dry, and fatigue-dispelling; it removes exhaustion and impurities, and is a purifier of the bladder.
Thus ends the section on <s>kāñjika</s> (fermented gruel). //
// Now begins the section on <s>mūtra</s> (animal urines). //

body.text:
auṣṭraṃ (mūtraṃ) go 'jāvimahiṣīgajāśvoṣṭrakharodbhavam /
(pittalaṃ rūkṣatīkṣṇoṣṇaṃ lavaṇānurasaṃ kaṭu /
kṛmiśophodarānāhaśūlapāṇḍukaphānilān /
gulmāruciviṣaśvitrakuṣṭhārśāṃsi jayel laghu /)

children.translated_text: The urine group comprises [urines of] camel, cow, goat, horse, elephant, buffalo, and donkey —

children.text: tiktaṃ tīkṣṇaṃ laghūṣṇaṃ salavaṇasurasaṃ pittalaṃ bhedi rūkṣam /
children.translated_text: They are bitter, sharp, light, hot, with a salty and pleasant taste, <s>pitta</s>-aggravating, purgative, and dry;

children.text: hṛdyaṃ rucyaṃ krimighnaṃ hutavahajananaṃ kuṣṭhamehau vināśī (śi)
children.translated_text: They are pleasant to the heart, appetizing, worm-destroying, fire-kindling, and destroy <s>kuṣṭha</s> (skin diseases) and <s>meha</s> (urinary disorders);

They conquer <s>gulma</s> (abdominal tumors), <s>ānāha</s> (distension), <s>arśas</s> (hemorrhoids), <s>śūla</s> (colic), <s>vāta</s>, <s>kapha</s>, and <s>viṣa</s> (poison), and destroy <s>śopha</s> (swelling), <s>pāṇḍu</s> (anemia), and <s>udara</s> (abdominal diseases).

body.translated_text: Urine derived from cow, goat, sheep, buffalo, elephant, horse, camel, and donkey is <s>pitta</s>-aggravating, dry, sharp, hot, with a salty after-taste, and pungent; it is light and conquers <s>krimi</s> (worms), <s>śopha</s> (swelling), <s>udara</s> (abdominal diseases), <s>ānāha</s> (distension), <s>śūla</s> (colic), <s>pāṇḍu</s> (anemia), <s>kapha</s>, <s>vāta</s>, <s>gulma</s> (abdominal tumors), <s>aruci</s> (anorexia), <s>viṣa</s> (poison), <s>śvitra</s> (leucoderma), <s>kuṣṭha</s> (skin diseases), and <s>arśas</s> (hemorrhoids).

body.text:
mūtraṃ tathāṣṭādaśakuṣṭhaśophapāṇḍūdaronmādakaphāmayaghnam /
sevyaṃ niddarśā (?) vikāram etat rūkṣaṃ tathāmlaṃ krimiṣu praśastam /
body.translated_text: <s>Mūtra</s> (urine) likewise destroys the eighteen types of <s>kuṣṭha</s> (skin diseases), <s>śopha</s> (swelling), <s>pāṇḍu</s> (anemia), <s>udara</s> (abdominal diseases), <s>unmāda</s> (insanity), and <s>kapha</s> disorders; it should be used for such ailments; it is dry, sour, and praised for [treating] <s>krimi</s> (worms).
// Thus ends the section on <s>mūtra</s> (animal urines). //
// Now begins the section on <s>dhānya</s> (grains). //

children.text: snigdho vātaharas tridoṣaśamanaḥ pathyaḥ sadā prāṇināṃ
children.translated_text: <s>Śāli</s> (rice) is unctuous, alleviates <s>vāta</s>, pacifies all three <s>doṣas</s>, is always wholesome for living beings,

children.text: śreṣṭhaḥ pauṣṭika [śreṣṭho brīhiṣu ṣaṣṭikaḥ] śramaharaḥ kṛcchrādiḍoṣāpahā /
children.translated_text: The foremost and nourishing — <s>ṣaṣṭika</s> (sixty-day rice) is the best among rices — it removes fatigue and eliminates diseases such as <s>kṛcchra</s> (dysuria);

children.text: gaura(ś cā)śvāsitagaurato 'pi nitarāṃ sevyaḥ karoty uccakaiḥ
children.translated_text: The white variety is to be preferred even more than the dark and white [mixed], as it greatly produces
<s>Śukra</s> (semen/vitality), removes <s>śvāsa</s> (dyspnea), alleviates fatigue, and eliminates diseases such as <s>kāsa</s> (cough). // 1 //
Sweet in taste and in post-digestive effect, it pacifies <s>vāta</s>, <s>kapha</s>, and <s>pitta</s>;
It is wholesome in <s>jvara</s> (fever) and <s>ajīrṇa</s> (indigestion), and removes all types of febrile afflictions;
For children, the elderly, young women, the delicate, and those accustomed to comfort,

children.text: ayaṃ sevyo rājā bhavati hi mahāśāliramalaḥ // 2 //
children.translated_text: This king of rices, the great pure <s>śāli</s>, should be regularly consumed. // 2 //

body.text: dhānyaṃ vāpitam uttamaṃ tad akhilaṃ (chi)channodbhavaṃ madhyamaṃ

children.text: jñeyaṃ dyadavargapittaṃ (tad yad avāpitaṃ) tad adhamaṃ nissāradoṣapradam // 3 //
children.translated_text: That which is uncultivated is known to be the lowest, devoid of essence and producing <s>doṣas</s>. // 3 //

body.translated_text: Grain that is cultivated is the best; that which grows from self-sown [fallen] seeds is middling;

children.translated_text: {cf. Rājanighaṇṭu 16.158ab}

children.text: dagdhā yadbhavicpeṣyaṃ tetha (?) vipine yad vāpitāḥ śālayaḥ
children.translated_text: Rice that grows in burnt forest land where [the ground] has been cleared by fire,

children.text: ete chinnabhavā bhavanti khalu te viṇmūtrabandhapradāḥ // 3 //
children.translated_text: Such self-grown [wild] rices cause binding of feces and urine. // 3 //
{cf. Rājanighaṇṭu 16.158cd}

children.text: deśe deśe tu jātāś ca nānāvarṇāś ca śālayaḥ /
children.translated_text: In different regions grow different varieties and colors of <s>śāli</s> (rice);
Among them, the foremost by nature is the supreme pacifier of all three <s>doṣas</s>. // 4 //
<s>Rakta</s> (red), <s>Bhīruka</s>, <s>Puṇḍarīka</s>, <s>Kalama</s>, <s>Tūrṇa</s>, <s>Mahāpuṣpaka</s>,
<s>Dīrgha</s>, <s>Kāñcanahāyana</s>, <s>Asitaśrita</s>, <s>Puṣpapāṇḍuja</s>, <s>Pāṇḍuka</s>,

children.text: sāgarakhyās tapanīyakāḥ śakunako rodhras tu saugandhikaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Sāgara</s>, <s>Tapanīyaka</s>, <s>Śakunaka</s>, <s>Rodhra</s>, and <s>Saugandhika</s> —
These and others such as <s>Dhāna</s>, along with <s>Pataṅgī</s> and <s>Dūṣaka</s>, are excellent, auspicious <s>śāli</s> rices. // 5 //

body.text:
susabhāḥ (?) yācanadīpanā balakarā snigdhās tridoṣāpahāḥ
śuklaśleṣmavivardhanā rucikarāḥ saṃdīpanās tarpaṇāḥ /
body.translated_text: They are appetizing, digestive-stimulating, strength-giving, unctuous, pacifiers of all three <s>doṣas</s>; the white ones increase <s>śleṣman</s> (phlegm); they are taste-promoting, appetite-kindling, and nourishing;
They are wholesome, beneficial in all diseases, fatigue-removing, and destroyers of hunger, thirst, and exhaustion;

body.text: śreṣṭhā vrīhiṣu ṣaṣṭikāḥ kalapa (ma) kā raktā mahāśālayaḥ // 6 //
body.translated_text: The best among rices are <s>ṣaṣṭika</s> (sixty-day rice), <s>kalamaka</s>, <s>rakta</s> (red rice), and the great <s>śāli</s> rices. // 6 //

children.translated_text: The various types of <s>śāli</s> rice are appetizing, nourishing, pleasant to the heart, and digestive;
They are heavy, nourishing, and wholesome. // 7 //
[A certain rice variety] is pleasant to the heart, sweet, revitalizing, and light;
It is aphrodisiac and strength-giving; taken with ghee, it destroys the three <s>malas</s> (bodily wastes). // 8 //
<s>Rājānna</s> (royal rice) destroys <s>kapha</s> and <s>vāta</s>, is sweet, and alleviates <s>pitta</s>;
It bestows beauty, <s>śukra</s> (vitality), great radiance, <s>sattva</s> (mental clarity), purity, and strength. // 9 //

children.text: kṛṣṭi [ṣṇa] śāli [stri] tridoṣaghno madhuraḥ kārśyahā tathā /
children.translated_text: <s>Kṛṣṇa-śāli</s> (black rice) destroys all three <s>doṣas</s>, is sweet, and removes emaciation;
It alleviates <s>pitta</s>, is slimy, and bestows <s>śukra</s> (vitality), beauty, complexion, and strength. // 10 //
These properties of <s>śāli</s> (rice) have been declared and should be known by those learned in the <s>śāstras</s> (medical sciences);
All wild-grain food destroys <s>kuṣṭha</s> (skin diseases). // 11 //
It quickly removes all diseases and also purifies the mouth.

children.text: dhānye śreṣṭhaṃ ṣaṣṭikaṃ rājabhojyaṃ māṃse tv ājaṃ taittirīkaṃ hitaṃ syāt /
children.translated_text: Among grains, <s>ṣaṣṭika</s> (sixty-day rice) is the best, fit for kings; among meats, goat and partridge are most beneficial; water should be [filtered through] black clay; among milk, ghee, and such, that of the cow is praised foremost.

children.text: pānīyaṃ syāt kṛṣṇamṛtsnāsam etaṃ kṣīrājyādau gavyam ādau praśastam //

body.translated_text: // Thus ends the section on <s>śāli</s> (rice varieties). //

children.translated_text: They are hot, dry, astringent, and sweet, predominantly light in post-digestive effect,
They destroy <s>kapha</s>, aggravate <s>vāta</s> and <s>pitta</s>, and always cause <s>viṣṭambha</s> (constipation);
This has been declared as the characterization of <s>romāka</s> and other [coarse] grains for mankind;
Properly, with [preparations of] <s>bala-śāka</s> (greens), liquids, and broths, the subsequent order is established.

body.translated_text: // Thus ends the section on <s>dhānya</s> (grains). //
// Now the properties of <s>śimbi-dhānya</s> (leguminous grains) are described. //
First, the properties of <s>mudga</s> (mung bean):

children.text: mudgaḥ pittakaphāpaho vraṇaharaḥ kaṃvā(ṭhā) mayaghno laghuḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Mudga</s> (mung bean) alleviates <s>pitta</s> and <s>kapha</s>, heals wounds, destroys diseases of the throat, and is light; it is wholesome for those with <s>vāta</s> excess, purgation [recovery], parasites, and always for eye diseases;
It does not cause flatulence, and alleviates <s>vāta</s>; it is recommended for those with weak digestive fire;
It is the best among <s>sūpas</s> (soups/broths), is voice-enhancing, and eliminates urinary diseases.

body.translated_text: Now, <s>māṣa</s> (black gram):

children.translated_text: <s>Māṣa</s> (black gram) is unctuous, strength-giving, increases fecal bulk, is desiccating, and produces <s>śleṣman</s> (phlegm);
It is hot in potency and quickly provokes <s>rakta-pitta</s> (bleeding disorders);

children.text: hanyād vātaṃ gurur atiraso rocako bhakṣa (kṣya) māṇaḥ
children.translated_text: It destroys <s>vāta</s>, is heavy, exceedingly flavorful, and appetizing when consumed;
Sweet, it is always vitalizing for men who enjoy the pleasures of exertion. // 1 //
{cf. Rājanighaṇṭu 16.81}
<s>Māṣa</s> is heavy, loosens feces and urine, is unctuous, hot in potency, sweet, and destroys <s>vāta</s>;
It is nourishing, promotes breast milk production, and especially gives strength and increases <s>śukra</s> (vitality) and <s>kapha</s>;

children.text: kaṣāyabhāvānna purīṣabhedī na mūtralo me (nai)va balāsakartā (?) //
children.translated_text: Due to its astringent quality, it does not [excessively] break down feces, nor increase urine, nor produce <s>balāsa</s> (phlegmatic discharge).
Sweet in post-digestive effect, very dense, nourishing, and promoting breast milk and appetite;

children.text: māṣaiḥ samānāṃ phalam ātmagutma(pta) mūcuś ca kākāṇḍaphalaṃ tathaiva //
children.translated_text: The fruit of <s>kākāṇḍa</s> (a plant) and <s>ātmagupta</s> (<s>Mucuna pruriens</s>) are said to have properties equal to <s>māṣa</s>.

body.translated_text: // Thus end the properties of <s>māṣa</s> (black gram). //
Now the properties of <s>kulattha</s> (horse gram):

children.translated_text: <s>Kulattha</s> (horse gram), the dark variety, is astringent in taste,
Pungent in post-digestive effect, and destroys <s>kapha</s> and <s>vāta</s>;
An astringent, and removes <s>pīnasa</s> (rhinitis) and <s>kāsa</s> (cough). // 1 //

body.translated_text: It is a destroyer of <s>śukra</s> (excessive semen), <s>aśmarī</s> (urinary stones), and <s>gulma</s> (abdominal tumors),

children.translated_text: It removes <s>ānāha</s> (distension), <s>medas</s> (fat), <s>gudakīla</s> (rectal fistula), <s>hikkā</s> (hiccup), and <s>śvāsa</s> (dyspnea), but aggravates <s>śoṇita</s> (blood) and <s>pitta</s>;
It destroys <s>kapha</s> and cures eye diseases, especially when combined with wild <s>kulattha</s>. // 2 //

body.translated_text: Now the properties of <s>rājamāṣa</s> (a type of bean):

children.translated_text: <s>Rājamāṣa</s> is appetizing, aggravates <s>kapha</s>, is sour, and increases <s>pitta</s>;
It is very tasty, aggravates <s>vāta</s>, is dry, astringent, and yet very heavy. // 3 //
It is dry, astringent, and promotes poison, grief, <s>śukra</s> (vitality), <s>balāsa</s> (phlegmatic discharge), deterioration of vision, and wasting;

children.text: kaṭur vipāke madhuraś ca śimbiḥ pravṛddhaviṇmūtra (mā)rutapittalaś ca // 4 //
children.translated_text: <s>Śimbi</s> (legumes in general) are pungent in post-digestive effect and sweet; they increase feces, urine, <s>vāta</s>, and <s>pitta</s>. // 4 //

body.text: sitāsitaḥ pītakaraktavarṇā bhavanti vai naikavidhās tu śibiṃ(mbyaḥ) : //
body.translated_text: They come in white, dark, yellow, and red colors, and <s>śimbī</s> (legumes) are of many kinds.
Now the properties of <s>tila</s> (sesame):

body.text: īṣatkaṣayo madhuraḥ satikto(ktaḥ) saṃgrāhakaḥ pittakaras tathoṣṇaḥ //
body.translated_text: <s>Tila</s> (sesame) is slightly astringent, sweet, and bitter; it is astringent [in action], aggravates <s>pitta</s>, and is hot;

body.text: tilo vipāke madhuro baliṣṭhaḥ snigdho vraṇālepanapathya uktaḥ //
body.translated_text: In post-digestive effect it is sweet, very potent, unctuous, and is declared wholesome for wound application.

children.translated_text: It is beneficial for teeth, generates <s>agni</s> (digestive fire) and <s>medhā</s> (intellect), reduces urine, promotes breast milk, benefits hair, destroys <s>vāta</s>, and is heavy.

children.text: tileṣu sarpiṣv asita [sarveṣv asitaḥ] pradhāno medhyaḥ sito hīnataras tathānyaḥ //
children.translated_text: Among all sesame seeds, the black is foremost; it promotes <s>medhā</s> (intellect); the white is inferior, and other types are even lesser.
It is beneficial for teeth, generates complexion, strength, <s>agni</s> (digestive fire), and <s>buddhi</s> (intellect), promotes breast milk, destroys <s>vāta</s>, and is heavy;
It is unctuous, aggravates <s>pitta</s>, reduces urine, benefits hair, is exceedingly wholesome for wounds;

children.text: grāhyuṣṇo dhṛtikṛt kaṣāyamadhuras tikto vipāke kaṭuḥ
children.translated_text: It is astringent, hot, promotes fortitude, is astringent and sweet [in taste], bitter, pungent in post-digestive effect;
The black <s>tila</s> is the most wholesome; the white is of lesser quality; other types of <s>tila</s> have even fewer properties. // 1 //

body.translated_text: Thus ends [the section on] <s>tila</s> (sesame). //
// Now the properties of <s>yava</s> (barley) are described. //

children.text: yavaḥ kaṣāyo madhuro himaś ca kaṭur vipāke kaphapittahāraḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Yava</s> (barley) is astringent, sweet, cooling, and pungent in post-digestive effect; it removes <s>kapha</s> and <s>pitta</s>;

children.text: vraṇeṣu pathyas tilavac ca nityaṃ prabaddhamūtro bahuvātavarśa [rcā]ḥ // 1 //
children.translated_text: It is wholesome for wounds as sesame is; it binds urine and is rich in <s>vāta</s>-[aggravating properties]. // 1 //
It promotes stability, <s>agni</s> (digestive fire), <s>dhātu</s> (bodily tissues), voice, and complexion; it is somewhat slimy and scrapes away corpulence;

children.text: medomaruttṛṭ [ḍ] haraṇo virūkṣaḥ prasādanaḥ śoṇitapittayoś ca // 2 //
children.translated_text: It removes <s>medas</s> (fat), <s>vāta</s>, and thirst; it is dry and purifies blood and <s>pitta</s>. // 2 //

body.text: ebhir guṇair hīnamataś ca nityaṃ vidyād yavebhyo 'nyatha [ya] vānaśeṣaḥ /
body.translated_text: One should know that all other minor grains are always inferior to barley in these properties.

children.text: yavaḥ kaṣāyo madhuraḥ saśīto mehe hitaḥ pittakaphāmayaghnaḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Yava</s> (barley) is astringent, sweet, and cooling; it is beneficial in <s>meha</s> (urinary disorders) and destroys <s>pitta</s> and <s>kapha</s> disorders;

children.text: prasṛṣṭavarco 'nyayavaḥ sabalyo balyaś ca vṛṣyaś ca male hitaś ca // 3 //
children.translated_text: Other barley [varieties] loosen the bowels and are strengthening, virility-promoting, and beneficial for the <s>malas</s> (bodily wastes). // 3 //

children.text: śītaḥ kaṣāyaḥ surasaś ca rūkṣo mehakrimiśleṣmaviṣāpahaś ca /
children.translated_text: <s>Veṇu-yava</s> (bamboo grain) is cooling, astringent, pleasant in taste, dry, and removes <s>meha</s> (urinary disorders), <s>krimi</s> (worms), <s>śleṣman</s> (phlegm), and <s>viṣa</s> (poison);

children.text: mādhuryayukto balavāṃs tathaiva pittāpaho veṇuyavaḥ pradiṣṭaḥ // 4 //
children.translated_text: It is endowed with sweetness and strength, and is declared to alleviate <s>pitta</s>. // 4 //

body.translated_text: Thus ends [the section on] <s>veṇu-yava</s> (bamboo grain). //
Now the properties of <s>godhūma</s> (wheat):

body.text: godhūma ukto madhuro guruś ca balyaḥ sthiraḥ śukrarucipradaś ca

children.text: snigdho '[ti] si śīto 'nilapītahārī [pittahantā] saṃdhānakṛcchrāśmaharaḥ saraś ca // 1 //
children.translated_text: It is unctuous, cooling, and destroys <s>vāta</s> and <s>pitta</s>; it promotes healing of fractures and removes urinary stones; it is laxative. // 1 //

body.translated_text: <s>Godhūma</s> (wheat) is declared sweet, heavy, strengthening, stabilizing, and bestowing <s>śukra</s> (vitality) and appetite;

children.translated_text: Unctuous and sweet in taste, sweet in post-digestive effect, generally harboring <s>āma</s> (undigested matter),

children.text: balyaḥ śītakaraḥ saro rucikaraḥ saṃdhānakārī guruḥ /
children.translated_text: Strengthening, cooling, laxative, appetizing, promoting healing, and heavy;
It increases <s>śukra</s> (vitality) and <s>śleṣman</s> (phlegm), promotes fortitude, and destroys <s>pitta</s> and <s>vāta</s>;

children.text: godhūmas tu manoharaḥ sthirakaraḥ śveto vikārāpahā // 2 //
children.translated_text: <s>Godhūma</s> (wheat) is delightful, stabilizing, and the white variety removes disorders. // 2 //

body.translated_text: Now the properties of <s>kusumbha</s> (safflower):

body.text: kaṭur vipāke kaṭukaḥ kaphaghno vidāhako vātaharaḥ kusumbhaḥ //
body.translated_text: <s>Kusumbha</s> (safflower) is pungent in post-digestive effect, pungent, destroys <s>kapha</s>, causes burning, and removes <s>vāta</s>.
Now the properties of <s>siddhārthaka</s> (white mustard):

children.text: uṣṇas tathā svāduraso 'nilaghnaḥ pittolbaṇaḥ syāt kaṭuko vipāke /
children.translated_text: <s>Siddhārthaka</s> (white mustard) is hot, sweet in taste, destroys <s>vāta</s>, exceedingly aggravates <s>pitta</s>, and is pungent in post-digestive effect;

children.text: pāke rase vāpi kaṭuḥ pradiṣṭaḥ siddhārthakaḥ śoṇitapittakartā // 1 //
children.translated_text: It is pungent in both taste and post-digestive effect; <s>siddhārthaka</s> causes blood and <s>pitta</s> disorders. // 1 //

body.translated_text: It is sharp and hot in potency, and destroys <s>kapha</s> and <s>vāta</s>; the dark <s>sarṣapa</s> (mustard) likewise [has similar properties].
Now, the properties of <s>Āḍhakī</s> (pigeon pea):

children.translated_text: <s>Āḍhakī</s>
pacifies <s>Kapha</s> (phlegm) and <s>Vāta</s> (wind), and is hot in <s>Vīrya</s> (potency),
it removes diseases of the heart, spleen, abdomen, and <s>Vāta</s>, and alleviates pain and obesity;
it cures cough, dyspnea, vomiting, thirst, and fever, is wholesome, and remedies throat ailments,

children.text: yā [pā]mākuṣṭhabhagandareṣu na tathā rucyās tu pathyā bhṛśam // 1 //
children.translated_text: it is beneficial in skin diseases, poisoning, fistula-in-ano, and similar conditions, yet it does not greatly promote appetite. || 1 ||

body.translated_text: <s>Āḍhakī</s> destroys <s>Kapha</s> and <s>Vāta</s>, but when dry, it aggravates <s>Vāta</s>. || 2 ||

children.text: tasyaitad vidaṃ [vidhaṃ] bhojyaṃ svādu viṣṭambhanaṃ guru /
children.translated_text: Its prepared food is sweet, produces <s>Viṣṭambha</s> (constipation), and is heavy;
it kindles the digestive fire, destroys <s>Kapha</s> and <s>Pitta</s>, and eliminates all types of <s>Prameha</s> (urinary disorders). || 3 ||

body.text:
hṛdyaṃ vāsukhaṃ datvā āḍhakī bhuddhapūṣakaḥ / [?] sūrīcaikaḍhanaṃ // [?]
mudgapū [yū]ṣaguṇāḥ //
body.translated_text: It is pleasing to the heart and gives comfort from <s>Vāta</s>; <s>Āḍhakī</s> with <s>Pūṣaka</s> [?]; the single wealth of <s>Sūrī</s> [?]. Properties of <s>Mudga-Yūṣa</s> (mung bean soup):

children.translated_text: It removes fever, bestows strength, and destroys <s>Raktapitta</s> (bleeding disorders);
the learned declare that <s>Mudga-Yūṣa</s> (mung bean soup) is excellent,
when prepared with oleaginous substances, it also destroys <s>Vāta</s> (wind),
it alleviates burning sensation in the body and is praised as beneficial in all diseases. || 1 ||

children.text: pittajvarātiśamanaṃ laghumudga[yū] pūṣaṃ saṃtāpahāri tad arocakanāśanaṃ ca /
children.translated_text: Light <s>Mudga-Yūṣa</s> (mung bean soup) greatly pacifies <s>Pitta</s>-type fever, removes heat, and destroys loss of appetite;

children.text: raktaprasādanam idaṃ yadi saindhavena yuktaṃ tadā bhavati sarvarujāpahāri // 2 //
children.translated_text: it purifies the blood, and when combined with <s>Saindhava</s> (rock salt), it removes all pains. || 2 ||

children.text: vyapagatamaladoṣāḥ prāṇinaḥ kṣīṇamātrā adhikataratṛṣārtā ye ca dharmaprataptāḥ /
children.translated_text: Those beings who are free from impurities and toxins, who are emaciated, who are excessively afflicted by thirst, who are tormented by righteous austerities,

children.text: jvalanamukhavidagdhā ye 'tisārābhibhūtāḥ punar iha manujās te mudupū [yū]ṣasya yogyāḥ // 3 //
children.translated_text: who are scorched by the mouth of fire, and who are overcome by <s>Atisāra</s> (diarrhea) — for such people, <s>Mudga-Yūṣa</s> (mung bean soup) is suitable. || 3 ||

body.translated_text: Properties of <s>Kulittha-Yūṣa</s> (horse gram soup):

children.text: vīrye colāḥ [ṣṇāḥ] kulitthāḥ kaphapavanaharāḥ pittaraktapradāś ca
children.translated_text: <s>Kulittha</s> (horse gram) is hot in <s>Vīrya</s> (potency), removes <s>Kapha</s> and <s>Vāta</s>, but aggravates <s>Pitta</s> and <s>Rakta</s> (blood);
sour in post-digestive effect, it alleviates dyspnea, cough, abdominal diseases, and pains of the heart, head, and bladder;
it cures urinary retention, <s>Prameha</s> (urinary disorders), and urinary stones, and it breaks down <s>Śukra</s> (semen);
it is most excellent in hemorrhoids, fistula, skin diseases, swelling, rectal conditions, worm infestations, abdominal tumors, and similar afflictions. || 1 ||

body.translated_text: Properties of <s>Masūra-Yūṣa</s> (lentil soup):

children.translated_text: <s>Masūra</s> (lentil) is light, very dry, clear, and removes eye diseases and urinary disorders;
it eliminates <s>Śleṣma</s> (phlegm) and <s>Pitta</s>, promotes appetite, but causes <s>Vāta</s> diseases;
it produces <s>Viṣṭambha</s> (constipation), and is effective in treating abdominal distension, <s>Kṛcchra</s> (dysuria), and urinary stones;

children.text: sarve pittavikārajeṣu [vi] hitā hṛdyāś ca māsūryakāḥ // 1 //
children.translated_text: all lentil preparations are beneficial in <s>Pitta</s>-type disorders and are pleasing to the heart. || 1 ||

body.translated_text: Now, the properties of <s>Kalāya</s> (field pea):

children.translated_text: It produces abundant <s>Vāta</s> (?), is very dry,
removes <s>Kapha</s>, and is exceedingly effective against <s>Pitta</s>;
it promotes appetite but causes <s>Śūla</s> (colic pain) in people,
and is associated with <s>Āma</s> (undigested toxins) — thus is <s>Kalāya</s> described. || 1 ||

body.translated_text: Now the properties of <s>Caṇaka</s> (chickpea) are described:

children.translated_text: Dry, wind-producing, pacifying <s>Prameha</s> (urinary disorders), effective in treating <s>Kṛcchra</s> (dysuria) and urinary stones,
they cause loose stools, pacify <s>Pitta</s>, but produce <s>Ādhmāna</s> (flatulence) and related disorders;
they cure throat ailments, provide good nourishment and comfort, and destroy loss of appetite;

children.text: balyā varṇakarā vibhuktacaṇakāḥ puṃsaś ca naite hitāḥ // 1 //
children.translated_text: they give strength and improve complexion — such are well-cooked <s>Caṇaka</s> (chickpeas), though they are not wholesome for men when overeaten. || 1 ||

body.translated_text: Thus, dried <s>Caṇaka</s> (chickpeas):

children.translated_text: they pacify <s>Vāta</s> and <s>Pitta</s>, are cooling, and prevent <s>Mūtrakṛcchra</s> (dysuria). || 2 ||

body.translated_text: Fresh [chickpeas] are most virilifying, give strength, are phlegm-producing, and promote appetite;
Thus, fresh <s>Caṇaka</s> (chickpeas):

children.translated_text: Roasted <s>Caṇaka</s> (chickpeas) are light and cause extreme fatigue and exhaustion;
they cure vomiting, promote appetite, and bestow sleep, comfort, and nourishment. || 3 ||

body.translated_text: Thus, roasted <s>Caṇaka</s> (chickpeas):

children.text: āsitacaṇakayūṣo dāhanāśaṃ vidhatte prabalam ahitalabdhaṃ (?) sarvamehapraṇāśam /
children.translated_text: A soup of soaked <s>Caṇaka</s> removes burning sensation and powerfully destroys all types of <s>Prameha</s> (urinary disorders);
when combined with digestive fire and pepper, it removes <s>Vāta</s> diseases; when cooked with split-pulse water, it destroys all <s>Doṣas</s> (humors). || 4 ||

body.translated_text: Thus, black <s>Caṇaka</s> (chickpeas):

children.translated_text: White <s>Caṇaka</s> (chickpeas) pacify <s>Pitta</s> but aggravate <s>Śleṣma</s> (phlegm) and <s>Vāta</s>;
they are associated with producing constipation in feces, weakness of digestive fire, and loss of strength. || 5 ||

body.translated_text: <s>Caṇaka</s> water, cool as moonbeams, removes <s>Prameha</s> (urinary disorders), <s>Pitta</s>, blood disorders, and pain;

children.translated_text: it is satiating and has a beautiful sweetness. || 6 ||

body.translated_text: it is nourishing, possessing inherent oil-like qualities in digestion,
Thus, white <s>Caṇaka</s> (chickpeas):

children.text: śyāmākāḥ kodravā ye 'nye ye cānye 'nu ca śimbikāḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Śyāmāka</s> (millet), <s>Kodrava</s> (a type of grain), and other <s>Śimbikā</s> (legumes) of similar kinds,

children.text: apathyās te na śaṃsanti [śasyante] sukhināṃ nirujāṃ tathā // 1 //
children.translated_text: are unwholesome and not recommended for healthy and disease-free people. || 1 ||

children.text: yad yaj jīryaty atikṣipraṃ tat tal laghutaraṃ smṛtam /
children.translated_text: Whatever is digested very quickly, that is considered the lightest;

children.text: yavagodhūmamāṣāś ca tilāś cāpi navā hitāḥ // 2 //
children.translated_text: barley, wheat, <s>Māṣa</s> (black gram), and sesame — even these are wholesome when fresh. || 2 ||

body.translated_text: Thus ends the section on grains (<s>Dhānyavarga</s>).
May there be auspiciousness for the scribe and the reader! Salutations to <s>Śrī Sāmbasadāśiva</s>!
May there be prosperity!
Now, the properties of cooked foods (<s>Pakvānna</s>):
<s>Godhūma-Pheṇikā</s> (wheat froth preparation):

children.text: salaghurucirakāmā pheṇikātipraśastā balayati laghujīrā chardināśaṃ karoti /
children.translated_text: The highly praised <s>Pheṇikā</s> is light, pleasant, and beautiful; it gives strength, is easily digested, and cures vomiting;

children.text: badalavimukhamardhaṃ [?] cāmlapitte vidāhaṃ jaṭharabharaṇayogyā godhūmaiḥ saṃprayuktā // 1 //
children.translated_text: it removes [?] acidic <s>Pitta</s> and burning sensation; it is suitable for bearing the weight of the stomach, when prepared with wheat. || 1 ||

body.translated_text: <s>Pheṇiyā</s> (a type of wheat preparation):

children.text: guravo bṛṃhaṇāḥ snigdhā balyāḥ śukrakarāḥ parāḥ /
children.translated_text: They are heavy, nourishing, unctuous, give strength, and are supreme promoters of <s>Śukra</s> (semen);
they produce delight in women — those made from flour dumplings. || 2 ||

body.translated_text: <s>Godhūma-Sāñjīlāḍu</s> (wheat sweet ball):

children.text: toyājyena vimarditaṃ samasitaṃ kṛtvā sutaptaṃ tathā
children.translated_text: Having kneaded [the flour] with water and ghee, mixed with sugar, and well-heated,

children.text: khaṇḍājyena paced dhutāśanamṛdau kṛtvā subandhaṃ tataḥ /
children.translated_text: one should cook it in a portion of ghee in a well-heated vessel, making a good binding, then
with camphor, pepper, rock salt, and the four spices (<s>Caturjātaka</s>),

children.text: puṣpālambam iti bruvanti munayo nāmnā mahāmodakam // 3 //
children.translated_text: the sages call this by the name <s>Puṣpālamba</s>, the great <s>Modaka</s> (sweetmeat). || 3 ||

children.text: vṛṣyās tu kandarpakarā yathāgni saṃvardhitāḥ prītirucipradāyakāḥ /
children.translated_text: They are virilifying, aphrodisiac, enhance the digestive fire, and bestow love and appetite;

children.text: vātaṃ sapittaṃ praharanti bhuktāḥ sanmodakā modakarā narāṇām // 4 //
children.translated_text: when eaten, these <s>Modakas</s> destroy <s>Vāta</s> together with <s>Pitta</s> and bring delight to men. || 4 ||

children.text: modako gurur atīva vṛṣyakaḥ śleṣmalaś ciravipākatas tathā /
children.translated_text: <s>Modaka</s> (sweetmeat) is exceedingly heavy, virilifying, phlegm-producing, and slow to digest;

children.text: mandam agni janayec ca koṣṭabhṛkha (?) modako 'dhikabalapradaḥ sadā // 5 //
children.translated_text: it weakens the digestive fire and is difficult for those with abdominal disorders (?), yet <s>Modaka</s> always gives abundant strength. || 5 ||

body.translated_text: <s>Amṛtaphala</s> (ambrosia fruit preparation):

children.text: śamayati bahu pittaṃ śleṣmakopaṃ karoti janayati jaṭharāgniṃ vātarogān nihanti /
children.translated_text: It greatly pacifies <s>Pitta</s>, causes aggravation of <s>Śleṣma</s> (phlegm), kindles the stomach fire, and destroys <s>Vāta</s> diseases;

children.text: suratajanitakhedaṃ tatkṣaṇād eva hanyād amṛtaphalam udāraṃ cāru śaṃsanti khe (vai)dyāḥ // 6 //
children.translated_text: it instantly removes the fatigue born of sexual union — physicians praise the noble <s>Amṛtaphala</s> as excellent. || 6 ||

body.text: śamayaty arśaḥkṛcchrān harati savātaṃ tathā pittam // 7 //
body.translated_text: It cures hemorrhoids and <s>Kṛcchra</s> (dysuria), and removes <s>Vāta</s> together with <s>Pitta</s>. || 7 ||
<s>Kāpūrapaḍīyā</s> (camphor preparation):

children.text: rucyā balyā balamalakarā hṛdyagandhā sthirā ca
children.translated_text: It promotes appetite, gives strength, produces bodily vigor, is pleasing to the heart, fragrant, and stable;

children.text: tejo varṇaṃ vapuṣi kurute śukravṛddhiṃ karoti /
children.translated_text: it bestows radiance and complexion to the body and increases <s>Śukra</s> (semen);
it increases <s>Medas</s> (fat) rapidly and is excellent in <s>Pitta</s> disorders,
when cooked with ghee and combined with <s>Aguru</s> (aloe wood), honey, and <s>Elā</s> (cardamom). || 8 ||

body.text:
karpūrādyā vidalanakarā rājayakṣmāpahantrī
viśvasyaiṣā hitakaratamalkādinī (?) bhakṣaṇīyā //
body.translated_text: The camphor preparation is a splitting agent, destroys <s>Rājayakṣmā</s> (consumption), is beneficial to all, and is an edible containing <s>Āmalakī</s> (?) and similar ingredients.

children.translated_text: <s>Ghārikā</s>, <s>Iṃḍurikā</s>, <s>Apūpā</s>, <s>Vaṭikā</s>, <s>Vaṭaka</s>, and similar preparations:

children.text: vṛṣyakā rocakā balyā guravaḥ syuḥ svayonivat // 9 //
children.translated_text: are virilifying, appetite-promoting, strengthening, and heavy, similar in nature to their base ingredients. || 9 ||

body.translated_text: <s>Indrārikā</s> (a sweetmeat preparation):
<s>Indrārikā</s>:

children.translated_text: It is virilifying, appetite-promoting, digestive-fire-kindling, strengthening, heavy, and flow-producing;
it nourishes the <s>Prāṇa</s> (vital breath), is rich in flavor, and carries <s>Śleṣma</s> (phlegm);
it pacifies flatulence, constipation, abdominal tumors, and destroys <s>Pitta</s> and blood disorders;

children.text: snehenāpi supūritā ca satataṃ (bhakṣye) kṣa kṣeyam indrārikā //
children.translated_text: when well-prepared with oil, this <s>Indrārikā</s> is always an excellent food.

body.translated_text: <s>Dhṛtapūra</s> (ghee-filled preparation):

children.translated_text: <s>Dhṛtapūra</s> gives strength, is virilifying, sweet, and cooling;

children.text: hanti vātaṃ raktapittaṃ śleṣmalaṃ ca viśeṣataḥ //
children.translated_text: it destroys <s>Vāta</s> and <s>Raktapitta</s> (bleeding disorders), and especially removes <s>Śleṣma</s> (phlegm).

body.translated_text: <s>Sāḍiyā</s> (a preparation):

children.translated_text: <s>Kṣārakharjūrikā</s> (alkaline date preparation) is unctuous, and bestows <s>Śukra</s> (semen), flesh, and strength;
it gives power, promotes sexual desire, is pleasing to the heart, and destroys vomiting and loss of appetite.

body.translated_text: <s>Kṣīravaṭikā</s> (milk cake):

body.text:
susnigdhā vaṭikā ca dugdhamṛditā kāntyai ca saukhyapradā
tṛṣṇāśaktikarī śramapraśamanī mandāgnaye durjarā //
body.translated_text: The very unctuous <s>Vaṭikā</s> prepared with milk gives beauty and comfort, promotes thirst-quenching ability, removes fatigue, but is difficult to digest for those with weak digestive fire;

body.text: pittāsraṃ ca vināśayet tu satataṃ bhakṣyā supuṣṭipradā

children.translated_text: and this <s>Vaṭikā</s>, prepared soaked in ghee, kindles the fires of desire and digestion. || 13 ||

body.translated_text: it constantly destroys <s>Pitta</s> and blood disorders; this food is highly nourishing,
Oil-cooked <s>Kṣīravaṭikā</s> (milk cake):

children.translated_text: The very unctuous milk <s>Vaṭakas</s> bestow beauty, comfort, and strength;
those <s>Vaṭakas</s> made from meat and cooked in oil destroy <s>Vāta</s>. || 14 ||

body.translated_text: <s>Mudga-Vaṭaka</s> (mung bean fritters):

body.text: mūdgajātās tu ye kecit laghavo rucikārakāḥ /
body.translated_text: Those made from <s>Mudga</s> (mung bean) are light and promote appetite;
Those made from <s>Caṇaka</s> (chickpea) and similar:
Those made from <s>Caṇaka</s> and similar pulses are considered difficult to digest, light, and dry. || 15 ||
<s>Kāñjīka-Vaṭaka</s> (sour gruel fritters):

children.translated_text: Fritters made from meat and prepared in <s>Kāñjīka</s> (fermented gruel),
they destroy <s>Vāta</s>, promote appetite, are pleasing to the heart, but aggravate <s>Kapha</s> and <s>Pitta</s>. || 16 ||

body.translated_text: Prepared with <s>Rājikā</s> (mustard) powder:

children.text: rājīcūrṇe vimiśraḥ kaphapavanaharo rocano dīpanaḥ syān
children.translated_text: Mixed with mustard powder, it removes <s>Kapha</s> and <s>Vāta</s>, promotes appetite, and kindles the digestive fire;
it destroys weak digestion, pacifies fecal toxins, and digests all food;

children.text: kiṃ vā toyair vimiśro guḍalavaṇayutaḥ pittaraktādihantā
children.translated_text: moreover, when mixed with water and <s>Guḍa</s> (jaggery) and salt, it destroys <s>Pitta</s>, blood disorders, and similar ailments,
and removes thirst, fainting, spells, fever, and wind disorders, and destroys minor diseases. || 17 ||

body.text:
takraṃ komalaśṛṅgaberakalikākustuṃburīsaṃyutaṃ
yuktyāvartitam ardhaśoṣam aparaṃ bhāṇḍe sudhūpāvṛte /
havā [?] takramanoharāś ca vaṭakās teṣāṃ ruciṃ mārdavaṃ

children.text: svādaṃ saurabhabham udvahanty aharahaḥ tān vetti viśvambharā // 18 /
children.translated_text: flavor and fragrance daily — this the earth-bearer knows. || 18 ||

body.translated_text: <s>Takra</s> (buttermilk) combined with soft ginger, <s>Śṛṅgabera</s> (ginger) buds, and <s>Kustuṃburī</s> (coriander), skillfully churned, half-reduced, placed in a clean, fumigated vessel — those <s>Vaṭakas</s> prepared with buttermilk are delightful, and bestow appetite and softness,
Sour <s>Vaṭaka</s> (sour fritter):
Filled with cumin, <s>Bāhlīka</s> (asafoetida), fresh ginger, pepper, and <s>Sindhūttha</s> (rock salt), well-cooked, delicious, prepared by churning with yogurt and palmyra sugar,
mixed with oil extract, boiled and churned, and seasoned with its own flavors,
this sour <s>Vaṭaka</s> indeed destroys loss of appetite and pain. || 19 ||
Varieties of <s>Vaṭaka</s> (fritters):

children.translated_text: With <s>Kūṣmāṇḍa</s> (pumpkin), half-portion of pepper, <s>Sindhūttha</s> (rock salt), and <s>Methikā</s> (fenugreek),

children.text: piṣṭair māṣadalotthair vihitā vaṭakāś ca vaṭikāś ca // 20 //
children.translated_text: and with balls made from flour paste, both <s>Vaṭakas</s> and <s>Vaṭikās</s> are prepared. || 20 ||

body.translated_text: <s>Kohala-Vaḍā</s> (a type of fritter):
Wheat <s>Maṇḍaka</s> (flatbread):

children.translated_text: Fine wheat flour, covered and sealed, moistened with sweet water,
kneaded well by beautiful hands with oil, formed into round balls with fine dumplings,

children.text: antaḥ pātre sutapte karayugaracitā maṇḍakāḥ śvetadīrghā
children.translated_text: inside a well-heated vessel, the <s>Maṇḍakas</s> are fashioned by a pair of hands, white and elongated,
placed in vessels, sizzling and crackling, they are perfectly cooked. || 21 ||

children.text: te bhojyā bhaktayuktyā parivṛtasahitā mudgayūṣe vimiśrā
children.translated_text: They should be eaten with rice, accompanied by side dishes, mixed with <s>Mudga-Yūṣa</s> (mung bean soup),
or with <s>Āḍhakī</s> (pigeon pea) or lentils, with ghee-moistened meat sauces and <s>Jāṅgala</s> (wild game) and <s>Ānūpa</s> (marshy-region) meats;
in the early spring season, at the beginning of the second watch, this food is always wholesome,

children.text: gatrau kṣīrājyayuktā salila (lalita) narapater bhojanaṃ grīṣmakāle // 22 //
children.translated_text: and in summer, when prepared with milk and ghee, it is a delightful king's meal with water. || 22 ||

body.translated_text: Wheat <s>Maṇḍakas</s> promote appetite and are light, hot, and digestive-fire-kindling;
<s>Māṇḍepātiyā</s> (a preparation):
<s>Maṇḍakas</s> and <s>Maṇḍikās</s> are wholesome when cooked on embers. || 23 ||

body.text: atyuṣṇā maṇḍakā pathyā atiśītā guruḥ smṛtā /
body.translated_text: Very hot <s>Maṇḍakas</s> are wholesome; very cold ones are considered heavy;
those cooked in <s>Kukūla</s> (hot ashes), on a pan, or in an ember-grill or <s>Kandvāṅgāra</s> (ember pit). || 24 ||

children.translated_text: (One should know the <s>Apūpas</s> (cakes) of single or double grains, each successively better.)
They destroy blood disorders, aggravate <s>Pitta</s>, are sweet, and destroy <s>Vāta</s> (?);
when cooked on embers, wheat preparations are virilifying, digestive-fire-kindling, and aphrodisiac (?). || 26 ||

body.translated_text: Now, the properties of <s>Vaṭaka</s> (fritters) and other edible preparations:

children.text: bāhlījair māricair lavaṇapūḍu (lālavaṇapṛthu) tarair ārdrakaiḥ pūrṇagarbhaḥ
children.translated_text: Filled to the core with <s>Bāhlīka</s> (asafoetida), pepper, large and flat salt grains, and fresh ginger,

children.text: svinnaḥ śvāduḥ sugandhiḥ parimalabahulaḥ komalaḥ kuṅkumābhaḥ /
children.translated_text: steamed, delicious, fragrant, rich in aroma, soft, and saffron-colored,

children.text: kṣipto dantāntarāle murumuru kurute vyaktaśabdaṃ yathā vā
children.translated_text: when placed between the teeth, it makes a crunching 'muru-muru' sound distinctly,

children.text: dhanyo 'sau yat kapole praviśati vaṭakaḥ kāntayā prītidattaḥ // 27 //
children.translated_text: blessed is that <s>Vaṭaka</s> which enters the cheek, lovingly given by the beloved. || 27 ||

body.translated_text: <s>Koravaḍā</s> (a type of preparation):
Yogurt <s>Vaṭaka</s> (yogurt fritters):

children.translated_text: Those combined with <s>Śāli</s> (rice) flour pieces and yogurt are declared to be yogurt <s>Vaṭakas</s>;

children.text: ghoravātaśamanā rucipradāḥ pittam apy apaharanti dāruṇam // 28 //
children.translated_text: they powerfully pacify severe <s>Vāta</s>, promote appetite, and also remove <s>Pitta</s> severely. || 28 ||
Those made from <s>Caṇaka</s> (chickpea) and similar:
Preparations from <s>Caṇaka</s> and similar pulses are difficult to digest and greatly weaken the digestive fire;
they are light, promote appetite and digestive fire, when filled with <s>Māṣa</s> (black gram) and similar. || 29 ||

children.text: madhuraṃ madhurāmlaṃ tat tad eva prakaroti ca /
children.translated_text: That which is sweet or sweet-sour, that itself produces
aggravation of <s>Kapha</s> — thus is the filling of <s>Caṇaka</s> (chickpea) described. || 30 ||

body.translated_text: <s>Veṅgaṇī</s> (a preparation):
The experts call it <s>Veṣṭanikā</s> — well-cooked, wrapped in wheat flour, with <s>Dhana</s> (coriander), <s>Māṣa</s> (black gram), and <s>Mudga</s> (mung bean) filling;

body.text: tāṃ bhakṣayed atibalāṃ labhate (ramate) manuṣyas tailena vā saha ghṛtena sugandhinā vā // 31 //
body.translated_text: one who eats it gains great strength and delight, whether with oil or with fragrant ghee. || 31 ||

children.text: tāvad vargo 'tra bhakṣyāṇo (ṇāṃ) svadate sādhyate 'pi ca /
children.translated_text: Thus far is the group of edible foods (<s>bhakṣya</s>) here, which are tasty and also well-prepared,
hot, anointed with ghee, taken after bathing, and cooked over charcoal. // 32 //
Food prepared by mixing <s>guḍa</s> (jaggery) and wheat, cooked in oil,
produces <s>śleṣma</s> (phlegm) and <s>pitta</s> (bile), and removes <s>māruta</s> (wind). // 33 //

body.translated_text: On oil-fried preparations (<s>tailavaḍiyā</s>) —

children.translated_text: Those made from <s>śāli</s> (rice) are light, well-rounded, appetizing, and destroy <s>kapha</s> (phlegm);
those made from <s>śāli</s> (rice) and <s>mudga</s> (green gram) are heavy and appetizing. // 34 //

body.translated_text: On <s>śāli-mudga</s> pancakes (<s>pāpaḍa</s>) —

children.translated_text: <s>Pāyasa</s> (milk-pudding) causes distension, is strengthening, produces fat and <s>kapha</s> (phlegm), and is heavy;
<s>Kṛśarā</s> (rice-and-sesame porridge) produces <s>kapha</s> and <s>pitta</s>, is strengthening, and destroys <s>anila</s> (wind). // 35 //

children.text: taile vipakvā vaṭikāś ca śālibhiḥ sudurjarā rocanabhakṣaṇāś ca /
children.translated_text: Fried cakes (<s>vaṭikā</s>) cooked in oil with <s>śāli</s> (rice) are very difficult to digest and are appetizing foods;

children.text: kaphaprakopaṃ janayanti sadyo viśeṣataḥ kūravaḍā viśīrṇāḥ // 36 //
children.translated_text: they immediately provoke <s>kapha</s> (phlegm), especially the <s>kūravaḍā</s> variety which causes bloating. // 36 //

body.translated_text: On <s>kūravaḍā</s> preparations —

children.translated_text: <s>Saktu</s> (roasted barley flour) is nourishing, aphrodisiac, removes thirst, <s>pitta</s> (bile), and <s>kapha</s> (phlegm),
is appetizing, immediately strength-giving, purgative, and removes <s>pavana</s> (wind). // 37 //

body.translated_text: On <s>sātu</s> (roasted flour) —

children.translated_text: Food made from ground coriander seeds, and rice grains, are causes of worms;
the preparation made from rice grains is very difficult to digest, sweet in taste, and nourishing. // 38 //

body.translated_text: On rice-cake (<s>taṇḍulapīḍha</s>) —
// Thus ends the section on prepared foods (<s>kṛtānnavarga</s>) in the <s>Āyurvedamahodadhi</s> composed by <s>Suṣeṇa</s> //
// Now the properties of fruits are described //
First, the properties of <s>dāḍima</s> (pomegranate) —

children.translated_text: It pacifies the three <s>doṣas</s> (humors), is wholesome, aphrodisiac, sweet, and cooling,
destroys vomiting, loss of appetite, and thirst, and removes edema, <s>pitta</s> (bile), and fever. // 1 //
It pacifies burning sensation, cold affliction, and <s>pitta</s> (bile), and destroys all diseases;
the fully ripe fruit of <s>dāḍima</s> (pomegranate) bestows strength and complexion, and is pleasing to the heart. // 2 //
It has been declared by the learned as very sour, sweet, and possessing astringent qualities in taste,
pacifying in potency, removing wind, destroying <s>pitta</s> (bile), and kindling the digestive fire;

children.text: kiṃcit saṃgrahaṇaṃ kaphasya haraṇaṃ prāyo 'pi pāke punaḥ
children.translated_text: somewhat astringent and removing <s>kapha</s> (phlegm); moreover, in post-digestive effect,
thus is the <s>dāḍima</s> (pomegranate) renowned for its qualities through taste, potency, and post-digestive effect. // 3 //

children.text: dāḍimaṃ dvividham īḍitabhāryair amlam ekam aparaṃ maduraṃ ca /
children.translated_text: <s>Dāḍima</s> (pomegranate) is of two kinds as described by the ancients: one is sour and the other is sweet;

children.text: tatra vātakaphahāri kilāmlaṃ tāpahāri madhuraṃ laghu pathyam // 4 //
children.translated_text: of these, the sour one destroys <s>vāta</s> (wind) and <s>kapha</s> (phlegm), while the sweet one removes heat, is light, and wholesome. // 4 //
<s>Dāḍima</s> (pomegranate) is sweet, sour, and astringent, and destroys cough, <s>vāta</s> (wind), <s>kapha</s> (phlegm), and <s>pitta</s> (bile);

children.text: grāhi dīpanakaraṃ ca laghūṣṇaṃ śītalaṃ bhramahara rucidāyi // 5 //
children.translated_text: it is absorbent, kindles the digestive fire, is light, hot, cooling, removes dizziness, and promotes appetite. // 5 //

body.translated_text: Thus on <s>dāḍima</s> (pomegranate). //
Now the properties of <s>drākṣā</s> (grapes) —

body.text:
cakṣuṣyā raktapittaṃ śamayati madhurā śītavīryā vipāke
svāduḥ snigdhā kaṣāyā gururati ca tṛṣāśoṣadoṣāpahantrī /
drākṣā kṣīṇaru (kṣa)tānām apaharati vamīśvāsakāsajvarārtīs

children.translated_text: as well as bitter taste in the mouth and intoxication — among all fruits it is esteemed as the best. // 6 //

body.translated_text: Beneficial for the eyes, it pacifies <s>raktapitta</s> (bleeding disorders), is sweet, cooling in potency, sweet in post-digestive effect, unctuous, astringent, heavy, and removes thirst and the faults of <s>doṣas</s> (humors); <s>drākṣā</s> (grapes) remove the suffering of the emaciated, and cure vomiting, dyspnea, cough, and fever,
When fully ripe —

children.text: drākṣā saiva nu dhātuvṛddhijananī saṃtarpaṇī doṣahat
