children.translated_text: That very <s>drākṣā</s> (grape) promotes growth of bodily tissues (<s>dhātu</s>), is nourishing, destroys <s>doṣas</s> (humors),
removes thirst and distress, pacifies wind, and destroys vomiting and other diseases;

children.text: pāke 'amlā surasā rase ca madhurā (śītā) śāntā ca vīryeṇa sā
children.translated_text: sour in post-digestive effect, delicious in taste, sweet, and cooling in potency,

children.text: sā pakvā vihitā jvare ca kaphaje viṇmūtrasaṃśodhanī // 7 //
children.translated_text: that ripe grape is prescribed in <s>kapha</s>-type fever and purifies stool and urine. // 7 //

body.text:
śītā pitāsta(sra) doṣaṃ śamayati madhurā svādupākādi (ti) rucyā
cakṣuṣyā śvāsakāsaśramavamitra (śa)manī śoṣatṛṣṇājvaraghnī //
body.translated_text: It is cooling, pacifies <s>pitta</s> (bile) and blood disorders, is sweet, sweet in post-digestive effect, appetizing, beneficial for the eyes, pacifies dyspnea, cough, fatigue, and vomiting, and destroys desiccation, thirst, and fever;

children.text: drākṣā sukṣīṇavīryān api madanakarā kolā (kalākeli) dakṣān vidhatte // 8 //
children.translated_text: and <s>drākṣā</s> (grapes) even render the impotent capable of amorous play. // 8 //

body.translated_text: it removes burning, flatulence, fatigue and the like; the supreme dried ripe grape is nourishing,
Thus on <s>drākṣā</s> (grapes). //
Now the properties of <s>mātuliṅga</s> (citron) —

children.translated_text: The rind is bitter, pungent, removes <s>kapha</s> (phlegm) and worms, is unctuous, and destroys <s>anila</s> (wind);
the flesh is nourishing, pacifies <s>vāta</s> (wind) and <s>pitta</s> (bile), is aphrodisiac, and very difficult to digest;
the sour seed stimulates the digestive fire, removes dyspnea and cough,
and cures hiccups, vomiting, thirst, tastelessness, and indigestion — such is the product of <s>mātuliṅga</s> (citron). // 1 //

children.text: tiktā snigdhā bhavati kaṭukā mātuliṃgasya sā tvak
children.translated_text: The rind of <s>mātuliṅga</s> (citron) is bitter, unctuous, and pungent;

children.text: madhyaṃ snigdhaṃ ca (harati) madhuraṃ bṛṃhaṇaṃ vātapitte /
children.translated_text: the middle portion is unctuous, sweet, nourishing, and counteracts <s>vāta</s> (wind) and <s>pitta</s> (bile);

children.text: māṃsaṃ bhinnaṃ (snigdhaṃ) bhavati laghu tat kesaraṃ kāsahidhmā-
children.translated_text: the flesh when separated is unctuous and light; the seed cures cough and hiccups,
and conquers dyspnea, phlegm, wind, cold, and <s>gulma</s> (abdominal tumors) and colic caused by wind. // 10 //

children.text: sindhū (tthe) cchena ghanāgame (ca) vasitayā kāle śaratsaṃjñake
children.translated_text: In the rainy season it should be used with rock salt; in autumn with curd;
in winter with salt, fresh ginger, pepper, and mustard powder;

children.text: etais taiḥ śiśire madhāv api yutaṃ grīṣme guḍenānvitaṃ
children.translated_text: in the cool season with these same; in spring also combined thus; in summer with <s>guḍa</s> (jaggery) —

children.text: vaidyair bhūmipa sālu (mātu) liṃgam uditaṃ sarvartusādhāraṇam // 11 //
children.translated_text: thus physicians have declared, O king, that <s>mātuliṅga</s> (citron) is suitable for all seasons. // 11 //

body.translated_text: Now on <s>jambīra</s> (lemon) —

children.text: jambīram amlaṃ rasato vipāke vātāpahaṃ pittakaphapradaṃ ca /
children.translated_text: <s>Jambīra</s> (lemon) is sour in taste and post-digestive effect, removes <s>vāta</s> (wind), and aggravates <s>pitta</s> (bile) and <s>kapha</s> (phlegm);

children.text: annasya pārvanva (kaṃ tva) cireṇa kuryāt surocanaṃ vahnivivardhanaṃ ca // 12 //
children.translated_text: it promotes digestion of food gradually, greatly stimulates appetite, and increases the digestive fire. // 12 //

children.text: kaṭukamadhuram amlaṃ supratītaṃ raseṣu rucikaram udarāgner dīpanaṃ vātahāri /
children.translated_text: Pungent, sweet, and well-known as sour among the tastes, it promotes appetite, kindles the gastric fire, and removes <s>vāta</s> (wind);

children.text: nihata (harati) kaphasamīrau pittam āhanti vīryaṃ karaṇaphalam itīdaṃ vātapittaṃ vipakvam // 13 //
children.translated_text: it destroys <s>kapha</s> (phlegm) and wind, but aggravates <s>pitta</s> (bile) in potency — the fruit called <s>karaṇa</s> when ripe aggravates <s>vāta</s> and <s>pitta</s>. // 13 //

children.text: nimbūphalaṃ rocakam agnivṛddhiṃ karoti pittaṃ ca savātaraktam /
children.translated_text: The <s>nimbū</s> (lime) fruit promotes appetite and digestive fire, and removes <s>pitta</s> (bile) together with <s>vātarakta</s> (gout);

children.text: acākṣuṣaṃ śleṣmakaraṃ viśeṣāt bhuktānnapākaṃ kurute ca sadyaḥ // 14 //
children.translated_text: it is not beneficial for the eyes, especially produces <s>śleṣma</s> (phlegm), and immediately promotes digestion of eaten food. // 14 //

body.translated_text: (The <s>karaṇa</s> fruit is also not pleasing to the heart and promotes <s>raktapitta</s> (bleeding disorders).)

children.translated_text: <s>Nimbuka</s> (lime) destroys all worms, is sharp, sour, and said to remove abdominal diseases;
it is beneficial for <s>vāta</s>, <s>pitta</s>, <s>kapha</s>, colic, and thirst, and promotes appetite for spoiled grain. // 15 //

body.translated_text: Now on <s>nāraṅga</s> (orange) fruit —

children.text: nāraṅgasya phalaṃ balaṃ ca kurute susvādu hṛdyaṃ laghu
children.translated_text: The fruit of <s>nāraṅga</s> (orange) bestows strength, is very tasty, pleasing to the heart, and light,
excellent, kindles the digestive fire, pacifies acidity, and promotes digestion of eaten food;
it destroys all loss of appetite, removes fatigue, removes <s>vāta</s> (wind), and is nourishing;

children.text: bhuktvāpi pratibhakṣitaṃ na kurute kiṃcid vikāraṃ nṛṇām // 16 //
children.translated_text: even after eating, a second meal causes no disorder whatsoever in people. // 16 //

body.text: īṣadrase madhuraśītalam amlatiktaṃ vīryodgamāc chamanadīpanapācanaṃ ca

children.text: ārvedayati (?) kaphapittaharaṃ vipāke nāraṅgakaṃ phalam udāradhiyo munīndrāḥ // 17 //
children.translated_text: the great sages of noble intellect declare the <s>nāraṅga</s> (orange) fruit to be <s>kapha</s> and <s>pitta</s>-destroying in post-digestive effect. // 17 //

body.translated_text: Slightly sweet and cooling in taste, sour-bitter, pacifying, appetite-stimulating, and digestive in potency,
Now on <s>madhukarkaṭī</s> (sweet melon) —

children.text: susvādu pāke rasataś ca raktapittaprakopaṃ vilayanti māndye (?) /
children.translated_text: Very tasty in post-digestive effect and in taste, it alleviates <s>raktapitta</s> (bleeding disorders) and sluggishness;

children.text: dāhajvaraṃ nāśayatīti nityaṃ prāhuś ca vaidyā madhukarkaṭī ca // 18 //
children.translated_text: it always destroys burning sensation and fever — thus physicians describe <s>madhukarkaṭī</s> (sweet melon). // 18 //

body.translated_text: Now on <s>mocā</s> (banana) fruit —

children.text: mocaṃ svādurasaṃ vipākamadhuraṃ vīryeṇa śītaṃ jaḍaṃ
children.translated_text: <s>Moca</s> (banana) is sweet in taste, sweet in post-digestive effect, cooling and dense in potency,

children.text: pittaghnaṃ tv anilāpahaṃ gurutaraṃ pathyaṃ na mande 'nale /
children.translated_text: destroys <s>pitta</s> (bile), removes wind, is very heavy, and is not wholesome when the digestive fire is weak;
it immediately increases eaten food, removes exhaustion and thirst, and bestows peace;
for one with strong digestive fire, it gives comfort, removes diseases of <s>kapha</s>, and is nourishing for living beings. // 19 //

body.translated_text: Now on <s>nālikerī</s> (coconut) fruit —

body.text:
snigdhaṃ svādurasaṃ vipākamadhuraṃ hṛdyaṃ jaraṃ(ḍa) durjaraṃ
pittaghnaṃ krimivardhanaṃ madakaraṃ vātāmayadhvaṃsanam /
āmaśleṣmavikopanaṃ praśamanaṃ vahner bhramadhvaṃsanaṃ
kandarpasya balaṃ dadāti nitarāṃ tan nālikerīphalam
body.translated_text: The <s>nālikerī</s> (coconut) fruit is unctuous, sweet in taste, sweet in post-digestive effect, pleasing to the heart, difficult to digest, destroys <s>pitta</s> (bile), increases worms, is intoxicating, and destroys diseases of <s>vāta</s> (wind); it aggravates <s>āma</s> (undigested matter) and <s>śleṣma</s> (phlegm), pacifies the digestive fire, removes dizziness, and abundantly bestows the strength of <s>Kandarpa</s> (the god of love).
On coconut water (<s>nālikerodaka</s>) —

children.translated_text: Very tasty, aphrodisiac, light, appetite-stimulating, dry, and cooling, it removes <s>vāta</s> (wind) and <s>pitta</s> (bile) and purifies the bladder;

children.text: syān nārikelasalilaṃ śaśikānti pathyaṃ pittajvarasya viṣahāri vadanti vaidyāḥ // 20 //
children.translated_text: coconut water, radiant as moonlight, is wholesome, and physicians declare it removes poison and fever caused by <s>pitta</s>. // 20 //

body.translated_text: Now on <s>bhavya</s> (Dillenia indica) fruit —

children.text: bhavyaṃ bhavyataraṃ svādu kiñcid amlaṃ surocanam /
children.translated_text: <s>Bhavya</s> is most excellent, tasty, slightly sour, and very appetizing;
it destroys <s>vāta</s> (wind), removes discomfort and nausea, and kindles the digestive fire. // 21 //

body.translated_text: Now on <s>āmalakī</s> (Indian gooseberry) fruit —

children.text: karamara (?) hanti (vātaṃ tad amlatvāt) vātadamlaṃ cātpittaṃ mādhuryaśaity ataḥ /
children.translated_text: It destroys <s>vāta</s> (wind) due to its sourness, <s>pitta</s> (bile) due to its sweetness and cooling nature,
and <s>kapha</s> (phlegm) due to its dryness and astringency — thus the fruit of <s>dhātrī</s> (gooseberry) conquers the three <s>doṣas</s> (humors). // 22 //
somewhat sweet in taste, sweet in post-digestive effect, and destroying the three <s>doṣas</s> (humors);
it cures urinary diseases, pacifies <s>prameha</s> (diabetes), and breaks distension,
beneficial whether eaten before or after food, always of ambrosial taste, and wholesome — such is <s>dhātrī</s> (gooseberry) fruit. // 23 //

body.translated_text: {cf. <s>Bhāvamiśra</s>: <s>Bhāvaprakāśa</s> 41}

children.text: rūkṣaṃ svādu kaṣāyam amlakaṭukaṃ snigdhaṃ suse (?) rocanaṃ
children.translated_text: Dry, sweet, astringent, sour, pungent, unctuous, and very appetizing,

children.text: cakṣuṣyaṃ balavarṇadaṃ dhṛtikaraṃ vṛṣyaṃ ca buddhipradam /
children.translated_text: beneficial for the eyes, bestowing strength and complexion, promoting fortitude, aphrodisiac, and conferring intelligence;
destroying itching and leprosy, removing fever, and eliminating thirst, burning, and heat,
in short, <s>dhātrī</s> (gooseberry) fruit pacifies the three <s>doṣas</s> (humors) for all living beings. // 24 //

children.text: tridhāphale (dhātrīphalaṃ) dinaṃ (tadvini) hanti mehān arocakādīn vividhān vikārān /
children.translated_text: The <s>dhātrī</s> (gooseberry) fruit taken daily destroys <s>meha</s> (urinary disorders), loss of appetite, and various diseases;

children.text: amlaṃ ca (mlatva) mādhuryakaṣāyataḥ kramāt doṣatrayaghnaṃ laghu śītavīryam // 25 //
children.translated_text: sour, and due to its sweetness and astringency in succession, it destroys the three <s>doṣas</s>, is light, and cooling in potency. // 25 //

body.translated_text: On old <s>āmalaka</s> (dried gooseberry) fruit —

children.text: pānī ya (?) malakaṃ (prācīnāmalakaṃ) vṛṣyaṃ svādu hṛdyaṃ kaphāpaham /
children.translated_text: Old <s>āmalaka</s> (dried gooseberry) is aphrodisiac, tasty, pleasing to the heart, and removes <s>kapha</s> (phlegm);
it is cooling, aphrodisiac, life-prolonging, and supremely removes burning and fever. // 26 //

body.translated_text: Now on <s>āmra</s> (mango) fruit —

children.translated_text: When unripe, it generates <s>pitta</s> (bile), <s>kapha</s> (phlegm), blood discharge, and <s>vāta</s> (wind); the stone produces similar effects;
when ripe, it is sweet in taste, pacifies the three <s>doṣas</s> (humors), and nourishes the emaciated body;
it promotes growth of bodily tissues (<s>dhātu</s>), is sweet in post-digestive effect, nourishing, and bestows radiance,
prevents thirst and desiccation, promotes appetite — <s>āmra</s> (mango) is the best among fruits. // 27 //

children.text: santarpaṇīyaḥ sakalendriyāṇāṃ balaprado vṛṣyatamaś ca hṛdyaḥ /
children.translated_text: It is nourishing, beneficial for all sense organs, bestows strength, is most aphrodisiac, and pleasing to the heart;

children.text: strīṣu praharṣaṃ vipulaṃ dadāti phalādhirājaḥ sahakāra eva // 28 //
children.translated_text: it gives abundant delight among women — the king of fruits is indeed the <s>sahakāra</s> (grafted mango). // 28 //

children.text: āmraṃ pākasya kāle madhuram iha raseneṣad amlaṃ ca hṛdyaṃ
children.translated_text: The <s>āmra</s> (mango) at the time of ripening is sweet in taste, slightly sour, and pleasing to the heart,

children.text: retovṛddhiṃ vidhatte śamayati pavanaṃ pācanaṃ dīpanaṃ ca /
children.translated_text: it promotes increase of semen, pacifies wind, aids digestion and kindles appetite;

children.text: ānandaṃ saṃdadhāti pratidiśati balaṃ vīryataḥ suśrutādyāḥ
children.translated_text: it bestows bliss, grants strength through potency — <s>Suśruta</s> and other authorities

children.text: vikhyātāḥ sarvaloke hy atijanitakaphaṃ durjaraṃ kīrtayanti // 29 //
children.translated_text: well-known in the world declare that it excessively produces <s>kapha</s> (phlegm) and is difficult to digest. // 29 //

children.text: yat kāminyadharovṛṣaṃ (ṣṭhasaṃ)bhṛtam iti khyātaṃ viśiṣṭair buddhaiḥ
children.translated_text: That which is renowned by the wise as resembling the nectar of a beloved woman's lips,

children.text: yad daityapramukhaiḥ prayatnanirataiḥ kṛṣṭaṃ suraiḥ sāgarāt /
children.translated_text: that which was churned from the ocean with great effort by <s>Daityas</s> (demons) and <s>Suras</s> (gods),

children.text: yan nānārucibhiḥ svabhāvasadṛśaṃ khyātaṃ ca mithyaiva tat
children.translated_text: that which is famous for various delightful tastes and beautiful by nature — yet all that is merely illusory compared to this,
for the <s>pīyūṣa</s> (ambrosia) that removes all doubt is indeed created in the form of <s>rasāla</s> (mango preparation). // 30 //

body.translated_text: Now on <s>kapittha</s> (wood-apple) fruit —

children.translated_text: Unripe <s>kapittha</s> (wood-apple) removes itching of the throat, causes numbness of the tongue,
aggravates the three <s>doṣas</s> (humors), removes poison, is astringent, and appetizing;
when ripe, it has the power to remove dyspnea, vomiting, fatigue, exhaustion, thirst, and hiccups,

children.text: sarvaṃ grāhi viṣāpahaṃ ca kathitaṃ sevyaṃ tataḥ sarvadā // 31 //
children.translated_text: is wholly astringent and removes poison — thus it is described as fit to be consumed at all times. // 31 //

body.translated_text: On <s>phanāsa</s> (jackfruit) —

children.translated_text: <s>Phanāsa</s> (jackfruit) is difficult to digest, sweet-sour, and destroys <s>vāta</s> (wind) and <s>pitta</s> (bile);
it removes <s>vāta</s> (wind) and <s>pitta</s> (bile), is heavy, and weakens the digestive fire. // 32 //

children.text: madhurā bṛṃhaṇī vṛṣyā pittalā tvak truṭipradā /
children.translated_text: The pulp is sweet, nourishing, aphrodisiac, and bilious; the rind promotes thirst;

children.text: pittaghnī svāduhṛdyā ca mañjety āhur guṇottamāḥ // 33 //
children.translated_text: it destroys <s>pitta</s>, is tasty and pleasing to the heart — those who know its excellent qualities call it <s>mañja</s>. // 33 //
Astringent-sweet, dry, pungent, and producing <s>śleṣma</s> (phlegm);
it is astringent, difficult to digest, causes numbness of the tongue, is cold, and heavy. // 34 //

body.translated_text: On <s>ṭeṃbaru</s> (Diospyros) —
Now the properties of <s>karamarda</s> (Carissa carandas) —

children.translated_text: <s>Karamarda</s> is very sweet when fully ripe, and also sour in taste;
it pacifies <s>vāta</s> (wind) and <s>pitta</s> (bile), and destroys <s>śleṣma</s> (phlegm) and worms. // 65 //

body.translated_text: On <s>karaveda</s> (curry leaf fruit) —
Now the properties of <s>ciñcā</s> (tamarind) —

children.translated_text: The ripe fruit of <s>amlikā</s> (tamarind) greatly promotes <s>raktapitta</s> (bleeding disorders);
the ash of its bark is astringent and hot, and removes <s>kapha</s> (phlegm), worms, and <s>anila</s> (wind). // 36 //

body.translated_text: On <s>ciñcā</s> (tamarind) —
Now the properties of <s>bhallātaka</s> (marking nut / almond) —

children.translated_text: The skin and flesh of <s>bhallātaka</s> is nourishing, sweet, and cooling;
its stone is equal to fire, promotes intellect, and supremely removes <s>kapha</s> (phlegm) and <s>vāta</s> (wind). // 37 //

body.translated_text: On <s>biṃbadāma</s> (almond) —
Now on <s>kharjūra</s> (date) —

children.translated_text: <s>Kharjūra</s> (date) pacifies <s>raktapitta</s> (bleeding disorders), is sweet, sweet in post-digestive effect, and very cooling,
it removes thirst and desiccation, and cures irregular fevers, intoxication, pain, dyspnea, and hiccups.

children.text: snigdho vṛṣyo balāsaṃ janayati nitarāṃ vahnimāndyaṃ vidhatte
children.translated_text: Unctuous and <s>vṛṣya</s> (aphrodisiac), it generates <s>balāsa</s> (phlegmatic disorder) excessively and causes dullness of the digestive fire,

children.text: kāntiṃ vai puṣṭiyuttyā vapuṣi samadhikaṃ mūtrakṛcchraṃ nihanti // 38 //
children.translated_text: yet it bestows radiance with nourishment to the body exceedingly, and destroys <s>mūtrakṛcchra</s> (dysuria). // 38 //
The middle portion of dates and <s>kharjūra</s> (dried dates) is said to be of the same kind,

children.text: viśeṣād ūrdhvage rakte dāhe pitte ca śasyate // 39 //
children.translated_text: and especially when there is upward-moving blood, burning, and <s>pitta</s> (bile), it is recommended. // 39 //

body.translated_text: Now, the fruit of <s>sindī</s> (jujube).

children.translated_text: <s>Sindola</s> (jujube) pacifies <s>kapha</s> (phlegm), <s>vāta</s> (wind), and <s>pitta</s> (bile), removes <s>raktātisāra</s> (bloody diarrhea),
alleviates skin diseases, <s>bhagandarā</s> (fistula-in-ano), and <s>arśas</s> (hemorrhoids), and sharply cuts <s>aśmarī</s> (urinary calculi);
it is always beneficial in <s>hṛdroga</s> (heart diseases), strength-giving, and kindles <s>kāma</s> (desire) and <s>agni</s> (digestive fire),

children.text: kāse kṣīṇavirecane jvaragate (de) śastaṃ ca sindīphalam // 40 //
children.translated_text: and in <s>kāsa</s> (cough) and for emaciation and purgation, and in fever, the fruit of <s>sindī</s> is praised. // 40 //

body.translated_text: Now, the fruit of the golden <s>kadalī</s> (plantain).

children.text: suvarṇamocā kaphapitta [vāta] hāriṇī viṣṭambhinī dīpanakāriṇī ca /
children.translated_text: The golden <s>mocā</s> (plantain) removes <s>kapha</s> (phlegm), <s>pitta</s> (bile), and <s>vāta</s> (wind), is constipating, and kindles the digestive fire;
it is difficult to digest, and removes burning sensation,
and it certainly pacifies blood together with <s>pitta</s> (bile). // 41 //

body.translated_text: <s>Utatī</s> (wild plantain) — variant reading.

children.translated_text: Slightly astringent and sweet, it subdues <s>vāta</s> (wind) and <s>pitta</s> (bile),

children.text: balyā vṛṣyā ca hṛdyā ca viśeṣād utatī guruḥ // 49 //
children.translated_text: is strengthening, <s>vṛṣya</s> (aphrodisiac), and <s>hṛdya</s> (cordial); especially, <s>utatī</s> is heavy. // 49 //

body.translated_text: Now, the fruit of the <s>pippala</s> (sacred fig tree).

children.text: aśvavatthavṛkṣasya phalāni pathyāny atīva hṛdyāni suśītalāni /
children.translated_text: The fruits of the <s>aśvattha</s> (sacred fig) tree are wholesome, exceedingly <s>hṛdya</s> (cordial), and very cooling;

children.text: nighnanti pittaṃ saha śoṇitena dāhaṃ tṛṣāṃ chardim arocakaṃ ca // 43 //
children.translated_text: they destroy <s>pitta</s> (bile) along with blood, burning, thirst, vomiting, and loss of appetite. // 43 //

body.translated_text: [They cure disorders of <s>pitta</s> (bile) and blood, pain, burning, thirst, vomiting, swelling, loss of appetite, and faults.]
The fruit of <s>udumbara</s> (cluster fig).

body.text: audumbaraṃ phalam atīva suśītalaṃ ca sadyo nivārayati śoṇitapittam ugram // 44 //
body.translated_text: The fruit of <s>audumbara</s> (cluster fig) is exceedingly cooling and immediately arrests severe <s>śoṇitapitta</s> (bleeding disorders). // 44 //
Now, the fruit of <s>umbī</s> (a variety of fig).
It causes very severe obstruction of urine, and especially promotes the mixing of blood and wind.
Now, the fruit of <s>rājakośātakī</s> (pointed gourd variety).

children.translated_text: <s>Surājakośātakī</s> destroys <s>pitta</s> (bile), and in severe diseases, in poisoning and alcoholic intoxication,

children.text: śramaklame mehabhagandare ca vraṇeṣu pitteṣv api nityapathyam // 45 //
children.translated_text: in fatigue and exhaustion, in <s>meha</s> (urinary disorders) and <s>bhagandara</s> (fistula-in-ano), and in wounds and in conditions of <s>pitta</s> (bile), it is always wholesome. // 45 //

body.translated_text: Now, the fruit of <s>sirākośātakī</s> (ridge gourd).

children.translated_text: <s>Sirākośātakī</s> removes <s>pitta</s> (bile) and destroys <s>kṣuttṛḍ</s> (hunger and thirst);
it is beneficial in <s>meha</s> (urinary disorders), always removes burning, and destroys vomiting caused by <s>pitta</s> (bile). // 46 //

body.translated_text: Thus ends the <s>phalavarga</s> (chapter on fruits) in the <s>Āyurvedamahodadhi</s> composed by <s>Suṣeṇa</s>.
Now, the <s>śākavarga</s> (chapter on vegetables).

children.text: phalaṃ parthyāgataṃ śākam āśuṣkaṃ taruṇaṃ navam /
children.translated_text: <s>Śāka</s> (vegetable) is that which grows on trees as fruit, fresh, young, and new —

children.text: patraṃ puṣpaṃ phalaṃ nālaṃ kandaṃ saṃsvedajaṃ tathā // 1 //
children.translated_text: leaf, flower, fruit, stalk, and tuber, as well as that which grows by steaming. // 1 //

children.text: śākaṃ ṣaḍvidham uddiṣṭaṃ sarvaṃ vidyād yathottaram /
children.translated_text: <s>Śāka</s> (vegetables) are declared to be of six kinds; one should know that each succeeding type is superior;
all vegetables should be understood as not to be eaten with goat's milk, and are beneficial for people. // 2 //

body.translated_text: Elsewhere, the well-balanced seasonal vegetable <s>punarnavā</s> (Boerhavia diffusa) is mentioned.
Now, the properties of <s>taṇḍulīyaka</s> (Amaranthus).

children.translated_text: Cool, dry, exceedingly light, it removes <s>pitta</s> (bile) and blood disorders,

children.text: svāduḥ pāke bhavati ca rase svādur evātihṛdyaḥ /
children.translated_text: sweet in <s>vipāka</s> (post-digestive taste) and sweet in <s>rasa</s> (taste), it is exceedingly <s>hṛdya</s> (cordial);
it destroys diseases arising from irregular poisoning and aggravation of <s>śleṣma</s> (phlegm) and <s>vāta</s> (wind),
and immediately dispels marrow and barley afflictions — <s>taṇḍulīya</s> (Amaranthus) is extremely wholesome. // 3 //

children.text: rase vipāke madhuro 'tiśīto rūkṣas tuṣāraḥ kaphanāśanaś ca /
children.translated_text: Sweet in taste and <s>vipāka</s> (post-digestive effect), very cooling, dry, cold, and destroying <s>kapha</s> (phlegm);

children.text: sadāhapittaṃ rudhiraṃ viṣaṃ ca viśeṣato hanti ca taṇḍulīyaḥ //
children.translated_text: it especially destroys <s>pitta</s> (bile) with burning, blood, and poison — thus is <s>taṇḍulīya</s>.

body.translated_text: Now, <s>vāstuka</s> (Chenopodium) and <s>cillī</s> vegetable.

children.text: vāstuko 'gnikaro rase ca madhuraḥ pittāpahaś cākṣuṣaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Vāstuka</s> kindles the digestive fire, is sweet in taste, removes <s>pitta</s> (bile), and is good for the eyes,
unctuous, destroys <s>vāta</s> (wind), removes worms, and eliminates disorders of <s>kuṣṭha</s> (skin diseases);
it purifies the stool and urine, and is an expellant of <s>śleṣma</s> (phlegmatic) diseases,

children.text: śākānām api yo [co]ttamo laghutaraḥ pathyaḥ sadā prāṇīnām // 5 //
children.translated_text: and among all vegetables, it is the best, very light, and always wholesome for living beings. // 5 //
Among all varieties of <s>vāstuka</s>, the thorny <s>vāstuka</s> is recommended;

children.text: cillir vāstukavajñeyā tato nyūnā ca kiṃcana // 6 //
children.translated_text: <s>Cillī</s> is to be known as similar to <s>vāstuka</s>, but somewhat inferior. // 6 //
With alkaline properties, it conquers worms, pacifies the three <s>doṣas</s> (humors), kindles the digestive fire, and is digestive,
good for the eyes, sweet, laxative, appetite-promoting, removes flatulence and colic;
it purifies stool and urine, improves the voice, is unctuous, and in <s>vipāka</s> (post-digestive effect) is pungent —
thus <s>vāstuka</s> pacifies all diseases, and <s>cillī</s> is likewise excellent. // 7 //

body.translated_text: <s>Cillitākavalā</s> — variant reading.
Now, <s>śigru</s> (drumstick) vegetable.

children.text: kaphasya vātasya śamaṃ karoti uṣṇaṃ ca pittaṃ kurute 'gnidīptim /
children.translated_text: It pacifies <s>kapha</s> (phlegm) and <s>vāta</s> (wind), is hot, aggravates <s>pitta</s> (bile), kindles the digestive fire,

children.text: hṛdyaṃ krimighnaṃ ca surocakaṃ ca ādhmānaviḍbandhavināśanaṃ ca // 8 //
children.translated_text: is <s>hṛdya</s> (cordial), destroys worms, promotes appetite, and eliminates flatulence and constipation. // 8 //

body.translated_text: <s>Śigru</s> vegetable
Now, <s>rājakā</s> (mustard greens).

children.translated_text: <s>Rājikā</s> (mustard) destroys <s>kapha</s> (phlegm) and wind disorders, promotes appetite, kindles the digestive fire, and is not <s>hṛdya</s> (cordial);

children.text: kaṃva hṛdyam iva [kaṇṭharukkrimivi]nāśanakartrī uṣṇavīryam upahanti ca śūlam // 9 //
children.translated_text: it is somewhat like a cordial, destroys throat afflictions and worms, has hot potency, and alleviates colic. // 9 //

body.translated_text: Heavy in digestion — variant reading.
Now, <s>śatapuṣpā</s> (dill).

children.translated_text: <s>Śatapuṣpā</s> (dill) destroys <s>vāta</s> (wind), removes <s>śūla</s> (colic), <s>gulma</s> (abdominal tumors), and abdominal distension,
it is especially a digestive stimulant, and slightly aggravates <s>pitta</s> (bile). // 10 //

body.translated_text: Now, <s>kustumbarī</s> (coriander).

children.text: sugandhir vātapittaghnī laghvī rucyā jvare hitā /
children.translated_text: Fragrant, it destroys <s>vāta</s> (wind) and <s>pitta</s> (bile), is light, appetizing, and beneficial in fever;
fresh <s>kustumbarī</s> (coriander) is remembered as cooling, an ornament to dishes. // 11 //

body.translated_text: Now, <s>rājavallī</s> (a creeper vegetable).

children.text: balyā vṛṣyā ca kaṇṭhyā kaphapavanaharā syāt tridoṣe praśastā
children.translated_text: Strengthening, <s>vṛṣya</s> (aphrodisiac), good for the throat, it removes <s>kapha</s> (phlegm) and <s>pavana</s> (wind), and is praised in the three <s>doṣas</s> (humors),
light, it alleviates excessive urination, controls vomiting, and destroys <s>kṛcchra</s> (dysuria);

children.text: pittodreke ca rakte viṣamaviṣaharī dīpanī śākaśreṣṭhā [varyā]
children.translated_text: in excess of <s>pitta</s> (bile) and blood, it removes irregular poisons, is a digestive stimulant, and the best among vegetables,
<s>Rājavallī</s>, among leaf vegetables, promotes the growth of fruits and tender shoots. // 12 //

body.translated_text: Now, <s>kusumbhī</s> (safflower greens).

children.text: dṛṣṭiprasādaṃ kurute viśeṣād rucipradaṃ dīptikaraṃ ca vahneḥ /
children.translated_text: It especially bestows clarity of vision, promotes appetite, and kindles the digestive fire;
<s>Kausumbha</s> (safflower) vegetable is declared the best, removing disorders of feces and urine, and destroying impurities. // 13 //

body.translated_text: Now, <s>sārṣapa</s> (mustard greens).

children.text: atyuṣṇavīrya kurute 'gnidīptiṃ raktaṃ sapittaṃ tv atha kaṇṭharogam /
children.translated_text: Of very hot potency, it kindles the digestive fire, but aggravates blood together with <s>pitta</s> (bile) and causes throat diseases;

children.text: acākṣuṣaṃ śukrakaraṃ vidāhi na sārṣapaṃ śākam idaṃ hi pathyam // 14 //
children.translated_text: it is not good for the eyes, is <s>śukrakara</s> (semen-producing), and causes burning — this <s>sārṣapa</s> (mustard) vegetable is not wholesome. // 14 //

body.translated_text: Now, <s>vārtāka</s> (eggplant).
// <s>Sadāśiva</s> (?) //

body.text:
sakṣāraṃ kaphapitta (vāta) hāri malakṛdvahnes tu saṃdīpanaṃ
tiktoṣṇaṃ madhuraṃ tathā kaṭurasaṃ tv īṣac ca pittapradam /
hṛdyaṃ vātavikiṃ na madyapathyam api tat dravye va sarve punaḥ (?)
(hṛdyaṃ rucyam apittalaṃ kapham aruñjitsarvaśākottamaṃ)

children.text: vārtākaṃ paripūrṇajātasarasaṃ bālaṃ na pakvaṃ hitam // 15 ///
children.translated_text: <s>vārtāka</s> (eggplant) that is fully ripe and juicy, young and not overripe, is beneficial. // 15 //
<s>Vārtāka</s> (eggplant) destroys <s>kapha</s> (phlegm) and <s>vāta</s> (wind), and slightly aggravates <s>pitta</s> (bile);

children.text: sarasaṃ mūtralaṃ proktaṃ balakṛdbālam eva tat // 16 //
children.translated_text: when juicy, it is diuretic, and it is said to be strength-giving when young. // 16 //
Prepared with salt, pepper, and powder, cooked properly over fire, greatly pleasing like a jackal's favorite,

children.text: harati pavanamādyaṃ śleṣmahantṛ prasiddhaṃ jaṭharabharaṇayojyaṃ cāru bhojyaṃ bharītam // 17 //
children.translated_text: it powerfully removes <s>pavana</s> (wind) and is well known as a destroyer of <s>śleṣma</s> (phlegm) — <s>bharīta</s> (stuffed eggplant) is a delightful food suitable for those with abdominal heaviness. // 17 //

body.translated_text: <s>Vṛntāka bharita</s> (stuffed eggplant).
Now, the fruit of <s>bimbī</s> (Coccinia grandis).

children.text: bimbīphalaṃ svādu śītaṃ stambhena lepa(kha)naṃ guru /
children.translated_text: The fruit of <s>bimbī</s> is sweet, cooling, astringent, scraping, and heavy;
it destroys <s>pitta</s> (bile), blood disorders, burning, and swelling, and causes <s>vāta</s> (wind), flatulence, and constipation. // 18 //

body.translated_text: The fruit of <s>bimbī</s>.
Now, the fruit of <s>pharkoṭī</s> (bitter gourd variety).

children.text: tiktaṃ sutīvraṃ madhuraṃ tathāmlaṃ vātāpahaṃ pittavināśanaṃ ca /
children.translated_text: Bitter, very sharp, sweet, and also sour, it removes <s>vāta</s> (wind) and destroys <s>pitta</s> (bile),

children.text: śleṣmākaraṃ cetanapātanaṃ (dīpanapācanaṃ) ca koṭībhavaṃ cāgnikaraṃ narāṇām // 19 //
children.translated_text: it produces <s>śleṣma</s> (phlegm), is a digestive stimulant, and the product of <s>koṭī</s> kindles the digestive fire for people. // 19 //
The fruit of <s>karkoṭikā</s> (spiny gourd) removes <s>gulma</s> (abdominal tumors), <s>śūla</s> (colic), <s>pitta</s> (bile), and <s>kapha</s> (phlegm);
it destroys the three <s>doṣas</s> (humors), <s>meha</s> (urinary disorders), and <s>kuṣṭha</s> (skin diseases), and is slightly sweet and bitter. // 20 //

body.translated_text: It cures <s>kāsa</s> (cough), <s>śvāsa</s> (dyspnea), and fever, is a supreme destroyer of <s>mārutā</s> (wind), and is light.
<s>Kaṅkoḍā</s> — variant reading.
Now, the properties of <s>mūlaka</s> (radish).

children.text: kiṃcit kṣāraṃ satiktaṃ kaṭukarasayutaṃ mūtralaṃ doṣahāri
children.translated_text: Somewhat alkaline, slightly bitter, with pungent taste, diuretic, and removing the <s>doṣas</s> (humors),
excellent in <s>gulma</s> (abdominal tumors) and consumption, and in severe <s>śvāsa</s> (dyspnea) and <s>kāsa</s> (cough) conditions;

children.text: kaṇṭhyaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ svarāṇām apaharati rujaṃ netrarogāpahāri
children.translated_text: good for the throat, excellent for the voice, it removes pain and cures eye diseases —

children.text: syād evaṃ bālamūlaṃ mahad api ca hitaṃ snigdhapākaṃ (pakvaṃ) samīre // 21 //
children.translated_text: thus young <s>mūlaka</s> (radish) is such, and the mature one too is beneficial, unctuous when cooked, in wind disorders. // 21 //

body.translated_text: // <s>Mūlā</s> (radish) — variant reading. //
Now, <s>sūraṇa</s> (elephant foot yam).

children.translated_text: Appetizing, a digestive stimulant, destroyer of worms, kindling a sluggish digestive fire,
<s>hṛdya</s> (cordial), producing <s>śleṣma</s> (phlegm), light, strength-giving, and destroying hemorrhoids;
it makes even the blind see, removes <s>śvāsa</s> (dyspnea) and <s>kāsa</s> (cough),

children.text: cākṣuṣyo 'pi ca (sū) s taraṇaḥ smṛtikaro hṛtpārśvaśūlāpahaḥ //
children.translated_text: is good for the eyes, and that <s>sūraṇa</s> (elephant foot yam) improves memory and removes pain in the heart and sides.

body.translated_text: <s>Sūraṇa</s> (elephant foot yam).
Now, <s>bhūkanda</s> (a type of tuber) and <s>piṇḍālu</s> (a type of yam).

body.text:
bhūkandas tv ativātalo balakaraḥ śleṣmāṇam atyarthakṛt
viṣṭambhī gurumedaso 'pi viṣamo vātāmayān kārakaḥ /
mehaṃ kuṣṭharujaṃ karoti satataṃ tad vātaraktaṃ haret
piṇḍāluḥ kṛmikoṣṭhakṛcchram apahṛt pittāmayadhvaṃsakaḥ (yottejanaḥ)
body.translated_text:
<s>Bhūkanda</s> is extremely aggravating to <s>vāta</s> (wind), strength-giving, producing <s>śleṣma</s> (phlegm) excessively,
constipating, heavy, and also increasing fat, causing <s>vāta</s> (wind) disorders;
it constantly causes <s>meha</s> (urinary disorders) and <s>kuṣṭha</s> (skin disease) pain, yet it removes <s>vātarakta</s> (gouty conditions);
<s>piṇḍālu</s> removes worm-caused <s>kuṣṭha</s> (skin disease) and <s>kṛcchra</s> (dysuria), and destroys <s>pitta</s> (bile) diseases.
// <s>Piṇḍālu</s> (yam). //
Now, fresh <s>ārdraka</s> (ginger).

children.text: ārdraṃ dīpanapācanaṃ rucikaraṃ vṛṣyaṃ kaduṣṇaṃ varaṃ
children.translated_text: Fresh <s>ārdraka</s> (ginger) is a digestive stimulant, promotes appetite, is <s>vṛṣya</s> (aphrodisiac), pungent, hot, and excellent;
it entirely produces fat, removes <s>kapha</s> (phlegmatic) diseases, reduces swelling, and conquers colic;
it cleanses the tongue and throat; with salt, it is always wholesome when eating,
and when ground with neem water, it removes <s>kapha</s> (phlegm) and is a digestive stimulant. // 24 //
When combined with neem and ocean salt, <s>ārdraka</s> (ginger) removes blood and <s>pitta</s> (bile);
it is a digestive stimulant, appetite-promoting, <s>hṛdya</s> (cordial), and removes the three <s>doṣas</s> (humors). // 25 //

body.translated_text: // <s>Ārdraka</s> (ginger). //
Now, the properties of the tubers of <s>kumuda</s> (white water lily), <s>utpala</s> (blue lotus), and <s>padma</s> (lotus).

children.translated_text: The tubers of <s>kumuda</s> (white water lily), <s>utpala</s> (blue lotus), and <s>padma</s> (lotus) aggravate <s>māruta</s> (wind);
they are astringent, pacify <s>pitta</s> (bile), are sweet in <s>vipāka</s> (post-digestive effect), and cooling. // 26 //
<s>Hṛdya</s> (cordial) and removing <s>kapha</s> (phlegm), the tubers are pungent and aggravate <s>pitta</s> (bile);
they remove <s>meha</s> (urinary disorders), <s>kuṣṭha</s> (skin diseases), and worms, are <s>vṛṣya</s> (aphrodisiac), strengthening, and act as <s>rasāyana</s> (rejuvenative). // 27 //
The tubers of <s>kumuda</s> (white water lily), <s>utpala</s> (blue lotus), and <s>padma</s> (lotus) are beneficial and cooling,
sweet and astringent, they destroy <s>pitta</s> (bile), blood disorders, and burning sensation. // 28 //

body.translated_text: The tuber of <s>padma</s> (lotus).
Now, the properties of <s>mṛṇāla</s> (lotus stalk).

children.translated_text: Cooling, it destroys <s>raktapitta</s> (bleeding disorders), and supremely removes burning and fever;
the stalk of <s>mṛṇāla</s> (lotus) is <s>vṛṣya</s> (aphrodisiac), and destroys thirst and vomiting. // 29 //

body.translated_text: The lotus stalk.
Now, the properties of <s>śṛṅgāṭaka</s> (water caltrop).

children.text: śṛṅgāṭakaḥ śoṇitapittahārī laghuḥ saro vṛṣyatamo viśeṣāt /
children.translated_text: <s>Śṛṅgāṭaka</s> (water caltrop) removes <s>śoṇitapitta</s> (bleeding disorders), is light, laxative, especially <s>vṛṣya</s> (aphrodisiac),
it destroys the three <s>doṣas</s> (humors), the three kinds of heat, and swelling, promotes appetite, and causes <s>meha</s> (urinary disorders) and burning. // 30 //

body.translated_text: Now, the properties of <s>vārikaśeruka</s> (water chestnut).

children.text: hanty asrapittamaruciṃ vamimohadāhaṃ tṛṣṇāmadaklamaharaṃ madhuraṃ ca śītam /
children.translated_text: It destroys blood and <s>pitta</s> (bile) disorders, loss of appetite, vomiting, delusion, and burning; it removes thirst, intoxication, and exhaustion, is sweet and cooling;

children.text: kaṇṭhāsyaśoṣaśamanaṃ guru raktapitte kṣīṇe ca pathyamati vārikaśeri (ru)kaṃ syāt // 31 //
children.translated_text: it pacifies throat and mouth dryness, is heavy, and in <s>raktapitta</s> (bleeding disorders) and wasting diseases, <s>vārikaśeruka</s> (water chestnut) is extremely wholesome. // 31 //

body.translated_text: Now, the description of tubers to be avoided.

children.text: bālaṃ hy anārtavaṃ jīrṇaṃ viddhaṃ tu kṛmibhakṣitam /
children.translated_text: Young, out-of-season, old, pierced, or infested with worms —

children.text: kandaṃ ca varjayet sarvaṃ yo vā samyaṅ na rohati // 32 //
children.translated_text: all such tubers should be avoided, as well as any that do not sprout properly. // 32 //

body.translated_text: Now, the properties of <s>kaliṅga</s> (watermelon).

children.translated_text: <s>Hṛdya</s> (cordial) and wholesome for those with seminal disorders, it removes all <s>doṣas</s> (humors),
<s>kaliṅga</s> (watermelon) impairs eyesight and depletes semen, and conquers <s>kapha</s> (phlegm) and <s>vāta</s> (wind). // 33 //

body.translated_text: // <s>Kaliṅga</s> (watermelon). //
Now, the properties of <s>kūṣmāṇḍa</s> (ash gourd).

body.text:
vṛṣyaṃ varṇakaraṃ balopajananaṃ pittāpahaṃ vātajit*
mūtrāghātaharaṃ pramehaśamanaṃ kṛcchrāśmarīchedanam /
body.translated_text:
<s>Vṛṣya</s> (aphrodisiac), complexion-enhancing, strength-promoting, removing <s>pitta</s> (bile), conquering <s>vāta</s> (wind),
relieving urinary obstruction, pacifying <s>prameha</s> (urinary disorders), and breaking <s>aśmarī</s> (urinary calculi);
purifying feces and urine, pacifying thirst and pain, and nourishing emaciated limbs —

body.text: kūṣmāṇḍaṃ pravaraṃ vadanti bhiṣajo vallīphalānāṃ punaḥ // 34 //
body.translated_text: physicians declare <s>kūṣmāṇḍa</s> (ash gourd) the best among creeper fruits. // 34 //

children.translated_text: It pacifies urinary obstruction and promotes copious urination, alleviates <s>kṛcchra</s> (dysuria) and <s>aśmarī</s> (urinary calculi), and destroys <s>pitta</s> (bile);
it is wholesome in blood-related <s>pitta</s> (bile) disorders,
removes thirst, and is said to equally pacify the three <s>doṣas</s> (humors). // 35 //

body.translated_text: Now, the properties of <s>urvāruka</s> (cucumber).

children.text: e (u) rvārukaṃ pittaharaṃ śuśītaṃ mūtrāmayaghnaṃ rucikārakaṃ ca /
children.translated_text: <s>Urvāruka</s> (cucumber) removes <s>pitta</s> (bile), is very cooling, destroys urinary diseases, and promotes appetite;

children.text: susvādu dāhopaśamaṃ praśastaṃ pitte ca roge kapharogavarjyam // 36 //
children.translated_text: very sweet, it subdues burning, is praised in <s>pitta</s> (bile) disorders, but should be avoided in <s>kapha</s> (phlegmatic) diseases. // 36 //

children.text: vālukāni ca sarvāṇi durjarāṇi gūjaṇi (gurūṇi) ca /
children.translated_text: All <s>vāluka</s> (sandy/musk melon) varieties are difficult to digest and heavy,
they weaken the digestive fire and aggravate <s>raktapitta</s> (bleeding disorders). // 37 //

body.translated_text: <s>Vāluka</s> (musk melon) — variant reading.
Now, <s>sindhanī</s> (a gourd variety).

children.translated_text: <s>Siṃdhaṇī</s> pacifies <s>vāta</s> (wind), is <s>vṛṣya</s> (aphrodisiac), sweet, and cooling;

children.text: raktapitte ca dāhe ca pittārtīnāṃ praśasyate // 38 //
children.translated_text: it is recommended for those afflicted by <s>raktapitta</s> (bleeding disorders), burning, and <s>pitta</s> (bile). // 38 //

body.translated_text: <s>Sindhaṇī</s> — variant reading.
Now, the properties of <s>cillī</s>, <s>kākamācī</s> (black nightshade), and similar plants.

children.translated_text: <s>Ciplī</s> (a type of leafy green), like <s>vāstuka</s> (Chenopodium), destroys diseases, is astringent (<s>saṃgrāhī</s>), heavy, and aggravates <s>Vāta</s>,
<s>Kākamācī</s> (Solanum nigrum) destroys the three <s>doṣas</s>; <s>Cāṅgerī</s> (wood sorrel) alleviates <s>Kapha</s> and <s>Vāta</s>. // 39 //
<s>Paṅjī</s> destroys <s>Vāta</s> and is a digestive stimulant; <s>Bhāraṅgī</s>, <s>Nālicā</s>, and <s>Ṣaṇḍaka</s> (?)
are sweet, destroy <s>Kapha</s> and <s>Pitta</s>; <s>Kusumbha</s> (safflower) alleviates all diseases. // 40 //
<s>Mūlaka</s> (radish) is a producer of <s>doṣas</s> when raw, but when cooked it removes <s>Vāta</s> and <s>Kapha</s>,
<s>Rājikā</s> (mustard greens) aggravates <s>Pitta</s> and destroys <s>Vāta</s> and <s>Kapha</s>; so does <s>Taṇḍulīyaka</s> (Amaranthus). // 41 //
<s>Carṣābhūr</s> destroys <s>Vāta</s> and <s>Pitta</s>; <s>Siddhārtha</s> (white mustard) alleviates <s>Kapha</s> and <s>Vāta</s>,
destroys worms (<s>kṛmi</s>), <s>Pitta</s>, and <s>Kapha</s>; <s>Kāsamardaka</s> (Cassia occidentalis) is a digestive stimulant. // 42 //
<s>Karkoṭaka</s> (spiny gourd), <s>Vārtāka</s> (eggplant), <s>Paṭola</s> (pointed gourd), and <s>Kāravellaka</s> (bitter gourd)
remove eight types of diseases including <s>meha</s> (urinary disorders), fever, <s>śvāsa</s> (dyspnea), cough, obesity, and <s>Kapha</s>. // 43 //
<s>Kūṣmāṇḍa</s> (ash gourd) should be known as remover of all <s>doṣas</s> and purifier of the bladder,
<s>Rājakośātakī</s>, <s>Tumbī</s> (bottle gourd) fruit are extremely potent destroyers of <s>Pitta</s>. // 44 //
<s>Trapusa</s> (cucumber) aggravates <s>Vāta</s>, is <s>Vāta</s>- and <s>Śleṣma</s>-producing, and destroys <s>Pitta</s>,
<s>Kāliṅga</s> (watermelon), <s>Tucchaka</s>, and <s>Kaśeruka</s> (water chestnut) destroy <s>Vāta</s> and <s>Pitta</s>. // 45 //

body.translated_text: Now, the description of substances used for seasoning vegetables (<s>śākasaṃskārakadravya</s>).

children.translated_text: <s>Śuṇṭhī</s> (dry ginger), <s>Marīca</s> (black pepper), and <s>Pippalī</s> (long pepper) are considered destroyers of <s>Kapha</s> and <s>Vāta</s>,
<s>Hiṅgu</s> (asafoetida) destroys abdominal tumors (<s>gulma</s>), colic (<s>śūla</s>), and constipation (<s>vibandha</s>), and removes <s>Vāta</s> and <s>Kapha</s>. // 45 //
<s>Pacānī</s> (<s>Yavānī</s>, bishop's weed), <s>Dhānyaka</s> (coriander), and <s>Jīva</s> (seed) destroy <s>Vāta</s>, <s>Pitta</s>, and <s>Kapha</s>,
<s>Sauvarcana</s> (black salt) destroys constipation; <s>Saindhava</s> (rock salt) alleviates the three <s>doṣas</s>. // 47 //

children.text: etais tu saṃsrutaṃ pakvaṃ bhṛṣṭaṃ vyañjanasaurabham /
children.translated_text: Cooked food seasoned with these becomes well-prepared with fragrant condiments (<s>vyañjana</s>),
and gruel (<s>peyā</s>) and other such preparations remove all <s>doṣas</s> including tremors. // 48 //

body.translated_text: // Thus ends the section on fruits and vegetables (<s>phalaśākavarga</s>) in the <s>Āyurvedamahodadhi</s> composed by <s>Suṣeṇa</s>. //
// Now the <s>Śikariṇī</s> (yogurt-based preparation) is described. //

children.translated_text: Half an <s>āḍhaka</s> (measure) of well-aged yogurt,
sixteen <s>palas</s> of sugar (<s>khaṇḍa</s>), white as moonlight,

children.text: sarpiḥ palaṃ madhu palaṃ maricaṃ dvikarṣaṃ
children.translated_text: one <s>pala</s> of ghee (<s>sarpi</s>), one <s>pala</s> of honey, two <s>karṣas</s> of pepper (<s>marica</s>),
half a <s>pala</s> of <s>śuṇṭhī</s> (dry ginger), and also half a <s>pala</s> of the four spices (<s>caturjātaka</s>).
Gently churned with the hands on a smooth stone slab, made fragrant with camphor (<s>karpūra</s>) powder, beautifully arranged,

children.text: eṣā vṛkodarakṛtā mu (su)rasā rasālā cāsvāditā bhagavatā madhusūdanena // 2 //
children.translated_text: this excellent and delicious <s>rasālā</s>, made in a bull's-belly vessel, was tasted by Lord <s>Madhusūdana</s> (Viṣṇu). // 2 //

children.text: triṃśatpalāni dadhnaś ca tv agelārdhapalaṃ tathā /
children.translated_text: Thirty <s>palas</s> of yogurt, and half a <s>pala</s> of cardamom (<s>elā</s>),
half a <s>pala</s> each of honey and ghee, and half a <s>pala</s> of pepper (<s>marica</s>) and cardamom (<s>elā</s>), // 3 //

children.text: palāny aṣṭau ca khaṇḍasya paṭe śuddhe 'vadhāra (gāla)yet /
children.translated_text: eight <s>palas</s> of sugar (<s>khaṇḍa</s>); one should strain this in a clean cloth,
and place it in a vessel scented with camphor (<s>karpūra</s>), and store it in the shade. // 4 //
This is called <s>Śikariṇī</s>; it kindles the digestive fire, increases strength,
promotes longevity, and destroys all diseases. // 5 //

body.text: (nāśa) sāna śyet tṛḍrujāsthaulyaṃ narāṇāṃ sarvadā hitā /
body.translated_text: It destroys drowsiness (<s>tṛḍrā</s>), lassitude, and obesity; it is always beneficial for people.
// The second <s>Śikariṇī</s>. //

children.translated_text: With the seeds of <s>Kapittha</s> (wood apple), <s>Mātuluṅga</s> (citron), <s>Elā</s> (cardamom), <s>Sārivā</s> (Hemidesmus),
combined with sugar (<s>śarkarā</s>), dry ginger (<s>śuṇṭhī</s>), sea salt (<s>sāmudra</s>), and <s>Mudga</s> (mung bean) powder,

body.text: sadā pathyā niyuñjayāc ca (ddhādhva) kṣīṇe dehe ca puṣṭidā // 7 //
body.translated_text: it is always wholesome; it should be administered when the body is emaciated and weakened. // 7 //

children.text: sujātaṃ dadhni bhedaṃ ca (nikṣiptaṃ) vastre baddhvā supīḍitam /
children.translated_text: Well-formed curds, broken apart (and strained), tied in a cloth and well-pressed,
one should prepare it in yogurt decorated with various flowers and fruits, making it delightful. // 8 //

children.text: sūktaṃ dadhirasaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ tad dhṛtaṃ śodhite paṭe /
children.translated_text: The excellent, well-expressed yogurt juice, held in a clean cloth,
combined proportionally with salt — this <s>Śikariṇī</s> is comparable to nectar (<s>amṛta</s>). // 9 //

body.translated_text: <s>Rasālā</s> destroys all <s>doṣas</s> and removes bleeding disorders (<s>raktapitta</s>).
// Another <s>Śikariṇī</s>. //

body.text: sanmātuliṅgasya dalaṃ tv agelāṃ saraṃgapippalyī sasamaṃ (?) sitayā sametam //
body.translated_text: A leaf of good <s>Mātuliṅga</s> (citron), with cardamom (<s>elā</s>), <s>Saraṅga</s> (a variety), <s>Pippalī</s> (long pepper), in equal parts, combined with sugar (<s>sitā</s>),

body.text: vyoṣāc ca gadyāṇayugaprayuktaṃ syād vārtakaṃ (?) dṛṣṭisamaṃ sitavastrabaddham // 10 //
body.translated_text: with <s>Vyoṣa</s> (the three pungents) and a pair of fragrant substances, like <s>Vārtaka</s> (?), equal to a <s>dṛṣṭi</s> measure, tied in a white cloth, // 10 //

children.text: karpūravāsāc ca tathaiva paścād yuktyā ca saṃmardma kṛtā rasālā /
children.translated_text: then scented with camphor (<s>karpūra</s>), and skillfully blended — thus the <s>rasālā</s> is prepared;

children.text: eṣā kṛtā śikhariṇī surasā rasālā suṣeṇadevena rathāśvahetoḥ // 11 //
children.translated_text: this <s>Śikariṇī</s>, a delicious <s>rasālā</s>, was prepared by <s>Suṣeṇadeva</s> for the sake of chariots and horses (i.e., for warriors). // 11 //

children.text: āsvāditā śikhariṇī parameśvareṇa doṣāṃś ca sarvān vinihanti vogrān /
children.translated_text: This <s>Śikariṇī</s>, tasted by the Supreme Lord, destroys all fierce <s>doṣas</s>,

children.text: pittāsraraktā (sṛgutthā)n api hanti sarvān bhojyāni sarvāṇy api jārayanti // 12 //
children.translated_text: it also destroys all conditions arising from <s>Pitta</s> and blood (<s>rakta</s>), and aids in the digestion of all foods. // 12 //

body.translated_text: // The <s>Amṛtaprāśa Śikariṇī</s> (nectar-tasting preparation). //

body.text:
nāraṅgaṃ dāḍimaṃ syāt palamadhukayutaṃ mātuluṅgasya toyaṃ
drākṣātoyaṃ samāṃśaṃ guḍadadhisahitaṃ śarkarājājimiśram /
body.translated_text: <s>Nāraṅga</s> (orange), <s>Dāḍima</s> (pomegranate), combined with <s>Pala</s> (a measure) of <s>Madhuka</s> (licorice), the juice of <s>Mātuluṅga</s> (citron), grape juice in equal parts, combined with jaggery (<s>guḍa</s>) and yogurt, mixed with sugar (<s>śarkarā</s>) and cumin (<s>jājī</s>),

body.text: (śreṣṭhā pāneṣu vṛṣyā sita) śreṣṭho pāde ca vṛṣyāt sama ricayutā saindhavair vāpitaṃ tan
body.translated_text: the best, one should add in appropriate proportion, combined with <s>Rica</s> (?) and flavored with <s>Saindhava</s> (rock salt),

body.text: niṣpīḍya sarvam etat kuru (racaya) śikhariṇāṃ rājayogyā yatas tāḥ // 13 //
body.translated_text: pressing out all of this, prepare the <s>Śikariṇī</s>, as it is fit for kings. // 13 //
And another:

children.translated_text: With <s>Mātuluṅga</s> (citron), sugar (<s>sitā</s>), cumin (<s>jājī</s>), pepper (<s>marica</s>), fresh ginger (<s>ārdraka</s>), and dry ginger (<s>nāgara</s>),
combined with camphor (<s>karpūra</s>), skillfully mixed with well-aged yogurt in equal parts, // 14 //

children.text: rasaṃ yogeṣu sarveṣu badarasya samasya ca /
children.translated_text: the juice of <s>Badara</s> (jujube) in equal proportion in all preparations,
mixed with dry ginger (<s>nāgara</s>) juice — among <s>rasālās</s>, this is comparable to nectar (<s>amṛta</s>). // 15 //

body.translated_text: Thickened in a clean cloth, it removes bleeding disorders (<s>raktapitta</s>).
// The <s>Śikariṇī</s> called <s>Candrāmṛtasrāviṇī</s> (flowing with lunar nectar). //

children.translated_text: With <s>Mātuliṅga</s> (citron), <s>Kapittha</s> (wood apple), <s>Āmlatittiḍī</s> (tamarind), and <s>Āmladāḍima</s> (sour pomegranate),
combined with sugar (<s>śarkarā</s>), yogurt (<s>dadhi</s>), and <s>piṣṭa</s> (flour) in a clean cloth, // 16 //
seasoned with pepper (<s>marica</s>), cumin (<s>jājī</s>), the four spices (<s>cāturjātaka</s>), and <s>bhūstṛṇa</s> (lemongrass),
consumed with fresh ginger (<s>ārdraka</s>), this <s>rasālā</s> is of nectar-like quality. // 17 //
It pacifies all diseases, removes burning sensation and <s>Pitta</s>,
removes excess blood (<s>raktaodreka</s>), is wholesome, and promotes the downward movement of all <s>Vāta</s>. // 18 //

body.translated_text: This <s>Śikariṇī</s> has been described as devised by <s>Suṣeṇa</s>.
// And another. //
The best, prepared with yogurt (<s>dadhi</s>), jaggery (<s>guḍa</s>), cumin (<s>jājī</s>), dry ginger (<s>nāgara</s>), and fresh ginger (<s>ārdraka</s>), // 19 //

children.translated_text: well-perfumed with the four spices (<s>caturjāta</s>) — among <s>rasālās</s>, this is comparable to nectar,
it pacifies all afflictions and destroys all excessive diarrhea (<s>atīsāra</s>). // 20 //
It removes excess <s>Pitta</s>, is wholesome, and destroys excessive <s>Pitta</s>-diarrhea;
this <s>rasālā</s>, comparable to nectar, was prepared by <s>Suṣeṇadeva</s>. // 21 //

body.translated_text: // Thus ends the <s>Śikariṇī</s> section (<s>Śikariṇīvarga</s>) composed by <s>Suṣeṇa</s>. //
Now the section on condiments (<s>Vyañjanavarga</s>).

children.translated_text: <s>Hiṅgu</s> (asafoetida), <s>Ṣaṇā</s>, cumin (<s>jājī</s>), <s>Mahauṣadha</s> (dry ginger), and <s>Dhānī</s> (coriander), powdered in triple proportion successively,

children.text: sadīpyakaṃ sūraṇapūṣa (?) māṃsarasaprayogeṣu ca nityam iṣṭam // 1 //
children.translated_text: combined with <s>dīpyaka</s> (a digestive spice) and <s>sūraṇa</s> (elephant yam) flour (?), this is always desirable in meat-juice preparations. // 1 //
<s>Yavānī</s> (bishop's weed) and <s>Jīraka</s> (cumin) in equal proportion, with double the amount of <s>sūraṇa</s> (elephant yam),
combined with a moderate amount of (?), thus the condiment becomes fragrant. // 2 //
It removes all diseases, is wholesome, and destroys flatulence caused by <s>Vāta</s>;
<s>Śuṇṭhī</s> (dry ginger), <s>Marica</s> (black pepper), and <s>Pippalī</s> (long pepper) in equal parts, powdered with dry ginger (<s>Nāga</s>), // 3 //
combined with <s>Cavya</s> (Piper chaba), <s>Citraka</s> (Plumbago), and <s>Kapittha</s> (wood apple) extract, well-prepared,

children.text: saindhavena mamopetaṃ takrapītaṃ ca yatra cit // 4 //
children.translated_text: with rock salt (<s>Saindhava</s>) and accompanied by buttermilk (<s>takra</s>) wherever drunk, // 4 //
this indeed is the best condiment (<s>vyañjana</s>), preventing all <s>Vāta</s> disorders,
pacifying great abdominal tumors (<s>mahāgulma</s>), prepared by <s>Suṣeṇa</s> for people. // 5 //

body.translated_text: It is recommended in all <s>Vāta</s> diseases, the supreme medicine for people.
// And another. //

body.text: marīcaṃ dīpyakaṃ śuṇṭhī cavyaṃ citrakam eva ca // 6 //
body.translated_text: <s>Marica</s> (black pepper), <s>Dīpyaka</s> (digestive stimulant), <s>Śuṇṭhī</s> (dry ginger), <s>Cavya</s> (Piper chaba), and <s>Citraka</s> (Plumbago), // 6 //

children.translated_text: <s>Pippalī</s> (long pepper), <s>Pippalīmūla</s> (root of long pepper), <s>Dhānyāka</s> (coriander), cumin (<s>Jājī</s>), and rock salt (<s>Saindhava</s>),
<s>Jīraka</s> (cumin), <s>Dāḍima</s> (pomegranate), <s>Pathyā</s> (Terminalia chebula), <s>Āmalaka</s> (Indian gooseberry), and fragrant <s>Hṛdyagandhaka</s>, // 7 //

children.text: etat kalpasamaṃ miśraṃ paktvā takre sapiṇḍake /
children.translated_text: all these mixed in equal proportions, cooked in buttermilk (<s>takra</s>) with added oil cake (<s>piṇḍaka</s>),
this removes <s>Vāta</s> and <s>Śleṣma</s> (Kapha), is pleasing, and supremely appetite-enhancing. // 8 //
It destroys <s>āma</s> (undigested toxins), diarrhea (<s>atisāra</s>), and colic (<s>śūla</s>), and cuts down abdominal tumors caused by <s>Vāta</s> (<s>vātagulma</s>),
it removes cough (<s>kāsa</s>) and dyspnea (<s>śvāsa</s>), is potent, gentle, and enriching (?),

children.text: uktā caiva sadā pathyā sottamā kaṭhinā smṛtā // 10 //
children.translated_text: it is always declared wholesome, and is considered the best by the wise. // 10 //

body.translated_text: The decoction (<s>Kvathikā</s>):

children.translated_text: <s>Marica</s> (black pepper), <s>Jaraṇa</s> (digestive), <s>Śuṇṭhī</s> (dry ginger), <s>Pippalīmūla</s> (root of long pepper), <s>Cavya</s> (Piper chaba),
<s>Dahana</s> (Plumbago, the digestive fire-kindler), <s>Rucaka</s> (a type of salt), <s>Dhānya</s> (coriander), <s>Pippalī</s> (long pepper), and rock salt (<s>Saindhava</s>),
with <s>Kapittha</s> (wood apple) extract, <s>Dāḍimikā</s> (pomegranate juice), and <s>Hiṅgu</s> (asafoetida),
well-cooked by a young woman's hands, with <s>Āmalakī</s> (Indian gooseberry) and good buttermilk (<s>takra</s>). // 11 //
This removes the foremost <s>Vāta</s> (wind), phlegm (<s>Śleṣma</s>), burning, and affliction (<s>kṛcchra</s>),
loss of appetite, abdominal hardness, colic (<s>śūla</s>), <s>āma</s> (undigested toxins), <s>Vāta</s> disorders, and diarrhea (<s>atisāra</s>).
The king of physicians, <s>Suṣeṇa</s>, knower of all sciences,
composes this <s>Kapittha</s>-condiment (<s>kapitthavyañjana</s>), a royal secret. // 12 //

body.translated_text: // And another. //

children.translated_text: <s>Trikaṭuka</s> (the three pungents), <s>Ajamodā</s> (celery seed), rock salt (<s>Saindhava</s>), two types of cumin (<s>Jīraka</s>),
<s>Kapittha</s> (wood apple) hand-churned, <s>Citraka</s> (Plumbago), and <s>Pippalī</s> (long pepper),
powdered with equal portions of ghee (<s>dhṛta</s>), these should be combined,
boiled together in equal proportion and mixed with buttermilk (<s>Rāmaṭha</s>). // 13 //
With added salt and good coriander (<s>dhānya</s>), and the extract of <s>Mātuluṅga</s> (citron),
this condiment (<s>vyañjana</s>) is always beneficial in <s>Kapha</s> and <s>Vāta</s> disorders;

children.text: vāte 'gnimāndye 'pi ca śūlamāndye mūrchāṃ nigṛhṇāti cirapravṛddhām //
children.translated_text: in <s>Vāta</s> conditions, weak digestive fire (<s>agnimāndya</s>), colic (<s>śūla</s>), and debility, it arrests even long-standing fainting (<s>mūrcchā</s>).

body.text: suṣeṇadevena kṛtā rasālā susaurabhā rogaharāpi pathyā // 14 //
body.translated_text: This <s>rasālā</s>, prepared by <s>Suṣeṇadeva</s>, is fragrant, disease-removing, and wholesome. // 14 //
// Thus ends the condiment section (<s>Vyañjanavarga</s>) composed by Śrī <s>Suṣeṇa</s>. //
// Now the qualities of meat (<s>māṃsaguṇa</s>) are described. //

body.text:
māṃsaṃ svādumatāṃ varaṃ subalakṛt snehādhikaṃ dehino
nityaṃ dhātuṣu sāmyakṛc ca kathitaṃ tad varṇakṛd bṛṃhaṇam //
body.translated_text: Meat is the foremost among tasty foods, it greatly strengthens the body, is rich in unctuousness (<s>sneha</s>), and it maintains equilibrium among the <s>dhātus</s> (bodily tissues); it is described as nourishing according to its class,

body.text: bhuktaṃ tṛptikaraṃ ca kāmakaraṇaṃ vātādidoṣān haret

children.translated_text: therefore, for the pacification of bodily <s>doṣas</s>, one should always eat meat. // 1 //

body.translated_text: when eaten it produces satisfaction, arouses desire, and removes <s>doṣas</s> beginning with <s>Vāta</s>;
Now the qualities of <s>Lāva</s> (quail) meat.

children.translated_text: <s>Lāva</s> (quail) birds are cooling, sweet, astringent, <s>vṛṣya</s> (aphrodisiac), fire-kindling, unctuous, light (?), and pleasing to the heart,

children.text: saṃgrāhikā vai kaṭupācitāś ca te saṃnipāteṣu hitāḥ samastāḥ // 2 //
children.translated_text: they are astringent (<s>saṃgrāhikā</s>), and remedies for skin disease (<s>kaṭu</s>) and itching; they are beneficial in all <s>Sannipāta</s> (combined doṣa) conditions. // 2 //

body.translated_text: // Thus <s>Lāva</s> (quail). //
Now the qualities of <s>Kṛṣṇa Tittiri</s> (black partridge).

children.translated_text: It is slightly heavy, sweet, exceedingly <s>vṛṣya</s> (aphrodisiac), and promotes intellect (<s>medhā</s>) and digestive fire (<s>agni</s>),

children.text: balyo vihanyāt sa kaphajvarāṃś ca vātāmayādyān śititittiriś ca // 3 //
children.translated_text: it is strengthening and destroys fever caused by <s>Kapha</s> and <s>Vāta</s> disorders; such is the grey partridge (<s>Śititittiri</s>). // 3 //

body.translated_text: // Thus <s>Kṛṣṇa Tittiri</s> (black partridge). //
Now the white partridge (<s>Gaura Tittiri</s>).

body.text:
gauras tittiriko 'gnikṛt kaphaharo rūkṣo 'tipittāpahaḥ
śleṣmāṇaṃ vinihanti caiva balavān raktaṃ ca pittaṃ jayet /
body.translated_text: The white partridge kindles the digestive fire, removes <s>Kapha</s>, is dry, and extremely cooling for <s>Pitta</s>; it destroys phlegm (<s>Śleṣma</s>), is strengthening, and conquers blood and <s>Pitta</s> disorders.
Now the <s>Kāpiñjala</s> (grey francolin).

children.translated_text: It removes excess blood-<s>Pitta</s>, is very cooling and light, always strengthening and exceedingly <s>vṛṣya</s> (aphrodisiac),
in <s>Vāta</s> conditions it is mild and cooling, destroys worms (<s>kṛmi</s>), and eliminates urinary disorders (<s>meha</s>);
in conditions of wasting, semen depletion, and fat loss, it kindles the digestive fire; the <s>Kāpiñjala</s> is recommended,
it swiftly dissolves <s>Vāta</s> and blood disorders, and destroys <s>Pitta</s> diseases. // 4 //

body.translated_text: Now the qualities of <s>Vārtaka</s> (a type of bird).

children.text: pāṇḍupramehapiḍikākṛmisaṃbhaveṣu rogeṣu vātabahuleṣu ca śasyate ca /
children.translated_text: It is recommended in diseases of anemia (<s>pāṇḍu</s>), urinary disorders (<s>prameha</s>), hemorrhoids (<s>piḍikā</s>), and worms (<s>kṛmi</s>), and in conditions dominated by <s>Vāta</s>,

children.text: vātāsrapittakaphajān vinihanti kīlān gulmāgnimāndyam aruciṃ laghu vārtakaṃ ca // 5 //
children.translated_text: it destroys hemorrhoids (<s>kīla</s>) caused by <s>Vāta</s>, blood, <s>Pitta</s>, and <s>Kapha</s>, as well as abdominal tumors (<s>gulma</s>), weak digestion (<s>agnimāndya</s>), and loss of appetite; <s>Vārtaka</s> is light. // 5 //

body.translated_text: Now the qualities of <s>Krakara</s> and <s>Upacakrikā</s> (types of birds).

body.text:
laghuś ca vṛṣyā ca balopabṛṃhaṇī
hṛdyā tathā krakarorucikriyā (sakrakaropacakrikā) //
body.translated_text: They are light, <s>vṛṣya</s> (aphrodisiac), and nourishing in strength, pleasing to the heart; such are <s>Krakara</s> and <s>Upacakrikā</s>.
Now the qualities of peacock (<s>Mayūra</s>) meat.

children.translated_text: It is astringent, pungent, exceedingly <s>vṛṣya</s> (aphrodisiac), very tasty, beneficial for the throat (<s>kaṇṭhya</s>),
with alkaline taste, appetite-stimulating, poison-destroying, and destroyer of weak digestion,

children.text: (svaryaṃ) śvarye medhyam atīva hṛṣṭijananaṃ śrotrendriye dārḍhyakṛt
children.translated_text: beneficial for the voice, promoter of intellect (<s>medhya</s>), exceedingly joy-producing, and strengthening for the auditory sense organ,
peacock (<s>Māyūra</s>) meat is always unctuous, hot, and pacifies wind (<s>Anila</s>), blood (<s>Asra</s>), and <s>Pitta</s>. // 7 //

body.text: hemantakāle śiśire vasante sevyaṃ hi māyuram uśanti māṃsam /
body.translated_text: In winter (<s>Hemanta</s>), in the cold season (<s>Śiśira</s>), and in spring (<s>Vasanta</s>), peacock meat is recommended for consumption.
Now the qualities of rooster (<s>Kukkuṭa</s>) meat.

children.text: uṣṇaḥ svādutaro balasvarakaro vṛṣyaḥ sadā bṛṃhaṇaḥ
children.translated_text: The rooster is hot, exceedingly sweet, producer of strength and voice, <s>vṛṣya</s> (aphrodisiac), always nourishing,
unctuous upon digestion, great destroyer of wind (<s>Anila</s>), and producer of fat (<s>medas</s>), <s>Kapha</s>, and sluggishness;

children.text: āyuṣyaṃ kurute kṣayeṣu viṣame mehe vamau śasyate
children.translated_text: it promotes longevity, is beneficial in wasting diseases (<s>kṣaya</s>), recommended in irregular conditions and urinary disorders (<s>meha</s>) and vomiting,
the rooster (<s>Kukkuṭaka</s>) is declared a pacifier of <s>doṣas</s> and destroyer of all diseases. // 9 //

body.translated_text: Now the qualities of pigeon (<s>Kapota</s>) and other birds.

children.text: kapotapārāvatabhṛṅgarājā jaṭī kuliṅgaṃ gṛhajaṃ pikaś ca /
children.translated_text: <s>Kapota</s> (pigeon), <s>Pārāvata</s> (dove), <s>Bhṛṅgarāja</s> (a bird), <s>Jaṭī</s>, <s>Kuliṅga</s> (sparrow), <s>Gṛhaja</s> (domesticated bird), and <s>Pika</s> (Indian cuckoo),
<s>Bhedāśi</s>, <s>Ḍiṇḍī</s>, <s>Śuka</s> (parrot), <s>Sāri</s> (myna), <s>Vālūka</s>, <s>Khañjarīṭa</s> (wagtail), and green birds — all are commendable. // 10 //
They are astringent, <s>Vāta</s>-producing, dry, fruit-eating, and desert-dwelling,
they are declared to remove <s>Pitta</s> and <s>Śleṣma</s> (Kapha), but cause scanty urine and stool. // 11 //

children.text: kāṣāyā lavaṇā himāḥ kaphakarā vṛṣyāḥ sadā durjarā
children.translated_text: they are astringent, salty, cooling, <s>Kapha</s>-producing, <s>vṛṣya</s> (aphrodisiac), always hard to digest,
they cause distension (<s>viṣṭambha</s>), increase urine, and produce burning in the mouth due to <s>Pitta</s>,
they produce <s>āma</s> (undigested toxins), flatulence, generate all three <s>doṣas</s>, and cause delusion and bad taste in the mouth.
they impair digestive fire, build strength, relieve fatigue, cause bad odor, and increase <s>Kapha</s>. // 12 //

body.translated_text: Among those, <s>Bhedāśī</s> is always <s>doṣa</s>-producing and a contaminant of waste products (<s>mala</s>);

children.text: ete prāvṛṣi sevitāḥ pratidinaṃ doṣavrajaghnāḥ khalu /
children.translated_text: These, when consumed daily during the rainy season, indeed destroy the multitude of <s>doṣas</s>;
all sky-roaming birds are strength-giving, aphrodisiac, and very difficult to digest. // 13 //

body.translated_text: Properties of pigeon (<s>kauliṅga</s>) //

children.translated_text: <s>Kauliṅga</s> (pigeon) is sweet, highly aphrodisiac, produces <s>Kapha</s>, and breaks up urinary stones (<s>śukrāśmarī</s>);
it greatly removes <s>Pitta</s> and blood disorders, is highly generative of semen, and produces unctuousness and sweetness in the mouth;

children.text: balyo mārutanāśanaḥ kṛmiharo vāryaś ca netrāmaye
children.translated_text: it is strengthening, destroys <s>Vāta</s>, removes worms, and should be avoided in eye diseases,
it pacifies hemorrhoids (<s>durnāma</s>), especially destroys <s>Vāta</s>, and is always difficult to digest. // 14 //

body.translated_text: Properties of domestic animals (<s>grāmya</s>) //

children.translated_text: All domestic animals alleviate <s>Vāta</s>, are nourishing, and increase <s>Kapha</s> and <s>Pitta</s>;
they are sweet in both taste and post-digestive effect, kindle the digestive fire, and increase strength. // 15 //

body.translated_text: Properties of pigeon (<s>kapota</s>) //

children.translated_text: Pigeon meat is heavy, very cold in potency, unctuous and mild, and aggravates

children.text: śleṣmā pitte praṇayavijarā jarjarā caṃ cadanāt [?] /
children.translated_text: <s>Kapha</s>; in <s>Pitta</s> disorders it promotes affection, removes aging, and is softening through its gentle action;
it is excellent for relieving fatigue in seminal debility, beneficial in difficult urination, in summer heat,

children.text: mohe yojyaḥ sa bhavati nṛṇāṃ kāyakārī balāya // 16 //
children.translated_text: and in fainting — it is suitable for people, building the body and promoting strength. // 16 //

body.translated_text: Now, the properties of <s>jāṅgala</s> (arid-land) meat //

children.translated_text: <s>Jāṅgala</s> meat destroys bladder disorders, is heavy, and cures nasal congestion;

children.text: laghupākaṃ na śītaṃ ca nātisnigdhamadāhi ca // 17 //
children.translated_text: it is light in digestion, neither cold nor excessively unctuous, and does not cause burning. // 17 //

body.translated_text: Now, the properties of goat and sheep meat //

children.translated_text: Goat meat is neither too cold, is heavy, unctuous, and does not aggravate the <s>doṣas</s>;
due to its similarity to the bodily tissues (<s>dhātus</s>), it is non-obstructive and nourishing;
sheep meat is nourishing, has a pleasant aroma, aggravates <s>Pitta</s> and <s>Kapha</s>, and is heavy. // 18 //

body.translated_text: Now, the properties of deer (<s>eṇa</s>) meat //

children.text: aiṇaṃ māṃsaṃ ca hṛdyaṃ balakaram api tat pittaraktaṃ nihanti
children.translated_text: Deer meat is pleasing to the heart and strength-giving; it destroys <s>Pitta</s> and blood disorders,

children.text: pāṇḍukṣīṇe sadāhe kaphapavanarujo nāśayaty āśu kīlān /
children.translated_text: in anemia and debility with burning sensation, it quickly destroys diseases of <s>Kapha</s> and <s>Vāta</s>, and hemorrhoids (<s>kīla</s>);
it overcomes splenic enlargement (<s>plīhā</s>), distension (<s>ānāha</s>), and constipation; it is supreme in removing fever and eliminates excess fat (<s>medas</s>);
it should be used for those with seminal debility; it promotes taste, is light, and cuts through asthma (<s>śvāsa</s>) and cough (<s>kāsa</s>). // 19 //

body.text:
medaḥ pucchodbhavaṃ syāt kaphapavanaharaṃ kāntidaṃ puṣṭidaṃ syāt
vātāsṛk pittakṛt syān madaharaviṣahṛc chvāsakāsaṃ chinatti /
body.translated_text: The fat from the tail region alleviates <s>Kapha</s> and <s>Vāta</s>, bestows radiance and nourishment, but aggravates blood and <s>Pitta</s>; it removes intoxication and poison, and cuts through asthma and cough.
Now, the properties of hare (<s>śaśaka</s>) meat

body.text: (balyaṃ vi) balābhiṣyandi tat syāt jvaraharaṇaparaṃ kṣīṇaretaḥpradhānaṃ

children.text: śastaṃ vātāmayānāṃ śaśakajapiśitaṃ hanti kuṣṭhāmayāṃś ca // 20 //
children.translated_text: hare meat is recommended for <s>Vāta</s> disorders and destroys skin diseases (<s>kuṣṭha</s>). // 20 //

body.translated_text: It is strengthening, non-obstructive, supreme in removing fever, and excellent for seminal debility;
Now, the properties of camel (<s>uṣṭra</s>) and similar meats //

children.translated_text: Camel meat is salty, and the meat of single-hoofed animals —
this group is slightly non-obstructive and is classified as <s>jāṅgala</s> (arid-land). // 21 //
Animals that dwell in watery places and drink water from afar,

children.text: ye mṛgāś ca vihaṅgāś ca mahābhiṣyandanā matāḥ // 22 //
children.translated_text: such deer and birds are considered highly obstructive. // 22 //

body.translated_text: Now, the properties of forest-dwelling animals //

children.translated_text: Due to their sweetness they are heavy, extremely dry and heating; in wasting, in intoxication-born disorders, in poisoning,
they are excellent; they promote urine and feces, are strength-giving, and destroy cough and hemorrhoids;

children.text: vātaṃ pittarujo haranti satataṃ snigdhāś ca kārśyāpahāḥ
children.translated_text: they always remove <s>Vāta</s> and <s>Pitta</s> disorders, are unctuous, and eliminate emaciation;

children.text: sarve te vanacāriṇaḥ kaphaharā mehe hitāḥ sarvadā // 23 //
children.translated_text: all those forest-dwellers alleviate <s>Kapha</s> and are always beneficial in urinary disorders (<s>meha</s>). // 23 //

body.translated_text: Now, the consideration of heaviness and lightness of meats //

children.translated_text: River-dwelling creatures are heavy in the middle portions, since they move with their tails and mouths;

children.text: saras taḍāgajānāṃ tu viśeṣāt sāraso laghuḥ // 24 //
children.translated_text: among those born in lakes and ponds, the crane (<s>sārasa</s>) in particular is light. // 24 //
Since they do not range far, those dwelling in springs and marshy grounds

children.text: kiṃcin muktāḥ śirodeśe atyarthaṃ guravas tu te // 25 //
children.translated_text: are somewhat freed in the head region, but are exceedingly heavy. // 25 //

children.text: adhastād guravo jñeyā matsyāḥ sarasijāḥ smṛtāḥ /
children.translated_text: Fish born in lakes are known to be heavy in the lower parts;

children.text: urovicāraṇās teṣāṃ pūrvam aṅgaṃ laghu smṛtam // 26 //
children.translated_text: of those that move with their chests, the front part of the body is considered light. // 26 //

children.text: śiraḥ skandhaḥ kaṭiḥ pṛṣṭhaṃ sakthinī cāma āśayaḥ /
children.translated_text: The head, shoulders, waist, back, thighs, and the abdominal region —

children.text: guru pūrvaṃ vijānīyād vātas tupathāttaram (laghavas tu yathottaraṃ) // 27 //
children.translated_text: one should know that the earlier parts are heavier, and progressively lighter thereafter. // 27 //

children.text: sarvaś ca prāṇināṃ dehe madhyo gurur udāhṛtaḥ /
children.translated_text: In the body of all living beings, the middle portion is said to be heavy;

children.text: pūrvabhāgo guruḥ puṃsām adhobhāgas tu yoṣitām // 28 //
children.translated_text: in males the front part is heavy, while in females the lower part is. // 28 //
The chest and neck of birds are considered especially heavy;
the middle portion of birds is considered compact and firm. // 29 //

children.text: atīva māṃsaṃ rūkṣaṃ ca vihaṅgānāṃ palāśinām /
children.translated_text: The meat of birds that eat leaves is exceedingly dry,
while the meat of birds that eat flesh is extremely nourishing. // 30 //
Those that eat fish aggravate <s>Pitta</s>; those that feed on grain alleviate <s>Vāta</s>;
<s>Jāṅgala</s> (arid-land), <s>Ānūpa</s> (marshy), domestic, carnivorous, and single-hoofed animals, // 31 //
<s>Prasaha</s> (predators), burrow-dwellers, and those classified by groups,

children.text: pratudā viṣkirāś caiva laghavaḥ syur yathottaram // 32 //
children.translated_text: <s>Pratuda</s> (peckers), <s>Viṣkira</s> (scratchers) — each successive group is progressively lighter. // 32 //

body.translated_text: Now, the properties of boar (<s>vārāha</s>) meat //

children.translated_text: Boar meat always destroys hemorrhoids (<s>durnāma</s>) and <s>Vāta</s> disorders, removes worms,
is unctuous, promotes sweating, is aphrodisiac, cooling, strength-giving, and nourishes heart disease;
it removes cough and asthma, pacifies urinary disorders (<s>prameha</s>), destroys hiccup and <s>Vāta</s>,

children.text: cākṣuṣya tu vidāhi ca bhramaharaṃ vārāhamāṃsaṃ sadā // 33 //
children.translated_text: is beneficial for the eyes, yet is heating, and removes vertigo — boar meat is always [thus]. // 33 //

body.translated_text: Now, the properties of conch, tortoise, and similar creatures //

children.translated_text: Conch (<s>śaṅkha</s>), tortoise (<s>kūrma</s>), and others are sweet in taste and post-digestive effect, and aggravate <s>Vāta</s>;
they are unctuous, cooling, beneficial in <s>Pitta</s>, and increase feces and <s>Kapha</s>. // 34 //
Among them, the black crab (<s>kṛṣṇakarkaṭaka</s>) is strengthening, hot in potency, and alleviates <s>Vāta</s>;
the white one promotes healing of fractures, loosens feces and urine, and destroys <s>Vāta</s> and <s>Pitta</s>. // 35 //

body.translated_text: Now, the properties of fish (<s>matsya</s>) //

children.translated_text: River fish are sweet, heavy, and remove sluggishness and heat;
they aggravate blood and <s>Pitta</s>, are slightly hot, aphrodisiac, unctuous, and produce little feces. // 36 //
Among them, the best is the one that feeds on aquatic moss (<s>śaivāla</s>), with an astringent secondary taste;
<s>Rohita</s> fish removes <s>Vāta</s> and does not excessively aggravate <s>Pitta</s>. // 37 //

body.text:
matsyā dvedhā dudvapannedvambu (?) jātās
tasmāt pūrve pañcadhā kalpanīyāḥ //
body.translated_text: Fish are of two kinds: those born in flowing water and those in still water;

body.text: nadyāḥ kaupāḥ sārasā vaidyutotthās tāḍāgotthāḥ sāgarotthās tathā syuḥ // 38 //
body.translated_text: the former should be classified into five types: river-born, well-born, lake-born, lightning-pool-born, pond-born, and ocean-born. // 38 //
Now, the suitability of specific fish according to season //

children.translated_text: In spring, those born in mountain streams are beneficial;
in the summer season (<s>grīṣma</s>), those from springs are recommended;

children.text: taḍāgajāḥ prāvṛṣi sarva eva snigdhā baliṣṭāś ca sṛjanti doṣān // 39 //
children.translated_text: in the rainy season, all pond-born fish are unctuous, powerful, and expel the <s>doṣas</s>. // 39 //

body.text:
śarady ṛtau nirjari (rjhara ?) jāś ca kūpajā
hitā hi matsyāḥ śiśire 'bdhijātāḥ //
body.translated_text: In autumn, stream-born and well-born fish are beneficial; in the cold season (<s>śiśira</s>), ocean-born fish are recommended.

children.translated_text: (In <s>śiśira</s>, lake fish; in spring, those born in reservoirs;

children.text: grīṣme tu cauṇḍyajā matsyāḥ prāvṛṭkāle taḍāgajāḥ // 40 //
children.translated_text: in summer, spring-born fish; in the rainy season, pond-born fish; // 40 //

body.text:
śaradi nairjharā matsyāḥ hemante kūpasaṃbhavāḥ)
ṣaṭkulo nadikāvarto grahī laghutaraḥ smṛtaḥ (?) /
body.translated_text: in autumn, stream-born fish; in <s>hemanta</s>, well-born fish.) The six-familied river-whirlpool fish is astringent and considered the lightest.
Now, the properties of fish according to habitat //
Those born in lakes and ponds are unctuous and of sweet taste. // 41 //

children.text: kauṣyā vṛṣyā vātahṛcchleṣmalāś ca gulmāṣṭhīlānāhakuṣṭhapradāḥ syuḥ /
children.translated_text: Well-born fish are aphrodisiac, alleviate <s>Vāta</s>, increase <s>Kapha</s>, and may cause tumors (<s>gulma</s>), abdominal lumps (<s>aṣṭhīlā</s>), distension, and skin diseases (<s>kuṣṭha</s>);

children.text: tāḍāgamatsyo gurubṛhaṇīyaḥ tathā ca śīto vṛṣado 'timūtraḥ /
children.translated_text: pond fish are heavy, nourishing, cooling, aphrodisiac, and promote urination;

children.text: tāḍāgavannirjharajāś ca medhyā cattū (?) sthirāyuṣyabalapradāś ca // 43 //
children.translated_text: those born in streams, like pond fish, are intellect-promoting, stabilizing, life-prolonging, and strength-giving. // 43 //

body.text: mama tadaśru (mahāsarassu) balinaḥ svalpāmbhas svabalā matāḥ /

children.text: sāmudro gurur uṣṇarūkṣamadhuraḥ śleṣmalo vātahā syāt (śleṣmāghiko vātahā)
children.translated_text: ocean fish are heavy, hot, dry, and sweet; they increase <s>Kapha</s> and alleviate <s>Vāta</s>,
they promote unctuousness, are strength-giving, and cause flatulence and distension;
they are prescribed in <s>Pitta</s> excess and <s>Kapha</s> disorders, are intellect-promoting, very pleasing to the heart,
yet they cause distension and aggravate cold and <s>Vāta</s> disorders excessively. // 44 //

body.translated_text: Those in great lakes are powerful; those in waters with little depth have proportional strength;

children.translated_text: It pacifies all three <s>doṣas</s>, is pleasing to the heart, destroys <s>Pitta</s>, and removes <s>Vāta</s>;
the ocean <s>Rohita</s> fish is praised as beneficial in all diseases and kindles the digestive fire. // 45 //
Ocean fish are heavy, unctuous, sweet, and do not excessively aggravate <s>Pitta</s>;
they are hot, alleviate <s>Vāta</s>, are aphrodisiac, promote feces, and increase <s>Kapha</s>. // 46 //
Ocean-born fish are especially strength-giving due to their abundant flesh;
river fish are superior to ocean fish in qualities due to their lightness. // 47 //
Furthermore, due to their greater digestive fire-kindling quality, spring-born and well-born fish are superior;
due to unctuousness and sweet post-digestive effect, reservoir fish are of even greater quality. // 48 //

body.translated_text: Now, the properties of <s>Krakara</s> and similar fish //

children.translated_text: <s>Krakara</s> destroys distension, flatulence, and urinary disorders, and alleviates <s>Kapha</s> and <s>Vāta</s>;
it removes fat, <s>Kapha</s>, and <s>Vāta</s>, and cures hiccup, flatulence, and related disorders. // 49 //
is nourishing, pacifies <s>Vāta</s>, alleviates <s>Vāta</s>, kindles the digestive fire, and is light. // 50 //

children.text: matsyānāṃ ca guruḥ śreṣṭho dīpano vātanāśanaḥ /
children.translated_text: The best among heavy fish kindles the digestive fire and destroys <s>Vāta</s>,
promotes taste, generates semen, and destroys urinary stone disorders (<s>āśmarī</s>). // 51 //

body.translated_text: <s>Rohita</s> is the foremost among fish — it destroys <s>Pitta</s> and removes <s>Vāta</s>,
Heavy fish //

children.text: śṛṅgī vātavināśano rucikaro vṛṣyaḥ kaphaghno mataḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Śṛṅgī</s> fish destroys <s>Vāta</s>, promotes taste, is aphrodisiac, and is known to alleviate <s>Kapha</s>;

children.text: kaṇṭāko viśado vṛṣānalakaro vāte kaphe pūjitaḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Kaṇṭāka</s> fish is purifying, aphrodisiac, and kindles the digestive fire, and is valued in <s>Vāta</s> and <s>Kapha</s> disorders;
<s>Pāṭhīna</s> is strengthening, aphrodisiac, generates semen, and constantly increases <s>Kapha</s>;

children.text: tasmād rohitako hito balakaro vātātmakaḥ śleṣmalaḥ // 52 //
children.translated_text: therefore <s>Rohitaka</s> is beneficial, strength-giving, alleviates <s>Vāta</s>, and increases <s>Kapha</s>. // 52 //

body.translated_text: // Thus ends the section on fish //
// Thus ends the section on the classification of meats in the <s>Āyurvedamahodadhi</s> composed by <s>Suṣeṇa</s> //
// Now the properties of the procedures of exercise (<s>vyāyāma</s>), rubbing (<s>udvartana</s>), and oil massage (<s>abhyaṅga</s>) are described //

children.translated_text: With <s>Śrī Nārāyaṇa</s> oil, <s>campaka</s> flower oil, or any other oil,

children.text: kāryaṃ mardanakovidaiḥ kṣitibhujāṃ mallaiḥ sadā mardanam /
children.translated_text: massage should always be performed on kings by skilled masseurs (<s>malla</s>);
with powders of <s>cāturjāta</s> (four spices), <s>lavaṅga</s> (clove), <s>kuṅkuma</s> (saffron), <s>niśā</s> (turmeric), <s>mustā</s>, and <s>sumāṃsī</s>,
combined with roasted <s>masūra</s> (lentil) and <s>mudga</s> (mung bean), one should have dry rubbing (<s>udvartana</s>) performed. // 1 //
