One should massage with oil prepared with <s>Vāta</s>-alleviating herbs;

children.text: na rūkṣamardanaṃ kuryāt tad dhi vātaprakopaṇam // 2 //
children.translated_text: one should not perform dry massage, for that aggravates <s>Vāta</s>. // 2 //
Having obtained comfortable sleep, with senses and mind well-pleased,
with a light stomach and having eaten properly,
fatigued by the burden of exertion, with limbs massaged with oil,
the king should approach the morning massage session. // 3 //
Oil massage (<s>abhyaṅga</s>) removes fatigue and <s>Vāta</s>, gives strength, and brings firmness to the body;
dry rubbing (<s>udvartana</s>) beautifies the limbs and conquers fat, <s>Kapha</s>, and lethargy;
it promotes longevity, gladdens the heart, and removes itching, fatigue, and vomiting,

children.text: snānād eva yathartu sevitam idaṃ śītair aśītair jalaiḥ // 4 //
children.translated_text: followed by bathing with cold or warm water as appropriate to the season. // 4 //

body.translated_text: Now, the properties of exercise (<s>vyāyāma</s>) //

children.text: sāmarthyaṃ sakalakriyāsu laghutām aṅgeṣu dīptiṃ parāṃ
children.translated_text: Capability in all activities, lightness of the limbs, supreme radiance,

children.text: agneḥ pāṭavam indriyeṣu laghutāṃ chedaṃ paraṃ medasaḥ /
children.translated_text: keenness of the digestive fire, lightness in the sense organs, and maximum reduction of fat,

children.text: utsāhaṃ manasaḥ śarīradṛḍhatāṃ śāntiṃ balād vyāpadāṃ
children.translated_text: enthusiasm of the mind, firmness of the body, and the peaceful removal of disorders by force —

children.text: cyāyāmaḥ śiśire vasantasamaye kuryād dhime sevitaḥ // 5 //
children.translated_text: exercise (<s>vyāyāma</s>) produces all these when practiced in the cold season (<s>śiśira</s>) and spring (<s>vasanta</s>) and winter (<s>hima</s>). // 5 //

body.translated_text: Now, those who should avoid exercise //

children.text: vātāmayaḥ pittarujānvitāś ca bālo 'tivṛddho 'pi kṛśo 'tijīrṇaḥ (py arjārṇī) /
children.translated_text: Those afflicted with <s>Vāta</s> diseases, those with <s>Pitta</s> disorders, children, the very old, the emaciated, the over-digested,
those with weak digestive fire, and those who regularly consume unctuous foods — these should abstain from exercise at such times. // 6 //

children.text: sthālyāṃ yathānāvaraṇīkṛtāyāṃ asaṃhitāyāṃ na ca sādhupākaḥ /
children.translated_text: Just as in an uncovered and unstable cooking pot, proper cooking does not occur,

children.text: anāptanidrasya tathā narendrāḥ vyāyāmahīnasya na cānupākaḥ // 7 //
children.translated_text: so too, O kings, for one who has not obtained proper sleep, there is no proper digestion without exercise. // 7 //

body.translated_text: Now, the properties of foot massage (<s>pādamardana</s>) //

children.translated_text: It removes <s>Vāta</s> disorders, pacifies <s>Kapha</s>, brings radiance and clarity,
destroys discoloration of the skin, promotes appetite, and gives firmness to all limbs;
it kindles the digestive fire, generates strength, and removes excessive sweating and fat —

children.text: padbhayāṃ mardanam ādiśanti munayaḥ śreṣṭhaṃ sadā prāṇinām // 8 //
children.translated_text: the sages always prescribe foot massage as the best practice for all living beings. // 8 //

body.translated_text: Now, those who should avoid foot massage //

children.translated_text: For one who is delicate, has weak digestive fire, or has slightly diminished strength,
and also for one with excess <s>Pitta</s>, foot massage should never be performed. // 9 //
For one whose body has been exercised and perspired, and whose feet have been massaged,
diseases do not approach, just as serpents do not approach <s>Vainateya</s> (Garuḍa). // 10 //

children.text: suvarṇavarṇaṃ kurute śarīraṃ dṛḍhatvam aṅge ca dadāti sadyaḥ /
children.translated_text: It renders the body golden in complexion and immediately gives firmness to the limbs;

children.text: sarvakriyālāghavam ātanoti saṃmardanaṃ mallavaraiḥ kṛtaṃ yat // 11 //
children.translated_text: massage performed by expert wrestlers (<s>mallavara</s>) extends lightness in all activities. // 11 //
It conquers <s>Vāta</s> disorders and produces [.........]

children.text: sarvapate mama caiṣa sagras tasyā sa eva samayaḥ kṣudhito padaiva // 12 //
children.translated_text: [text corrupt and largely illegible] // 12 //

children.text: yaḥ kṣaudhyalobhyabhāvena kuryād āha ca bhojanam /
children.translated_text: One who, out of hunger and greed, would eat food [without proper procedure]

children.text: suptavyālāṃ nilāvyādhīn dhyādīn so 'nyathā yaḥ prabodhatet // 13 //
children.translated_text: One who otherwise awakens sleeping serpents, blue jays, those afflicted with illness, and those in meditation, // 13 //

children.text: yaḥ kokavanyamadgākāmi sa naktaṃ bhoktum arhati /
children.translated_text: One who desires cuckoos, forest birds, and black beans — he is fit to eat at night,

children.text: saṃbhoktā vāsareyaś ca rātraur etāś cakoravat (?) // 14 //
children.translated_text: And one who eats during the day should [avoid] these at night, like the <s>cakora</s> (partridge) (?) // 14 //

body.translated_text: Now, the rules of eating //

children.translated_text: The contraction of the lotus of the navel of the heart, and the disappearance of <s>caṇḍa</s> (fierce) digestive fire —

children.text: ato naktaṃ na bhoktavyaṃ vaidyavidyāvidāṃ varaiḥ // 15 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, one should not eat at night, according to the best among those learned in medical science // 15 //

children.text: devārcāṃ bhojanaṃ nidrām ākāśe na prakalpayet /
children.translated_text: One should not perform worship of the gods, eating, or sleeping in the open sky,
Nor in darkness, nor at twilight, nor in a dwelling without a canopy // 16 //
One who is troubled and distressed during eating, tasting, or excretion of waste,
Due to the passing of the evening, for him there arise waves of digestive disturbance (?) //
Food that is discolored, decomposed, soggy, foul-smelling, and tasteless in condition,

children.text: atijīrṇam asātmyaṃ ca nādyād annaṃ ca vāritam // 18 //
children.translated_text: Over-digested and unsuitable — one should not eat such food, nor food that is prohibited // 18 //

body.translated_text: Things to be avoided after eating //

children.translated_text: Shade (?), pigeons, thin gruel, travel, carrying heavy loads, and much water —

children.text: bhojanānantaraṃ sevyaṃ na jātu hitam icchatā // 19 //
children.translated_text: These should never be resorted to immediately after a meal by one who desires well-being // 19 //

body.translated_text: The method of eating //

children.translated_text: One should eat food that is wholesome, measured, well-cooked, pleasing to the eyes, nose, and palate,

children.text: parīkṣitaṃ ca bhuñjīta na drutaṃ na vilambitam // 20 //
children.translated_text: And properly examined — neither too quickly nor too slowly // 20 //
<s>Atyaśana</s> (overeating) and <s>madhyāśana</s> (eating between meals),
<s>Śamana</s> (suppressive eating) and <s>aśata</s> (irregular eating) (<s>samaśana</s> and <s>viṣamāśana</s>) should be abandoned;
One should practice what is called <s>śoktaśamana</s> (proper moderation in eating),
Which gradually preserves strength and life (?) // 21 //

body.translated_text: The order of eating //

children.text: ādau svādu snigdhaṃ tanmadhye lavalamalāpū (lavaṇam amlam u)pabhojyam /
children.translated_text: First, sweet and unctuous food; in the middle, salty and sour food should be eaten;

children.text: rūkṣaṃ dravaṃ ca paścān na ca bhukte bhakṣayet kvacit kiṃcit // 22 //
children.translated_text: Dry and liquid food at the end — and after eating, one should never eat anything further // 22 //

body.translated_text: The four types of digestive fire //

children.translated_text: <s>Mandhu</s> (slow), <s>tikta</s> (sharp) (<s>manda</s> and <s>tīkṣṇa</s>), <s>viṣama</s> (irregular),
And <s>sama</s> (balanced) — the digestive fire (<s>vahni</s>) is of four kinds in people;
Light food for the slow fire, heavy food for the sharp fire,

children.text: tvad yād viṣame samaṃ same 'py adyāt // 23 //
children.translated_text: Appropriate food for the irregular fire, and any food for the balanced fire // 23 //

body.translated_text: Now, a discussion on the frequency of meals //

children.text: jīryaty annaṃ sukhaṃ bhuktam ekavāraṃ yad ṛcchayā /
children.translated_text: The food eaten once with pleasure is digested comfortably according to one's desire;

children.text: dvikālam api bhuñjīta samāgnis tv ardhamātrayā // 24 //
children.translated_text: One may also eat twice a day, but with a balanced fire, only half the quantity // 24 //

children.text: kaṭhinaṃ durjaraṃ yac ca yad vidāhakāṃ bhavet /
children.translated_text: That which is hard, difficult to digest, and that which causes burning sensation —

children.text: tat sarvaṃ niśi varjyaṃ syād dravaṃ laghu ca śīlayet // 25 //
children.translated_text: All such food should be avoided at night; one should habitually take liquid and light food // 25 //

body.translated_text: Now, the examination of food contaminated by poison //

body.text:
dhvāṅkṣaḥ svarān vikurute 'tra pikāṃtyakaś ca (?)
babhruḥ śikhaṇḍitanayaḥ prabhavet prahṛṣṭaḥ /
body.translated_text: The crow distorts its voice there, and the cuckoo and parrot (?); the tawny-crested peacock becomes agitated;
The <s>krauñca</s> (heron) rejoices and the red-crested one cries out,

body.text: chardiṃ śukaḥ pratanute dahate kapiś ca // 26 //
body.translated_text: The parrot begins to vomit, and the monkey experiences burning // 26 //

children.translated_text: The eyes of the <s>cakora</s> (partridge) become red and white upon seeing poison,

children.text: gatiś ca lakṣi (skhalati) haṃsasya līyante cātra makṣikāḥ // 27 //
children.translated_text: The gait of the <s>haṃsa</s> (swan) falters, and flies perish in its presence // 27 //
Just as fire crackles upon contact with salt,
Similarly, contact with poison-contaminated food is clearly perceived // 28 //

body.text: mayā suṣeṇa kṛtaṃ hitāya prāṇaṃ prasādaṃ tanayec ca (?) śīghram //
body.translated_text: This has been composed by me, <s>Suṣeṇa</s>, for the benefit of life, and it quickly bestows grace and progeny (?) //
Thus ends the section on the rules of eating (<s>bhojanavidhivarga</s>) in the <s>Āyurvedamahodadhi</s> composed by <s>Suṣeṇa</s> //
Now the qualities of <s>tāmbūla</s> (betel leaf) are described //

children.translated_text: With <s>karpūra</s> (camphor), <s>kaṅkola</s> (cubeb), <s>lavaṅga</s> (clove), <s>pūga</s> (areca nut), <s>jātī</s> (nutmeg) fruits, and pieces of <s>nāgara</s> (ginger);
Mixed with lime powder, the essence of <s>khadira</s> (catechu), <s>kastūrikā</s> (musk), and <s>candana</s> (sandalwood) powder // 1 //

children.text: tāmbūlam etat pravaraṃ vadanti saubhāgyadaṃ kāntisukhapradaṃ ca /
children.translated_text: This is declared the best <s>tāmbūla</s> (betel preparation), bestowing good fortune, beauty, and pleasure;

children.text: ārogyamedhāsmṛtibuddhivṛddhiṃ karoti vahner api dīpanaṃ ca // 2 //
children.translated_text: It promotes health, intellect, memory, and wisdom, and also kindles the digestive fire // 2 //

body.translated_text: Among substances that kindle the fire of desire (<s>anaṅga</s>), this is declared the foremost;

body.text: ato hi sarvaṃ(rve) sukhino manuṣyā aharniśaṃ prītikaraṃ bhajante // 3 //
body.translated_text: Therefore all happy people partake of this pleasure-giving substance day and night // 3 //

children.text: tāmbūlapatrāṇi haranti vātaṃ pūgīphalaṃ hanti kaphaprasekam /
children.translated_text: <s>Tāmbūla</s> (betel) leaves remove <s>vāta</s> (wind), the <s>pūgī</s> (areca) fruit destroys excessive <s>kapha</s> (phlegm);

children.text: cūrṇaṃ nihanyāt kaphavātam uccair hanyāc ca pittaṃ khadirasya sāraḥ // 4 //
children.translated_text: The powder powerfully destroys <s>kapha</s> and <s>vāta</s>, and the essence of <s>khadira</s> (catechu) destroys <s>pitta</s> (bile) // 4 //

children.text: itthaṃ hi tāmbūlam udāharanti doṣatrayasyāpi nivāraṇāya /
children.translated_text: Thus they declare <s>tāmbūla</s> (betel) to be effective in warding off all three <s>doṣas</s> (humors);

children.text: ato 'tra seveta naraḥ kathañcid vicakṣaṇaḥ prākṛtamānuṣo 'pi // 5 //
children.translated_text: Therefore a wise person should use it in some measure, even one who follows proper conduct // 5 //

body.translated_text: Now, contraindications for <s>tāmbūla</s> (betel) //

children.text: na netraroge na ca raktapitte kṣate ca dīpe na viṣe na śoṣe /
children.translated_text: Not in eye disease, nor in <s>raktapitta</s> (bleeding disorder), nor in wounds, nor in acute conditions, nor in poisoning, nor in emaciation,

children.text: madātyaye nāpi na mohamūrchāśvāseṣu tāmbūlam uśanti vaidyāḥ // 5 //
children.translated_text: Nor in intoxication, nor in delusion, fainting, or <s>śvāsa</s> (dyspnea) — physicians do not recommend <s>tāmbūla</s> (betel) // 5 //

body.translated_text: Now, the rules regarding the time for <s>tāmbūla</s> (betel) //

children.text: bhuktvānnaṃ salilaṃ pītvā bhuktvā ca bahu bhojanam /
children.translated_text: After eating food, after drinking water, and after consuming a large meal,

children.text: pratīkṣya ghaṭikām ekāṃ tāmbūlaṃ bhakṣayen naraḥ // 6 //
children.translated_text: One should wait for one <s>ghaṭikā</s> (24 minutes) and then chew <s>tāmbūla</s> (betel) // 6 //

body.translated_text: Now the qualities of <s>jātīphala</s> (nutmeg) //

children.translated_text: It pacifies <s>vāta</s> (wind) and <s>śleṣma</s> (phlegm), is cardiac tonic, and kindles the digestive fire,
It removes bad taste in the mouth and immediately aids in digesting what has been eaten // 7 //

children.text: jātīphalaṃ pācanam agnidīpanaṃ kaphāpahaṃ kaṇṭharujāpahaṃ ca /
children.translated_text: <s>Jātīphala</s> (nutmeg) is digestive, fire-kindling, <s>kapha</s>-removing, and relieves throat and itching ailments;

children.text: rasekaduḥ (prasekaha) śreṣṭham ajīrṇanāśe ajīrṇanāmu (?) ca pathyam etat // 8 //
children.translated_text: It is the best remedy for excessive salivation, for curing indigestion, and is wholesome in cases of <s>ajīrṇa</s> (indigestion) (?) // 8 //

children.text: kalikā dīpanī rucyā pāke cātitarāṃ himā /
children.translated_text: The bud (<s>kalikā</s>) is appetizing, aids digestion, and is exceedingly cooling in its post-digestive effect;
It destroys <s>vāta</s>, <s>pitta</s>, and <s>kapha</s>, and is effective against fever and vomiting // 9 //

body.translated_text: Now the qualities of <s>elā</s> (cardamom) //

body.text: elādvayaṃ chardiṣu mūtrakṛcchre made ca vai pathyam arocake ca /
body.translated_text: Both varieties of <s>elā</s> (cardamom) are beneficial in vomiting, <s>mūtrakṛcchra</s> (urinary difficulty), intoxication, and <s>arocaka</s> (loss of appetite) //
Now the qualities of <s>jātipatrī</s> (mace) //

body.text: svāduḥ suśītā madhurā ca pāke arocakaṃ hanti ca jātipatrī // 10 //
body.translated_text: Sweet, very cooling, and sweet in post-digestive effect, <s>jātipatrī</s> (mace) destroys <s>arocaka</s> (loss of appetite) // 10 //
Now, the rules regarding the ripening time of <s>kramuka</s> (areca nut) //

children.text: tāmbūlayogyaṃ kramukaṃ tu tajjñā māsatrayād ūrdhvam udāharanti /
children.translated_text: Experts declare that <s>kramuka</s> (areca nut) is suitable for betel use only after three months;

children.text: māse vyatīte tu bhavanti pūrṇāny atīva hṛdyāni manoharāṇi // 11 //
children.translated_text: After a month has passed, they become fully ripe, exceedingly cardiac-tonic and delightful // 11 //

body.translated_text: Now, the specific qualities of the special varieties of <s>kramuka</s> (areca nut) and <s>tāmbūla</s> (betel) //

children.translated_text: The large <s>kramuka-tāmbūla</s> (areca-betel) increases <s>śleṣma</s> (phlegm) and promotes worms;
The one at the end, white in color, increases <s>śleṣma</s> (phlegm) but destroys worms // 12 //

body.translated_text: Now the qualities of <s>karpūra</s> (camphor) //

children.translated_text: <s>Karpūra</s> (camphor) is pungent and hot, very cooling in post-digestive effect, and removes <s>kaṇḍu</s> (itching) and <s>prameha</s> (urinary diseases);
It removes nasal discharge and excess fluid, destroys worms, and conquers <s>tṛṭ</s> (thirst), <s>śvāsa</s> (dyspnea), and <s>kāsa</s> (cough);
It destroys <s>śleṣma</s> (phlegm), removes throat ailments, and conquers numbness of the tip of the tongue;
<s>Karpūra</s> (camphor) is indeed endowed with brilliant fragrance, destroys <s>pitta</s> diseases, and is crystal-like //
In throat ailments, numbness of the tongue, excessive nasal discharge and fluid,
<s>Karpūra</s> (camphor) destroys <s>śleṣma</s> (phlegm), <s>meha</s> (urinary disease), and worms, and is also beneficial for the eyes //

body.translated_text: It destroys <s>prameha</s> (urinary diseases), thirst, and burning sensation, and enhances beauty and good fortune // 16 //
Now the qualities of <s>kastūrī</s> (musk) //

children.translated_text: <s>Kastūrī</s> (musk) is supremely fragrant, possessing pungent taste, alkaline, bitter, and astringent;
It removes grief and mental anguish, eliminates <s>kapha</s> (phlegm) and <s>pavana</s> (wind), and is beneficial for <s>pitta</s> ailments and the eyes;
It causes delight to the mind, [destroys] irregular fevers and poisons, and removes bodily malodor;

children.text: kṣuttṛṣṇāpittakopaṃ praśamayati bhṛśaṃ klaibyaśoṣaṃ viṣaṃ ca // 17 //
children.translated_text: It greatly pacifies hunger, thirst, and aggravation of <s>pitta</s> (bile), and [cures] impotence, emaciation, and poisoning // 17 //

body.translated_text: Now, the section on unguents (<s>anulepanavarga</s>) //

children.translated_text: <s>Candana</s> (sandalwood) destroys <s>raktapitta</s> (bleeding disorders), and removes burning sensation, fainting, and diarrhea;
It is cooling, <s>śleṣma</s>-producing (phlegm-producing), cardiac tonic, and slightly aggravates <s>vāta</s> (wind) // 18 //
It always removes <s>pitta</s> and blood disorders, and is cooling like a forest (?);
It pacifies fainting, delusion, thirst, and poison, and destroys foul odor;
It cures itching, leprosy, and fistula, and clearly cuts through fainting;

children.text: mehaṃ kṛcchram api vyapohati sadā durnāmanirṇāśanam // 19 //
children.translated_text: It always dispels <s>meha</s> (urinary disease) and <s>kṛcchra</s> (dysuria), and destroys foul names (skin diseases) // 19 //

body.translated_text: It always dispels diseases of many kinds, and is the abode of fragrance (?) //

children.translated_text: <s>Malayādri</s> (Malaya mountain) sandalwood destroys delusion and removes <s>raktapitta</s> (bleeding disorders);
It pacifies fainting and emaciation, and destroys foul breath // 20 //

body.text:
śītaṃ pittavināśanaṃ samadhuraṃ kiṃcit satiktaṃ tathā
kaṇḍūśophaviṣāpahaṃ krimiharaṃ saubhāgyakāntipradam /
saugandhyaṃ kurute kim apy abhinavaṃ gātreṣu puṣṭipradaṃ
saṃtoṣaṃ vidadhāti cetasi paraṃ snigdhaṃ ca tṛṣṇāharam /

children.translated_text: <s>Candana</s> (sandalwood) or <s>kuṅkuma</s> (saffron) should be applied according to the seasons;
An unguent of deer-musk and <s>dhana</s> (coriander) should be used always;
With abundant flower garlands of love, <s>karpūra</s> (camphor) powder,
Pure white garments — suitable for use at all times // 22 //

body.translated_text: It is cooling, destroys <s>pitta</s> (bile), somewhat sweet and slightly bitter; it removes itching, swelling, and poison, destroys worms, bestows beauty and radiance; it produces a certain novel fragrance in the body, grants nourishment, gives supreme contentment to the mind, and is unctuous and thirst-removing;
// Thus ends the section on unguents (<s>anulepanavarga</s>) in the <s>Āyurvedamahodadhi</s> composed by <s>Suṣeṇa</s> //
Now the qualities of garments are described //

children.translated_text: White <s>dukūla</s> (fine silk) that is clean promotes the proper flow of <s>kapha</s> (phlegm) and <s>vāta</s> (wind);

children.text: yad vā sūtram ayaṃ vastraṃ tridoṣaśamanaṃ viduḥ // 1 //
children.translated_text: Or cotton cloth — this garment is known to pacify all three <s>doṣas</s> (humors) // 1 //
Very white <s>dukūla</s> (fine silk) bestows pacification of <s>pitta</s> (bile) caused by strength,
Increases <s>ojas</s> (vital essence) and brilliance, produces pleasure, and cuts through excessive burning at vital points;
It breaks down the fault of thirst, produces steadiness, bestows radiance, and is <s>śleṣma</s>-producing (phlegm-producing);

children.text: kṣaumaṃ śuklam atīva hṛdyam amalaṃ pittāmayadhvaṃsakam // 2 //
children.translated_text: <s>Kṣauma</s> (linen), when white, is exceedingly cardiac-tonic, pure, and destroys <s>pitta</s> diseases // 2 //

children.text: māñjiṣṭhaṃ ca vidāhi tat kaphaharaṃ pathyaṃ ca vātāmaya-
children.translated_text: That which is dyed with <s>māñjiṣṭha</s> (madder) is heating, removes <s>kapha</s>, is wholesome, and destroys <s>vāta</s> diseases;
It always produces great beauty and conquers aggravation of <s>śleṣma</s> (phlegm);
It is hot, destroys cold, removes impurities, and eliminates <s>śleṣma</s> (phlegm) and <s>vāta</s>;
The <s>māñjiṣṭha</s> (madder-dyed) cloth always removes diseases [...] (?) // 3 //

body.translated_text: // Thus ends the section on garments (<s>vastravarga</s>) in the <s>Āyurvedamahodadhi</s> composed by <s>Suṣeṇa</s> //
// Thus is completed the treatise composed by <s>Suṣeṇa</s> //
// May this be an offering to <s>Śrī Sāmbasadāśiva</s> //
// May there be auspiciousness //
// Salutations to <s>Śrī Sarasvatī</s> //
